findings.title: The gateway now enforces the PQ rule in production, but no model has passed PQ, so production AI drafting is refused
findings.evidenceAtHead: ENFORCEMENT (closed): server/services/ai-gateway/model-governance.ts:78-86 selectionRefusal returns 'pq-not-passed' for production document_drafting; gateway.ts:3292-3295 (explicit path) and :3312-3316 (strategy path) throw governanceError -> NO_PQ_QUALIFIED_MODEL (model-governance.ts:54-55, gateway.ts:4471). approved-models.ts:382-386 isQualifiedForHighRiskDrafting = approvedForHighRisk && (!production || pq.status==='passed'); AnA governed writes are gated by the same rule at server/services/ana/AnaToolExecutor.ts:507 (isServedModelApprovedForHighRisk). There is no env bypass: isProductionEnv is NODE_ENV only (pii-screen.ts:57-59). Command run at HEAD: tsx script calling selectionRefusal(claude-opus-4 / claude-opus-5-5) printed 'prod drafting pq-not-passed', 'dev drafting null', 'prod review null', 'passed entries: 0 of 16'. STILL OPEN: all 16 APPROVED_MODELS entries have pq {status:'pending', reference:null} (approved-models.ts:89,101,...,274). server/eval/pq/pq-protocol.json:6-8 status 'draft', approvedBy null, approvedOn null, so pq-verdict cannot produce PASS. run-pq.ts:26-29 says it measures the harness's own generation prompt and does not re-qualify production drafting prompts. Every deployment path runs NODE_ENV=production (terraform/modules/ecs-fargate/main.tf:153,296; docker-compose.yml:87; docker-compose.beta.yml:82), so document_drafting callers are refused there. These include server/routes/c2c/ai-editing.ts, server/services/authoring/section-generation-service.ts, ib-builder.ts, server/mcp/tools/drafting.ts and 23 other files (grep: 38 call sites). Stale comments at server/services/ai-gateway/effort.ts:156 and :207 still say the PQ clause is 'enforced nowhere yet'.
findings.fixedBy: e2258d07a (2026-09-29): server/services/ai-gateway/model-governance.ts:78-86, 157-189; server/services/ai-governance/approved-models.ts:382-386, 413-419; wired at server/services/ai-gateway/gateway.ts:3292-3316; AnA governed-write gate server/services/ana/AnaToolExecutor.ts:507
findings.remaining: (1) No model has a passed PQ. The protocol PQ-DRAFT-001 is still a draft with no approver, so no run can pass. (2) As a result, every NODE_ENV=production environment (AWS ECS staging and production, docker-compose, beta) refuses all document_drafting requests (Authoring editor AI actions, section generation, IB/CSR builders, MCP drafting tool) and all AnA governed content writes with 'No performance-qualified model is available for high-risk regulatory drafting in this environment.' (3) PQ scores the harness prompt, not the production drafting prompts, so a pass would not cover the prompts users actually run. (4) Callers that draft governed text under task labels other than document_drafting are not covered by the gateway rule. Only the AnA governed-write gate catches them, and model-governance.ts:25-30 lists them as known gaps. (5) /readyz does not reflect PQ: it reports ready while drafting is refused (tracked under AI-02). (6) The comments at effort.ts:156 and :207 are stale.
findings.severityRationale: The safety half is fixed: production now fails closed instead of drafting on an unqualified model. The core Authoring AI-drafting journey still cannot work at all in the pilot's production environment until the founder approves the protocol and a PASS is recorded. CLAUDE.md Rule 2 and launch DoD row for PQ remain unmet.
findings.humanTestingNote: On any NODE_ENV=production deployment (docker compose, beta compose, AWS staging), these are refused with 'No performance-qualified model is available for high-risk regulatory drafting in this environment.': AI drafting in the Authoring editor (generate, expand, rewrite section), section/IB/CSR generation, and AnA 'draft and save to Vault/editor'. Chat and review-style AnA turns still answer. Workaround for testers: exercise AI drafting on an `npm run dev` instance (NODE_ENV=development) with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set. A PQ-pending approved model then serves, and the ledger records pq_status 'pending'. Do not add a production bypass.
findings.instructions:
1. Founder/system owner: review server/eval/pq/pq-protocol.json (PQ-DRAFT-001). In a reviewed commit on concept2cure-v2, set "status":"approved", "approvedBy" and "approvedOn". Confirm first that the doc-quality gold bank meets components.generation.criteria.minTasksPerDocType (AI-07).
2. Engineering, on a controlled machine with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (BAA in place): run `npm run pq:run -- --model claude-opus-4` (pinned claude-opus-5-5). Only if the verdict is PASS, rerun with `--record`. The record lands at docs/evidence/PQ/<date>/claude-opus-4.json.
3. Failing-first: in server/services/ai-governance/approved-models.ts:89, temporarily set the claude-opus-4 entry to pq {status:'passed', reference:'docs/evidence/PQ/does-not-exist.json'}. Run `npx vitest run server/services/ai-gateway/__tests__/high-risk-model-approval.test.ts` and confirm verifyPqClaim fails. Then set reference to the real record path from step 2 and confirm it passes. Commit only the real reference.
4. Extend server/eval/pq/run-pq.ts so the generation phase also runs the production drafting prompts: the prompt-registry versions used by server/routes/c2c/ai-editing.ts and server/services/authoring/section-generation-service.ts. Write each prompt id and version into the PqRecord. In server/eval/pq/pq-verdict.ts verifyPqClaim, refuse a 'passed' claim whose recorded prompt versions differ from the current ones, so a prompt change invalidates the pass. Prove it by bumping one prompt version in a scratch change and watching high-risk-model-approval.test.ts fail.
5. Inventory governed-text authors that call the gateway with a taskType other than 'document_drafting' (start from the known-gaps list in model-governance.ts:25-30 and `grep -rn "callerModule" server/services/cmc server/services/authoring`). Relabel each to taskType 'document_drafting', or route its persistence through the AnaToolExecutor.ts:507 gate.
6. Correct the stale comments at server/services/ai-gateway/effort.ts:156 and :207 to point at model-governance.ts selectionRefusal.
7. Do not add any environment variable or request field that skips 'pq-not-passed' in production. model-governance.ts:20-23 forbids it.
8. Land readiness reflecting PQ (AI-02 step 1) in the same push.
findings.acceptance: a) Failing-first: on HEAD, selectionRefusal({id:'claude-opus-4',provider:'anthropic',model:'claude-opus-5-5'}, {taskType:'document_drafting'}, selectionGovernance(APPROVED_MODELS,{NODE_ENV:'production'})) returns 'pq-not-passed'. After step 3 it returns null, while every other entry still returns 'pq-not-passed'. b) high-risk-model-approval.test.ts fails for a 'passed' entry with a missing or mismatched record, and passes with the real one. c) pq-protocol.json has status 'approved' and a named approver and date. d) With NODE_ENV=production and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, an Authoring AI action through server/routes/c2c/ai-editing.ts returns a draft. Its ai ledger row (audit.ts) records model claude-opus-5-5 and pq_status 'passed'. The same request against a registry where the entry is 'pending' returns NO_PQ_QUALIFIED_MODEL. e) Changing a production drafting prompt version without a new PQ record makes high-risk-model-approval.test.ts fail.
findings.dependencies: Founder approval of PQ-DRAFT-001; Anthropic API key and BAA (D6); AI-07 gold bank size; AI-02 readiness change

findings.title: Production now gets an Anthropic drafting key, but /readyz and the deploy smoke ignore PQ, and Bedrock/Vertex are still undeployable
findings.evidenceAtHead: CLOSED: terraform/stack/main.tf:125-128 creates the anthropic_api_key secret and :326 passes ANTHROPIC_API_KEY to the container. variables.tf:351-358 validates the sk-ant- prefix. main.tf:190-194 requires the placement approvals to name 'anthropic'. terraform/environments/production/main.tf:92 and staging/main.tf:95 pass it. .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml:517 and :541 refuse a deploy without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. server/startup/ana-readiness-state.ts:227-300 (recordHighRiskCoverage) sets 'no_high_risk_model' when no enabled model isApprovedForHighRisk, and inline-endpoints.ts:82-83 turns that into deps.ana 'down'. STILL OPEN: readiness uses isApprovedForHighRisk only (ana-readiness-state.ts:243-251). `grep -rln 'isQualifiedForHighRiskDrafting|pq-not-passed|NO_PQ_QUALIFIED_MODEL' server` finds no startup or readiness file. So in production, with every entry PQ 'pending', /readyz reports ana 'ok' and ready:true while the gateway refuses every document_drafting request (model-governance.ts:84-85). The deploy smoke (deploy-aws.yml:1059-1061) only checks .ready==true and so goes green with drafting dead. That repeats the 'second incident' that ana-readiness-state.ts:84-95 documents. package.json:452 has only @anthropic-ai/sdk (no bedrock-sdk or vertex-sdk). server/services/ai-gateway/providers/cloud-models.ts:49-87 still pins Bedrock/Vertex Opus to claude-opus-4-7 with contextWindow 200000 and 0.015/0.075 pricing, while approved-models.ts:217-248 keeps them approvedForHighRisk:true. `grep -rn inference_geo server` returns nothing.
findings.fixedBy: c3e9e4930 (2026-10-01): terraform/stack/main.tf:125-128,190-194,326; terraform/stack/variables.tf:351-358; .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml:517,541. 25294ca56 (2026-09-25, merged after the audit): server/startup/ana-readiness-state.ts:227-300 'no_high_risk_model' readiness state
findings.remaining: (1) /readyz and the startup invariant (server/lib/startup-invariants.ts:116-127) ask 'approved for high-risk', not 'may serve drafting in this environment'. In production they report ready while every draft is refused for lack of a PQ pass, and the deploy smoke goes green. (2) The deploy preflight does not check that at least one high-risk-approved, PQ-passed model exists. (3) Bedrock and Vertex cannot be deployed: no SDK dependency, stale Opus 4.7 pins, 200K context, old pricing, yet they stay approvedForHighRisk. (4) The first-party Anthropic API is used with no data-residency parameter.
findings.severityRationale: The pilot-blocking part (no drafting-capable provider in the documented deploy) is fixed. What remains makes health checks misreport a dead drafting journey as ready, so operators and the deploy gate cannot see it. That must be fixed before pilot users rely on production. Bedrock/Vertex and residency are P2 for an FDA-only US pilot on first-party Anthropic.
findings.humanTestingNote: On a NODE_ENV=production staging deployment, /readyz and the boot banner say AnA is ready, but Authoring AI drafting is refused (see AI-01). Testers should not take the readiness page as proof that drafting works. Check the drafting journey directly, or test it on an `npm run dev` instance.
findings.instructions:
1. In server/startup/ana-readiness-state.ts recordHighRiskCoverage (:227-300), replace the local predicate `serves` (:250-251) for each task in HIGH_RISK_TASK_TYPES. The new check: `m.capabilities.includes(task) && selectionRefusal(m, { taskType: task }, selectionGovernance()) === null`, importing both from server/services/ai-gateway/model-governance.ts. Readiness and routing then share one rule, and that rule includes PQ in production.
2. Add a readiness state 'no_pq_qualified_model'. Its detail embeds NO_PQ_QUALIFIED_MODEL and lists each approved model with its pq status. Treat it as not serving in isAnaReadinessServing, as 'no_high_risk_model' is treated (the doctrine at ana-readiness-state.ts:84-95: a process that refuses every draft must not report ready). Note: once this lands, every NODE_ENV=production environment reports ready:false and the deploy-aws.yml smoke (:1059-1071) fails until AI-01 records a PQ pass. That is the true state. Sequence this with AI-01 and tell the founder before pushing, because it turns the staging deploy red.
3. Failing-first: add a case to the existing readiness tests (server/startup/__tests__ or wherever ana-readiness-state is tested). Use NODE_ENV=production and a gateway stub exposing claude-opus-4 enabled, with the real APPROVED_MODELS (all 'pending'). Assert 'no_pq_qualified_model'. Run it at HEAD and see it fail (HEAD returns 'ready'), then implement.
4. In .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml, next to the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY preflight (:517-541), add a step: `npx tsx -e "import {APPROVED_MODELS,isQualifiedForHighRiskDrafting} from './server/services/ai-governance/approved-models.ts'; if(!APPROVED_MODELS.some(m=>m.provider==='anthropic'&&isQualifiedForHighRiskDrafting(m,true))){console.error('no PQ-passed Anthropic drafting model');process.exit(1)}"`. Show it fail at HEAD in a dry run before relying on it.
5. Bedrock/Vertex (P2): until @anthropic-ai/bedrock-sdk or vertex-sdk is a dependency and an IAM or inference-profile path exists in terraform/stack, set approvedForHighRisk:false on claude-opus-4-bedrock and claude-opus-4-vertex in approved-models.ts:217-248 (record the reason in highRiskBasis and lastReviewed). When they are adopted, bump the cloud-models.ts:49-87 pins, prices and contextWindow to the current Opus pin, and update the matching approved-models entries so the drift gate passes.
6. Residency (P2): confirm in the current Anthropic API documentation whether a data-residency/inference-geography request parameter exists. If it does, send it from the Anthropic provider when the tenant placement policy requires US-only processing, and record it in the ledger row.
findings.acceptance: a) New readiness test: with NODE_ENV=production and only PQ-pending approved models enabled, evaluateAnaReadiness() returns 'no_pq_qualified_model' and /readyz returns ready:false with deps.ana 'down'. The test fails on HEAD. b) With NODE_ENV=development, or a PQ-passed entry, the same setup returns 'ready'. c) The deploy preflight step exits 1 on HEAD's registry and 0 once an Anthropic entry is PQ-passed. d) The drift test (approved-models drift gate) still passes after the Bedrock/Vertex change.
findings.dependencies: AI-01 (a PQ pass is what turns readiness back to ready); founder awareness that staging goes not-ready until then

findings.title: AnA run_python_script now runs only in the hardened container and refuses when that is not enabled
findings.evidenceAtHead: workers/artifact-compute/python-script-runtime.py was deleted in 930fe7b4c (`git ls-tree` shows it at 92ccdba1, absent at HEAD). No remaining Python runtime calls exec/eval/compile (`grep -n 'exec\|eval\|compile(' workers/artifact-compute/*.py` finds nothing). server/services/compute/scriptWorker.ts:10-15 now runs only the fixed docx-insert runtime. The handler server/services/ana/AnaToolExecutor.ts:7711-7771 returns {available:false} unless getContainerExecConfig().enabled (ANA_ENABLE_CONTAINER_EXEC==='true'). It runs the code only via containerExec.runInContainer with script 'exec python3 /work/__script.py'. server/services/compute/containerExec.ts:75-86 builds `--network none` (unless ANA_CONTAINER_ALLOW_NETWORK==='true'), `--cap-drop ALL`, `--security-opt no-new-privileges`, `--read-only` and `--user`. Outputs are persisted to a per-organization scratch dir (AnaToolExecutor.ts:7689-7709). No deploy config enables container exec or mounts docker.sock (grep of docker-compose*.yml, Dockerfile.optimized, terraform: none), so on ECS the tool fails closed. Command run: `npx vitest run server/services/ana/__tests__/run-python-script-container.test.ts` gave 3/3 passed, including 'does not run anywhere when container execution is not enabled'. Non-blocking note: stale comments still describe the deleted host runtime at server/services/ana/legacy-import-tool-defs.ts:178-189 and server/services/compute/sandboxEnv.ts:6.
findings.fixedBy: 930fe7b4c (2026-09-29): server/services/ana/AnaToolExecutor.ts:7711-7771; server/services/compute/scriptWorker.ts:10-15; server/services/compute/containerExec.ts:75-86; deleted workers/artifact-compute/python-script-runtime.py
findings.severityRationale: Model-written code no longer executes on the application host. The container path has no network by default, all capabilities dropped and a read-only root, and it is disabled in every deploy configuration.
findings.humanTestingNote: Expected behaviour, not a defect: on deployments without ANA_ENABLE_CONTAINER_EXEC=true and Docker (all staging and production configs), AnA reports that run_python_script is not available, runs nothing, and suggests the structured tools instead.
findings.instructions: n/a
findings.acceptance: n/a

findings.instructions:
1. Submission Twin readiness. In server/services/submission-twin-service.ts:897, replace `readinessSnap?.readinessPercent ?? 50` with an explicit no-snapshot branch. It returns readinessScore null, fragilityScore computed as now, and reason 'no_readiness_snapshot'. Type readinessScore as `number | null` in the return type (~:775-780). In client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/SubmissionTwin.tsx (interface at :33, memo text at :175-195), render an honest empty state ('No readiness snapshot for this package; run Submission Readiness first') when the score is null. Failing-first: add a server unit test (no c2cReadinessSnapshots row, readinessScore must be null) and a case in client/src/concept2cure/v2/__tests__/submissionTwin.test.tsx. Run both at HEAD and see them fail (HEAD returns 50).
2. Submission Twin claim figures. Remove 'Assign a confidence score (0-1)' from the prompt at submission-twin-service.ts:1159, and relevanceScore from :1193. Compute support deterministically: an assessment is 'direct' only if its evidenceText occurs verbatim in the retrieved document context (reuse the span check in server/services/clinical-regulatory-evidence/lineage-gate.ts); otherwise 'unsupported'. Order claims by section and position instead of confidence at :280. Keep the existing column, write null, and do not drop it (Rule 1).
3. Sentence traceability. In server/services/sentenceTraceabilityService.ts:579-580, ignore mapping.needsReview. Set needsReview = claimType in {statistical, safety, efficacy} OR no source whose excerpt occurs verbatim in that source's text. Set isSupported only when such a verbatim excerpt exists with linkType 'supports'. Remove the needsReview instruction at :499-501. Failing-first: a unit test where the model mock returns needsReview:false for a statistical sentence with no verbatim excerpt must yield needsReview:true. It fails at HEAD.
4. Drafting routes (server/api/drafting/routes.ts; mount at server/api/gcc/index.ts:31). No client caller, and the tables are not in C2C_MIGRATION_FILES. Unmount the router and delete the file. The commit message must name the canonical replacement: Authoring AI drafting via server/routes/c2c/ai-editing.ts and AnA drafting via server/services/ana/AnaDocumentDraftingService.ts. Run the CLAUDE.md working-agreement history search and quote its result. If unmount is refused, at minimum: drop citations whose sourceId matches no retrieved chunk, take page only from matchingChunk.page_number (:432), and remove the 0.5 and 0.8 confidence defaults (:244, :592).
5. ana-cortex (server/routes/ana-cortex.ts:33-50; mount at bootstrap/register-inline-routes.ts:137-139; no client caller). findings.humanTestingNote: In Authoring, open a section and choose 'Draft from sources'. findings.instructions:

2. Implement the block. In server/routes/authoring.router.ts, in the accept handler at line 4142, after consumeDraftCandidate (inside the transaction), build EvidenceEntry[] from the candidate's parked sources ({source:'context', content}). Run checkAnswer(generatedDraft, entries) from server/services/ana/answer-grounding.ts. For each figure in check.notFound (and, when the draft had no sources, each figure in check.unchecked), find its sentence in the generated draft (reuse splitSentences, or the sentence splitter in answer-check-sources.ts). If that sentence still appears verbatim in acceptedContent, ROLLBACK and return 409 {code:'UNSUPPORTED_FIGURES', figures:[...]}. Sentences the author edited are the author's own words and are not blocked. Record the figure list and the check engine version (ANSWER_CHECK_VERSION) on the existing accept audit entry, whatever the outcome.
3. Client. In client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/AuthoringAiDraft.tsx, render the 409 as a calm, factual refusal that names the figures, and keep the draft in the buffer so the author can edit it. When it is 'failed', return 503 {code:'RETRIEVAL_FAILED'}. In both cases file the turn with fileFailedDraftTurn. Write the tests red first: mock retrieval to return zero hits or to throw, and assert that gw.route is not called.

Extend checkAnswer, or add a wrapper in turn-record-draft.ts, so that a figure in a sentence the model attributed (the modelAttributions quote and src from parseDraftEnvelope) must be found in that src's chunk, not just in any shown chunk. Add a unit test in which the figure exists only in SRC-2 but is attributed to SRC-1, and assert notFound.
6. Legacy route. ai-editing.ts /ai/edit-section (line 122) and /ai/templates/:templateId/generate (line 1048) have no client caller. findings.instructions:
Work on concept2cure-v2 only (Rule 0).
1. Founder. Decide reuse terms for each publisher in server/eval/rag/guidance-corpus-manifest.json (publishers.<publisher>.terms, termsUrl, termsVerified), at least ICH and EMA. FDA guidance and govinfo eCFR are public domain. Provide a machine whose egress can reach database.ich.org, www.fda.gov, www.govinfo.gov, eur-lex.europa.eu and www.ema.europa.eu; this container's proxy refused them on 2026-09-28.
2. Engineer, on that machine. Follow the manifest's verifyProcedure steps 1-6 for all 24 entries: record sourceUrl, sha256 of the downloaded bytes, retrievedAt, byte size and date, and set versionVerified and verified to true. Re-pin US-CFR to the latest govinfo annual edition. Change any re-pinned key in server/eval/rag/gold-dataset.json in the same commit. Store the files outside git if the terms forbid redistribution, and record the path.
3. Evaluation corpus. Create one dedicated evaluation organisation and programme. Ingest each verified file through the manifest's admission path (server/routes/vault-ingest.ts -> ingestVaultDocument -> vault.document_chunks). Run node scripts/verify-rag-corpus.mjs --org-uuid <eval-org-uuid>, which must exit 0 and report 24 documents. Check that every vault.documents.content_hash equals the manifest sha256.
4. Pilot-tenant corpus (product). Write scripts/corpus/seed-regulatory-corpus.mjs. It takes --org-uuid and --program-id, reads the manifest, refuses any entry with verified:false or a sha256 mismatch, and ingests through the same ingestVaultDocument path, idempotent on (programme, document_code, version). Tenant data stays organisation-scoped under the existing RLS, and no shared cross-tenant table is added. If a later design does need a table, put it in public with organization_id INTEGER NOT NULL, list it in C2C_MIGRATION_FILES before the final RLS sweep pair, and run npm run ci:migration-set-order and ci:migration-drop-safety (Rule 1).
5. Currency. Add server/jobs/regulatoryCorpusStalenessSweep.ts. It re-fetches each verified entry's sourceUrl HEAD and listing page on a schedule, compares the date and sha256, and marks an entry stale when either changed or when the check could not run (fail closed). AnA's guidance tools must then say 'stale' or 'unverified' for that document. Register the job next to corpusIngestionSweep, and give it a unit test that is red first, with a mocked changed hash.
6. Search. Change fetchFdaGuidanceList in server/services/regulatory-currency/guidance-ingestion-service.ts to search the org's ingested corpus and return document_code, version and effective date. Keep {status:'unavailable', reason:'no_guidance_index'} when the org has no corpus. Add a test for both branches.
7. Verify by failing first. Before ingesting, show verify-rag-corpus exiting non-zero for the eval org, and show a run-eval item with a tampered sha256 reported as INCOMPLETE.
findings.acceptance: (a) Every answer-source entry in guidance-corpus-manifest.json has verified:true, a sha256, sourceUrl and date, and gold-dataset.json keysProvisional is false. (c) run-eval resolves keys for every positive gold item, so the hit-rate scores more than 0 items, and a tampered content_hash makes the run INCOMPLETE. (d) For a seeded pilot org, AnA's FDA guidance tool returns a document with a version and an effective date. For an unseeded org it still returns 'unavailable'. (e) The staleness sweep test flips an entry to stale on a changed hash, and the test was red before the job existed.

findings.title: PHI/PII screen is still text-regex only: clinical narratives classify as non-sensitive, and image/PDF/document blocks are labelled 'unscreened_media' in the ledger but still dispatched
findings.evidenceAtHead: No commits since 92ccdba1 touch server/services/ai-governance/classification/ or server/services/ai-gateway/pii-screen.ts or sensitive-placement-policy.ts (git log 92ccdba1..HEAD on those paths: empty). (1) heuristic-classifier.ts:33-48 has the same 7 detectors (ssn, email, credit_card, phone, labelled MRN, labelled DOB, labelled plan id); nothing for names, subject IDs or AE narratives. Command run: npx tsx scratch script classifying 'Subject 1001-023, Maria Gonzalez, a 54-year-old female, experienced a serious adverse event of hepatic failure on Day 14 and was hospitalized ... She died on 12 March 2026.' -> {"phi":false,"pii":false,"classes":["public"]}; positive control 'Contact jane@example.com' -> pii:true. (2) classification/index.ts:23 defaults AI_CLASSIFIER_MODE to heuristic; slm-classifier.ts:36-56 still falls back to the heuristic even when AI_CLASSIFIER_SLM_URL is set (stub). (3) pii-screen.ts:97-114 extractRequestText still reads only string content and type:'text' blocks ('Non-text blocks ... are not inspected'). (4) gateway.ts:1398-1413 maps that result to sensitiveDataClass 'none'; sensitive-placement-policy.ts:51 returns ALLOW_NON_SENSITIVE for 'none' before any zero-retention or approval check. (5) gateway.ts:4829-4843 ledgerDataClass (new since audit) only RECORDS 'unscreened_media' in the ledger; nothing refuses. (6) Media still reaches providers unscreened: routes/ana-ri/stream.ts:1628-1675 (ANA_ENABLE_PDF_INTAKE=true; sends PDF and also text/plain files as base64 document blocks, so even plain-text uploads skip the screen) and AnaDocumentDraftingService.ts:900-935 analyzeImage (image block). Mitigations that landed since audit, not closing the finding: org-placement.ts (d29275b1b) limits production vendors to anthropic/bedrock/local unless elected; gateway.ts:4693-4705 requestPlacementDenial enforces an org-level zeroDataRetention election for every data class.
findings.remaining: Entire finding: no detector for patient names, subject/randomisation IDs, age+sex+event narratives or dates of death/hospitalisation; no PHI-possible floor for clinical-document payloads; image, PDF and base64 document blocks are not inspected and not refused when the placement is not approved for PHI; the SLM classifier is an unimplemented seam. Only the ledger label is honest now ('unscreened_media').
findings.severityRationale: A design-partner biotech will upload protocols, CSRs and SAE narratives through AnA and Authoring. Today those are classed 'none' and dispatched with no zero-retention or approval check. The production vendor default (Anthropic/Bedrock/local) and the per-org ZDR election reduce the exposure, so the pilot can start. The screen still has to be fixed, or the pilot org configured with zero_data_retention and the limitation written into the DPA, before pilot users rely on it for clinical content.
findings.humanTestingNote: Not visible to testers. Classification is silent, and non-production defaults to audit mode, which never blocks. Testers must not upload real patient-identifying data on local or staging. If the fix below lands and staging runs AI_SENSITIVE_DATA_POLICY_MODE=enforce, AnA PDF/image requests will be refused until AI_PROVIDER_PLACEMENT_APPROVALS grants the provider PHI/zero-retention approval. That refusal is expected.
findings.instructions:
1. Failing-first tests. (a) Add server/services/ai-governance/classification/__tests__/clinical-narrative.test.ts asserting that HeuristicContentClassifier.classify() returns phi:true for: 'Subject 1001-023 ... 54-year-old female ... serious adverse event ... hospitalized ... died on 12 March 2026'; 'Patient 0042 (initials J.D.)'; 'randomization number R-10234'. Keep negative controls ('Study 1001 enrolled 240 subjects', plain ICH prose) at phi:false. Run it and confirm it FAILS at HEAD. (b) Add a gateway test, next to server/services/ai-gateway/__tests__/governance-review.test.ts and using its governedGateway()/stubDispatch helpers, with NODE_ENV=production and AI_SENSITIVE_DATA_POLICY_MODE=enforce: a request whose only content is an image block, or a base64 application/pdf document block, sent to a provider whose AI_PROVIDER_PLACEMENT_APPROVALS entry lacks zeroRetentionApproved must reject with GatewayPolicyError and dispatch nothing. Show it FAILS at HEAD.
2. In server/services/ai-governance/classification/heuristic-classifier.ts DETECTORS (lines 33-48), add phi-class detectors: subject/patient/participant/randomization identifiers (e.g. /\b(?:subject|patient|participant|pt|screening|randomi[sz]ation)\s*(?:id|no\.?|number|#)?\s*[:#]?\s*[A-Z]{0,3}\d{3,}(?:[-/]\d+)*\b/i), demographic narrative ('\d{1,3}-year-old (?:male|female|man|woman|boy|girl)'), and labelled dates of death, admission or hospitalisation. Keep each regex anchored to a label so regulatory prose does not false-positive. Update the module header to say what is covered.
3. In server/services/ai-gateway/pii-screen.ts extractRequestText (lines 102-114), also decode base64 document blocks whose media_type is text/plain and include their text. Export a new requestCarriesUnscreenedMedia(request) that returns true for image blocks, PDF/base64 document blocks, Files-API file blocks and request.imageContent. Move the media test out of gateway.ts ledgerDataClass (lines 4836-4843) into this function and have ledgerDataClass call it, so there is one implementation.
4. In gateway.ts route() classification (lines 1398-1413) and the embedding path (lines 1668-1682): when the text result is 'none' and requestCarriesUnscreenedMedia(request) is true, set sensitiveDataClass to 'phi' (PHI-possible) and record the basis 'unscreened_media' on the request and the ledger row. decideSensitivePlacement (sensitive-placement-policy.ts:47-) then requires a zero-retention-approved placement. Do NOT map it to 'unknown': that is DENY_DETECTOR_FAILURE and would misreport the reason.
5. Clinical-document floor: when payloadProvenance is 'tenant_governed' and the callerModule/taskType is a clinical drafting or analysis task (document_analysis, section generation, AnA attachment intake in routes/ana-ri/stream.ts:1628-1675), raise 'none' to 'phi'. Keep the list as an explicit const in pii-screen.ts with a comment that names each entry.
6. Leave AI_CLASSIFIER_MODE=slm documented as not implemented. In server/startup/ai-governance-posture.ts, refuse boot in production when AI_CLASSIFIER_MODE=slm, because slm-classifier.ts:52-55 silently uses the heuristic even with a URL set.
7. Re-run the step-1 tests and show they now pass. Run server/services/ai-gateway/__tests__/tenant-capacity.test.ts and the existing classification tests to confirm no regressions.
8. Pilot operations (founder): until steps 2-5 land, set the pilot organization's placement policy to zero_data_retention=true, and set AI_PROVIDER_PLACEMENT_APPROVALS so that only a contracted ZDR Anthropic/Bedrock lane carries zeroRetentionApproved. gateway.ts:4693-4705 then enforces ZDR on every call regardless of class.
All commits go on concept2cure-v2 (Rule 0).
findings.acceptance: (a) The new classifier test fails at HEAD and passes after the change. The SAE narrative, subject ID and randomization examples classify phi:true; plain regulatory prose stays public. (b) The new gateway test fails at HEAD and passes after: in production+enforce, an image-only or PDF-only request to a provider without zero-retention approval rejects with GatewayPolicyError and nothing is dispatched; the same request to a ZDR-approved provider is served, and its ledger row shows data class phi with basis unscreened_media. (c) A text/plain attachment containing 'MRN: 12345678' is classified phi (its text is now screened). (d) Production boot refuses AI_CLASSIFIER_MODE=slm.

At 92ccdba1 it was request.organizationId || '__global__' (policy.ts:520). gateway.ts ~3586-3615 refuseUnboundInProduction rejects production calls with no tenant before any bucket. Still open: policy.ts:259 rateBuckets is still a per-process Map; terraform/stack has api_desired_count but no Redis/ElastiCache (grep finds none), so the effective org limit is 100/min x task count. The never-checked dailyCost accumulator was deleted (grep dailyCost server -> none) rather than enforced, and no per-org token or cost cap exists anywhere in the gateway. bootstrap/register-ai-routes.ts:24 still wires only enforceWeeklyLimit('requests') on /api/ana, /api/ana-ri and /api/chat. enforceWeeklyLimit.ts:113-122 still fails open by default. findings.remaining: (1) Rate buckets are in-memory per process (policy.ts:259), so the limit multiplies with ECS task count and resets on deploy. (2) No per-organisation token or cost cap is enforced in the gateway, and none is applied by default per plan. findings.severityRationale: Attribution is correct now. Every bound call is metered to its org, and tenants no longer share a bucket. For one invited, founder-supported pilot org, the remaining gaps are spend control and multi-instance precision, not safety or integrity. They need fixing before enterprise GA or self-serve plans.

ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING plus a row-count assertion (Rule 1 seed corollary), or resolve defaults in code from the org's plan when no row exists. Terraform has no Redis, so either (a) provision ElastiCache in terraform/stack and back checkRateLimit (policy.ts:541-580) with INCR+PEXPIRE on key ai:rl:{rateBucketKey}:{floor(now/60000)}, or (b) without Redis, divide maxRequestsPerMinutePerOrg (gateway.ts:4311) by an AI_RATE_LIMIT_INSTANCE_COUNT env set from var.api_desired_count in terraform/stack/main.tf, and document that it is approximate. findings.instructions:
1. Work on concept2cure-v2 only (git pull --ff-only, or fetch and merge, never rebase). First record the red case: bring up `docker compose -f docker-compose.beta.yml --env-file .env.beta up --build`, POST a clean PDF to /api/vault/ingest, and save the 503 FILE_SCAN_UNAVAILABLE response under docs/evidence/.
2. In docker-compose.beta.yml and docker-compose.yml, add a `clamav` service on network c2c. Use the image pinned at terraform/stack/variables.tf:91 (clamav/clamav:1.4.6@sha256:57deb108fc4c72778aa83eafbca7bb7153e28c3f57c005afd38d31f16da86f23), the environment CLAMD_CONF_StreamMaxLength=100M and CLAMD_CONF_AlertExceedsMax=yes (as at terraform/modules/ecs-fargate/main.tf:242-246), and healthcheck test ['CMD-SHELL','clamdcheck.sh'], interval 30s, timeout 10s, retries 3, start_period 300s. Publish no host port. On the `app` service, add `depends_on: clamav: condition: service_healthy` and the environment CLAMAV_HOST: clamav and CLAMAV_PORT: '3310'. Update each file's header comment, including the memory note: clamd holds about 1.3 GB, and briefly twice that during a reload.
3. In scripts/ci/check-compose-boot-contract.mjs, add a rule for every stack whose app has NODE_ENV=production. CLAMAV_HOST must be a non-empty literal naming a service in the same file. That service must have a healthcheck, and the app must depend on it with condition service_healthy (the compose equivalent of deploy-aws.yml:716-737). Add a --self-test case that removes the clamav service and asserts the check fails. Run the self-test against the HEAD compose files before step 2 and show it red.
4. In server/services/securityHealth.ts checkClamavConnectivity (:222-233): when NODE_ENV === 'production' and CLAMAV_HOST is unset, return status 'fail', critical: true, reason 'CLAMAV_HOST not set: production refuses every upload (server/middleware/uploadSafety.ts)'. Keep 'skipped' for development and test only. Extend its unit test with a production-and-unset case, which is red at HEAD.
5. In /readyz (server/startup/inline-endpoints.ts:50), add deps.virusScan. In production with CLAMAV_HOST set, send zPING\0 over TCP and expect PONG within 2 s, caching the result for at most 30 s. 'down' makes /readyz return 503. Outside production, report 'skipped'. Add a test beside server/startup/__tests__/readyz-vault-storage.test.ts with a fake listener that never answers, so 'down' is red before the change. Do not point the ECS container healthCheck at /readyz (terraform/modules/ecs-fargate/main.tf:181-205 explains why).
6. After terraform apply on AWS staging, run four checks: an EICAR upload gets 400 FILE_SCAN_REJECTED; a clean PDF gets 201; a roughly 45 MB PDF gets 201, which proves the CLAMD_CONF_StreamMaxLength override is honoured by the image; and stopping clamd leaves /readyz at 503 until ECS replaces the task. File the outputs under docs/evidence/.

findings.title: SSO (SAML JIT) and SCIM-provisioned users still cannot apply any electronic signature; the only workaround is minting a local password through Forgot password, which bypasses the IdP
findings.evidenceAtHead: server/routes/sso.ts:922 still creates SAML JIT users with passwordHash `saml:${crypto.randomUUID()}`. server/routes/scim.ts:840 creates SCIM users with `scim:${crypto.randomUUID()}`. server/services/part11/reverify-signer.ts:150-245 (verifySignerPassword) admits a signer only on a bcrypt match against users.password_hash; a placeholder hash never matches, and the failure is counted toward lockout (:236-237). SignerReverified.authenticationMethod is only 'password' | 'password+mfa' (:39-47). There is no IdP step-up, ForceAuthn or signing-PIN path anywhere in the module. In production an authenticator is also required (:84-87, :297-300). Every signing ceremony goes through reverifySigner: task-signoff.ts:192, mdx-qms.ts:583, ana-features.ts:2255, pccp.ts:272, governed-signed-act.ts:204, submission-sign-release.ts:260, document-lifecycle.ts:130, mdx-rbm.ts:1034,1155. So an SSO user also cannot sign a Submission Center release or a QMS record. The only code that reads saml:/scim: hashes is a compliance report (audit/compliance-reports/queries/access-review.ts:69). Workaround present at HEAD: server/routes/auth.ts handleForgotPassword (:2335-2440) has no SSO exclusion, so an SSO account can set a local bcrypt password and then sign. MFA enrolment (auth.ts:2096, :2174) needs no password.
findings.remaining: Everything in the audit's fix: IdP re-authentication bound to the signature (SAML ForceAuthn, or OIDC prompt=login with max_age) or a signing PIN, the method recorded in the manifest, and a signing dialog that offers it to SSO accounts. Meanwhile the forgot-password route lets an SSO-provisioned account hold an IdP-independent local password. That is the only way such a user can sign today, and it weakens IdP control. Deprovisioning still works only through SCIM's account standing.
findings.severityRationale: The pilot is sales-led with invited orgs. Invitations create password accounts (password-setup-token.ts:98-108), and those sign normally with password and authenticator. SSO-only signing is not on the pilot's critical path unless the design partner mandates SSO, in which case it becomes P0: nobody could approve, freeze, release or sign QMS records. That is the founder's open question 3 in the audit.
findings.humanTestingNote: Testers will not see this with invited password accounts. A tester who signs in through SAML SSO and tries to sign (Authoring approve or freeze, Submission release, QMS) gets 'Signature rejected: password verification failed (§11.200)', and repeated tries count toward the account lockout. Workaround for testing only: use invited password accounts.
findings.instructions:
1. Founder decides two things: the signing method for SSO accounts (IdP re-authentication or a signing PIN), and whether SSO-provisioned accounts may hold a local password. Record the decision in docs/LAUNCH_DEFINITION_OF_DONE.md. Work on concept2cure-v2 only (merge, never rebase).
2. Red first: add tests/db/sso-signer.dbtest.ts. It creates a user with password_hash 'saml:<uuid>' and an enrolled authenticator and drives the authoring e-sign route and submission-sign-release (submission-sign-release.ts:260) with the new credential, expecting success. At HEAD both return 401 PASSWORD_VERIFICATION_FAILED.
3. For IdP re-authentication:
   - in server/routes/sso.ts, add POST /api/sso/step-up/start {intent, recordId}. It issues an AuthnRequest with ForceAuthn="true" and a single-use nonce as RelayState;
   - in the existing ACS handler, on a step-up RelayState, verify InResponseTo, that NameID/email equals the session user, and that AuthnInstant is within 5 minutes;
   - insert a grant into a new table public.signing_step_up_grants (id uuid pk, organization_id INTEGER NOT NULL, user_id int not null, intent text, record_id text, authn_instant timestamptz, expires_at timestamptz, consumed_at timestamptz). Create it in a new IF NOT EXISTS-guarded migration added to C2C_MIGRATION_FILES before the final sweep pair (ci:migration-set-order), so the tenant RLS sweep covers it.
   For a PIN instead: add users.signing_secret_hash in a new additive migration (ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS), and an Account route to set it that requires a fresh IdP sign-in plus TOTP. Hash it with bcrypt and count wrong PINs against the same lockout.
4. In server/services/part11/reverify-signer.ts:
   - add stepUpGrantId (or signingPin) to SignerCredentials;
   - add authenticationMethod values 'idp-reauth+mfa' (or 'pin+mfa');
   - when the account's hash starts with 'saml:' or 'scim:', verify the new credential instead of the password. Consume the grant atomically with UPDATE … SET consumed_at=now() WHERE consumed_at IS NULL AND expires_at>now() AND user_id=$ AND record_id=$ RETURNING. Keep the account-standing, lockout and authenticator rules unchanged.
   Thread the credential through every caller listed in evidenceAtHead, and persist the derived method on the signature row and in the §11.50 manifest.
5. Client signing dialog: expose the account's auth method next to signingPostureOf (reverify-signer.ts:102-107) on GET /session and /me. Render 'Re-authenticate with your identity provider' (popup or redirect to /api/sso/step-up/start) instead of the password field for SSO accounts.
6. In the same change, refuse a local password for SSO-provisioned accounts. handleForgotPassword (auth.ts:2335) and handleResetPassword (:2453) return the same generic response but issue no token when password_hash starts with 'saml:' or 'scim:', so the IdP stays the only credential. Show this refusal failing before the change.
7. Make each of these fail and keep the failing cases as tests: a stale grant older than 5 minutes, a replayed grant, a grant for another user or record, and a password attempt on an SSO account.
findings.acceptance:
- Red first: at HEAD, a SAML JIT user's sign attempt returns 401 PASSWORD_VERIFICATION_FAILED (captured in the new dbtest).
- After: the same user signs after step-up, and the signature row and export manifest show authenticationMethod 'idp-reauth+mfa' (or 'pin+mfa'). Stale, replayed and cross-user or cross-record grants are refused with 401. Forgot-password for a saml: or scim: account issues no reset token.
- The existing password-account signing dbtests stay green.
findings.dependencies: Founder decisions on the method and on local passwords for SSO accounts. The design partner's SSO requirement sets the priority. The SSO lane owns server/routes/sso.ts and the IdP test tenant.

findings.title: Vault versioning works now (server-assigned check-in, version list, compare, conflict offers 'upload as new version'); restore and check-out/check-in are still missing
findings.evidenceAtHead:
Fixed:
- server/routes/vault-ingest.ts:133-135 accepts supersedesDocumentId (a sent version or filing is refused, :171-185).
- server/services/vault/vault-version-checkin.ts planCheckIn (:69-187) requires the head to be current in the caller's program and org, assigns the next major (nextMajorVersion :59-62), and runs again under FOR UPDATE from vault-ingest.service.ts:266.
- migrations/20260930_vault_documents_version_lineage.sql adds a lineage guard trigger and a one-successor index, and it is in the applier set (scripts/db/migration-set.mjs:2236).
- GET /:id/documents/:documentId/versions (server/routes/c2c/project-vault.ts:1647-1700) lists the family with SHA-256, size, uploader, lifecycle and placements.
- client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/VaultVersions.tsx:385-394 has 'Upload new version', and VaultVersionCompare is imported at :23.
- Vault.tsx:853 and :1449-1452 offer 'Upload as a new version of <title>' on the name-clash conflict, and useVaultUpload.ts:117-122 sends supersedesDocumentId.
Still missing:
- grep -i 'restore|checkout|check-out|checked_out' over server/services/vault/*.ts, project-vault.ts, vault-ingest.ts, VaultVersions.tsx and Vault.tsx finds no restore or check-out feature.
- Re-uploading a prior version's bytes is refused with 409 CONTENT_ALREADY_A_VERSION ('These exact bytes are already version N', vault-version-checkin.ts:171-184), so a prior version cannot be restored.
- Versions are sequential majors only (no minor or draft versions).
findings.fixedBy: 5b9b67bbf (VR-08 check-in: vault-ingest.ts:133, vault-version-checkin.ts, migrations/20260930_vault_documents_version_lineage.sql); 15a38fbfe (VR-09 version list: project-vault.ts:1647, vault-version-family.ts, VaultVersions.tsx); 38179495f (a changed file is offered as the next version: Vault.tsx:1449-1452, useVaultUpload.ts:117-122).
findings.remaining:
1. No restore: there is no route to promote a prior version to a new version with a reason, and re-uploading its bytes is refused.
2. No check-out/check-in reservation: concurrent check-ins are only serialised at commit, and the loser is refused with VERSION_NOT_CURRENT. Nothing stops a second author from working on the document while it is out for revision.
3. Only major versions exist (1.0 → 2.0), so there is no minor or draft versioning.
findings.severityRationale: The dead end is gone. A revised protocol uploads as v2, its lineage is kept and enforced by the database, every version is listed and downloadable, and the conflict path offers the new-version action. Restore and check-out are standard GxP document-control features an enterprise buyer will ask for. A pilot can run without them, because downloading a prior version and re-uploading an edited copy works.
findings.humanTestingNote: Uploading a revised file works ('Upload new version' in the version list, or 'Upload as a new version of …' on a name clash). A tester who tries to restore an earlier version by uploading its file again gets 409 'These exact bytes are already version N of this document. Nothing was saved.' There is no restore button and no check-out. Workaround: none for an exact restore. Download the earlier version, and an edited copy uploads as a new version.
findings.acceptance:
- Red first: at HEAD, the restore route 404s and re-uploading v1's bytes returns 409 CONTENT_ALREADY_A_VERSION (captured).
- After: restoring v1 creates v3 with v1's SHA-256, superseding v2, with the reason in the audit chain. The version list shows v3 as current, with v1 and v2 retained and downloadable.
- While user A holds a check-out, user B's check-in or restore returns 409 DOCUMENT_CHECKED_OUT. After A checks in or the check-out expires, B succeeds.
- Under the runtime role, org Y cannot read or write org X's check-out row (RLS).
findings.dependencies: None blocking. CAT1-15 (withdraw/obsolete) completes the lifecycle. CAT1-06 if check-out should be limited to project members.

findings.title: Vault admission: allowlist widened, but no .xpt/.zip/.pptx, a 50 MB in-memory cap, and extraction/OCR/chunking still run inside the request
findings.evidenceAtHead: shared/constants/document-intake-formats.ts:17-38: the Vault list is now .pdf .docx .xlsx .txt .md .csv .tsv .json .xml .png .jpg .jpeg .gif .doc .xls .rtf. Still absent: .xpt, .sas7bdat, .zip, .pptx. Grep for xpt finds no upload path, only the eCTD/STF validators. :46 VAULT_UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES = 50*1024*1024. server/routes/vault-ingest.ts:55 MAX_FILE_SIZE = VAULT_UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES ('unchanged 50 MB'). :69-80 multer.memoryStorage() with limits.fileSize. server/services/storage/storage-provider.ts:20,51: put() takes a Buffer, and get() returns one. server/services/vault/vault-ingest.service.ts:381-404: pdfPageCount and extractDocumentText (OCR) are awaited inside the request. :715-718: chunkDocumentForIngest is awaited after commit, and it embeds over the network when ana.vault_chunking is on. OCR has no concurrency limit (server/services/ocr/*). terraform/modules/alb/main.tf:36 idle_timeout = 60. Compared against 92ccdba1:server/routes/vault-ingest.ts:53-56, which had the 9-extension list, 50 MB and memoryStorage.
findings.fixedBy: 10222a024 (shared/constants/document-intake-formats.ts:17-38): the allowlist was widened to .tsv/.json/.xml (so define.xml is admitted) and to .png/.jpg/.jpeg/.gif, with byte checks in server/utils/fileSignature.ts:45-64,134-150. 13efb8fca: one 50 MB cap shared by Vault and Data Room (no increase).
findings.remaining:
1. SAS transport datasets (.xpt), .zip and .pptx are refused with 400 FILE_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED.
2. Anything over 50 MB is refused with 413.
3. The whole file is buffered in memory three times over: multer memoryStorage, the Buffer-based storage put(), and the Buffer AV scan.
4. Text extraction, OCR and passage chunking (plus optional embedding) run synchronously inside the HTTP request. Behind the 60 s ALB idle timeout, a long OCR can return 504 while the ingest continues on the server.
5. Concurrent large or scanned uploads can exhaust the memory of one Fargate task.
findings.severityRationale: An FDA IND for a small biotech normally carries SEND datasets (.xpt plus define.xml) for nonclinical studies that started after Dec 2017 (FDA Data Standards Catalog). define.xml is now admitted, but .xpt is not, so the pilot cannot hold or file its Module 4/5 datasets in the platform. Large report PDFs over 50 MB are refused. This is not P0: PDF and DOCX, the bulk of IND content, upload, and datasets can be handled outside the platform with founder support.
findings.humanTestingNote:
Symptoms:
- The Vault file picker does not offer .xpt, .zip or .pptx. Choosing one anyway returns 'File type .xpt is not allowed. Accepted: …' (400).
- A file over 50 MB returns 'The file exceeds the 50 MB ingest limit.' (413).
- A large scanned PDF keeps the upload spinner running while it is OCR'd in the request. On staging behind the ALB this can end in a 504 even though the document was admitted. Refresh the Vault before retrying, or the retry may be treated as a re-upload or next version.

Workaround: test with text-layer PDFs and DOCX under 50 MB, and keep datasets outside the Vault.
findings.instructions:
1. File types. In shared/constants/document-intake-formats.ts:17-33, add vault:true entries:
   - '.xpt': textExtraction 'none', byteCheckSupported true, chat false, limitation 'SAS V5 transport; stored and hashed, not parsed'.
   - '.pptx': textExtraction 'none'.
   - '.zip': only if the founder confirms zipped content belongs in the Vault.
   In server/utils/fileSignature.ts, add signature checks: XPT V5 starts with the ASCII 'HEADER RECORD*******LIBRARY HEADER RECORD!!!!!!!' at offset 0; PPTX is ZIP magic PK\x03\x04 plus a presentationml content type (the MIME is already in the list at :64); ZIP is PK\x03\x04. Bind each MIME to its extension in verifyDeclaredTypeForName. Add a unit test asserting that every vault:true format has byteCheckSupported true, and show it failing by adding a format without a check.
2. Disk buffering. In server/routes/vault-ingest.ts:69-80, replace multer.memoryStorage() with multer.diskStorage into a per-request temp dir under os.tmpdir(). Unlink in a finally block on every outcome, including 4xx. Raise VAULT_UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES (shared constant :46) to the founder-chosen ceiling (for example 1 GB). Keep CHAT_UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES equal, or document why they differ, because 13efb8fca made them one cap on purpose.
3. Streaming storage. Add putStream({orgId, programId, filename, mime, stream}) to IStorageProvider (server/services/storage/storage-provider.ts:51). Implement it in s3-provider.ts with @aws-sdk/lib-storage Upload (multipart), computing SHA-256 while streaming, and in local-provider.ts with stream.pipeline to a file. Keep put(Buffer) for small callers. ingestVaultDocument takes a file path and uses putStream.
4. AV on files. Add scanFile/scanStream to server/utils/virusScan.ts (INSTREAM chunks from a read stream), and let assertUploadSafe (server/middleware/uploadSafety.ts) take a path. Keep it fail-closed in production. Set clamd StreamMaxLength at or above the new cap (ties to CAT1-01).
5. Async extraction. In server/services/vault/vault-ingest.service.ts, move :381-404 (pdfPageCount, extractDocumentText) and :708-718 (chunkDocumentForIngest) out of the request:
   - Commit the document with processing_status 'PENDING' (already written at :527) and a catalog extraction outcome of 'pending'.
   - Process it in a worker: bull is already a dependency at package.json:542, or use a DB-polled sweep modelled on server/services/vault/document-chunking-backfill.service.ts:147 backfillVaultChunks.
   - The worker reads the bytes from storage, extracts, updates extracted_text/page_count/word_count/processing_status ('EXTRACTED' or 'EXTRACTION_FAILED' with the reason) through recordExtractionOutcome, then chunks.
   - Confirm that the VR-06 immutability trigger on vault.documents permits these columns. If it does not, amend the creating migration in place with a dated header note (Rule 1); do not append.
6. Concurrency. Add a per-process semaphore (2 to 4) around OCR in server/services/ocr/index.ts.
7. Honest state. In client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/Vault.tsx, show 'Reading…' for PENDING and the stated failure for EXTRACTION_FAILED, never an empty excerpt. Full-text and passage search results state how many documents are still being read.
8. Verify every gate failing first: run each acceptance test on HEAD, record the red, then implement.
findings.acceptance:
1. A valid SAS V5 .xpt uploads with 201 and downloads with an X-Content-SHA256 equal to its source hash. A PE executable renamed .xpt gets 400 from the signature check. Both tests are red on HEAD (the first gets 400 FILE_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED).
2. A 200 MB PDF uploads with 201 using the local provider, and process RSS grows by less than 64 MB during the request. Red on HEAD (413).
3. A 300-page image-only PDF upload returns in under 5 s with processingStatus 'PENDING', and the worker then sets 'EXTRACTED' with page_count 300 and passages indexed. Red on HEAD, where the response waits for OCR.
4. Under NODE_ENV=production, an EICAR file still gets 400 FILE_SCAN_REJECTED, and with clamd stopped the upload gets 503.
5. The temp dir is empty after success, after a 4xx and after a 5xx.
findings.dependencies: CAT1-01 (a deployed clamd sized for large streams). A founder decision on the size ceiling and on whether .zip is admitted. Infra: S3 multipart permissions on the task role.

findings.title: Authoring approval: a document's author can still approve it with one signature, and no review is required
findings.remaining: Authoring /e-sign and /sign still let the document's creator (OWNER grant) or any global admin with a signing role approve and freeze alone. No REVIEWER signature or completed review is required before APPROVER. There is no multi-approver option, and the platform's canonical separation-of-duties check is not applied to Authoring.
findings.severityRationale: A GxP pilot's QMS SOPs and its auditor expect four-eyes approval of controlled regulatory documents. The platform's own policy (separation-of-duties.ts header: adopted 'for every review/approval/lock', 'un-disableable') is violated by the approval path of a launch app, and P-18 tells the customer the opposite. This is not P0: signatures are re-verified, attributable and hash-bound; the Vault copy will not carry a self-approval; and the pilot can run under a two-person SOP in the meantime.
findings.humanTestingNote:
Symptoms:
- A tester with an admin, approver or reviewer org role who created a document can open E-sign, choose Approval and sign. The document immediately becomes APPROVED and frozen, with one signature and no review.
- Filing that document to the Vault then reports that the Authoring approval was not carried (the author signed), so Authoring says Approved while the Vault version is unapproved.

Workaround: run the approval journey with separate accounts (author with the member role, reviewer, approver) and log self-approval acceptance as a known defect.
findings.instructions:
1. Model authorship. In server/services/governance/separation-of-duties.ts, add an 'authoring-document' case to resolveTargetAuthors (:327). The authors are:
   - authoring_documents.created_by (WHERE id = $1 AND tenant_id = $2);
   - UNION DISTINCT doc_revisions.created_by, joined through authoring_sections s ON s.id = r.section_id AND s.doc_id = $1 AND r.tenant_id = $2 (include origin 'genesis', which is the creator; exclude 'platform-generated');
   - the actor recorded when an AI draft was accepted (authoring_ai_draft_candidates), if that column exists.
   Cast ids to integer. Show a lookup failure throwing (503 path) in a unit test.
2. Enforce in the routes.
   - In POST /docs/:docId/e-sign (authoring.router.ts:5294), after the meaning validation and before reverifyAuthoringSigner (:5332), call assertSignerIsNotAuthor(`authoring-document:${docId}`, tenantId, Number(getActorId(req)), { command: 'sign', meaning: meaning === 'APPROVER' ? 'approval' : meaning === 'REVIEWER' ? 'review' : 'authorship' }).
   - Map the errors exactly as server/routes/document-lifecycle.ts:251 does: SeparationOfDutiesError → 403 SEPARATION_OF_DUTIES, AuthorUnresolved → 409, Unverified → 503.
   - Repeat the call inside the BEGIN block with { client } to close the race.
   - Apply the same in POST /docs/:docId/sign (:7373) and, for meaning REVIEWER, in POST /docs/:docId/freeze (:5019).
3. Required review. When meaning === 'APPROVER', and in /sign when the step clears the last workflow step, refuse with 409 REVIEW_REQUIRED (nothing written) unless, inside the transaction:
   (a) an authoring_signatures row exists with meaning 'REVIEWER' for this doc and content_hash = the current docHash, signed by someone who is neither the approver nor in the author set; and
   (b) no authoring_reviews row for the doc has review_status 'pending'.
   Extract this predicate from server/services/regulatory/authoring-approval-carryover.ts (the same rules: a reviewer covers D, signed no later than the approval, by a different person, neither is the author) into one exported function used by both, so there is no duplication. Then rewrite that file's header at :44-45.
4. Optional per-org tightening (admin may only tighten): an organization setting min_authoring_approvers, default 1. The APPROVED flip happens only on the Nth distinct APPROVER signature over the same docHash.
5. Tell the user before the dialog. In callerDocumentAccess (authoring.router.ts:1636-1745), fold the SoD and review-required decisions into `esign`, so DocumentWorkbench and AuthoringFilingBar (:145-148) withhold Approval and show the reason. The server stays the enforcement point.
6. After the code lands, correct the P-18 text in docs/LAUNCH_DEFINITION_OF_DONE.md to match. Do not edit it before.
7. Failing-first tests (pglite or tests/db with three users holding signing roles):
   (a) the creator with the admin role signs APPROVER → 403 SEPARATION_OF_DUTIES (red on HEAD: 200 and APPROVED);
   (b) a non-author approver with no REVIEWER signature → 409 REVIEW_REQUIRED (red on HEAD);
   (c) the reviewer also signing APPROVER → 403;
   (d) author signs AUTHOR, a reviewer signs REVIEWER, a third person signs APPROVER → APPROVED and frozen, and file-to-vault carries the approval.
   Run npm run ci:sign-ceremony.
findings.acceptance:
1. On a document created by user A (admin role), A's APPROVER e-sign returns 403 SEPARATION_OF_DUTIES, and the document status, authoring_signatures and frozen_documents are unchanged. Red on HEAD.
2. User B (approver role, not an author) signing APPROVER before any REVIEWER signature on the current hash returns 409 REVIEW_REQUIRED. Red on HEAD.
3. After C (reviewer) signs REVIEWER, B's APPROVER succeeds, and file-to-vault reports the approval carried.
4. The same refusals apply on /docs/:docId/sign.
5. The E-sign dialog does not offer Approval to the author, and shows the server's reason.
findings.dependencies: None blocking. CAT1-06 is needed only if approvers are to be designated per project. Test fixtures need at least three users with signing roles (P-18 approver/reviewer assignment exists).

findings.remaining:
All of the impact remains:
- A document uploaded to the project's Vault is never retrieved or cited by the editor's AI draft.
- Retrieval spans every project in the org, so a draft for program A can cite program B's Data Room uploads.
- Two retrieval stacks persist: the editor uses lumen atoms, AnA uses Vault passages.
The pre-audit tenant scoping (organizationUuid) and the 1d5de6ca6 always-on passage index are enablers, not a fix.
findings.severityRationale: 'AI drafting with citations to Vault evidence' is a core Authoring launch journey. Citing another program's material inside one sponsor is a data-integrity problem for a regulatory draft. The UI tells the user the evidence is project-scoped when it is not. This is not P0: there is no cross-tenant leak (org-scoped), retrieval status is reported honestly (ok/empty/failed), attributions resolve only to retrieved sources, and the AnA drafting path is grounded in the project's Vault.
findings.humanTestingNote:
Requires a configured AI provider.

Symptoms:
- A tester uploads a study report to the project's Vault, opens a section in the editor and clicks 'Draft <section> from Data Room sources'. The draft reports that no Data Room source met the relevance threshold (not grounded), or it cites chat/Data Room uploads from any project in the organisation. The Vault upload is never cited.
- Citations never show a Vault document or page.

Workaround: ask AnA, in the open project, to draft the section (its passage search reads the project's Vault), then send it to the editor through the canvas.
findings.instructions:
1. Project. In authoring.router.ts, add `to_jsonb(d)->>'client_program_id' AS program_id` to the section query (:3796-3802). If program_id is null, set retrievalStatus 'failed' with retrievalError 'This document is not in a project, so no project evidence could be retrieved', and do not fall back to an org-wide search (fail closed).
2. One retrieval path. Replace the searchHybrid block (:3832-3846) with searchDocumentPassages({ organizationId: tenantId, organizationUuid: orgUuid, query: searchQuery }, { limit: 5, programId: section.program_id }) from server/services/vault/document-passage-search.ts.
   - Map each hit to retrievedChunks { content: hit.text, title: hit.documentTitle, vaultDocumentId: hit.documentId, pageNumber: hit.pageNumber, chunkIndex: hit.chunkIndex }.
   - PassageSearchUnavailableError → 'failed' with its message.
   - No hits → 'empty', with the coverage note (indexed / total, unfiled Data Room uploads) carried in the draft metadata.
3. Evidence block (:3858-3870). Render each source as `[SRC-n] "<title>", p. <page>` (omit the page when it is null).
4. Attribution to Vault documents. Make the draft candidate and accept path (authoring.router.ts:4015-4075; services/clinical-regulatory-evidence/draft-candidate-store.ts; POST /sections/:sectionId/ai/draft/accept at :4142) carry a Vault reference: document id, version, page and chunk index. Either:
   (a) register one cre_evidence_sources row per Vault document version at ingest (source_type 'vault_document', metadata.vaultDocumentId) and resolve it like the existing link forms in retrieval-source-link.ts:61; or
   (b) add a nullable vault_document_id/page column to the candidate source table, in a new additive migration or by amending its creating migration in place with a dated note (Rule 1).
   The accept gate must still refuse an id that was not retrieved.
5. Zero duplication. Remove the lumen-atom retrieval from this route in the same change. Data Room captures reach the Vault through VR-11a filing; unfiled captures are reported in coverage, not searched silently. If the founder wants unfiled uploads included, route them through ragRouter (one router), not a second path.
6. Client. In AuthoringAiDraft.tsx (:156-193 messages, :533, :565, :573), say 'this project's Vault', and show document and page for each source.
7. Founder. Decide whether ana.vault_chunking (embeddings, which sends text to the provider) is on for pilot tenants. Keyword passage search works without it.
8. Failing-first tests (pglite or tests/db): see the acceptance criteria. Run each on HEAD first and record the red.

findings.title: Controlled DOCX export still has no document-control header/footer, page x of y, TOC or house style, and defaults to A4; only the uncontrolled working copy got a DRAFT banner header/footer
findings.evidenceAtHead: Code: server/services/authoring/authoring-export.ts renderDocx (388-492). The Document at 464-486 sets only numbering, footnotes and sections; there are no styles, no features.updateFields and no TableOfContents. The sections ternary at 475-485 attaches headers and footers ONLY when args.workingCopy is set, and they hold only the DRAFT banner text (no PageNumber). A controlled export is `{ children }`, with no section properties, header, footer or page size. A grep of server/ for TableOfContents|PageNumber matches only legacy generators (docx/docxFactory.ts, universal-packager.ts, biotech-artifact-generator.ts, templateExtractor.ts, common/exportFormats.mjs), none of them on the authoring export path. Both callers use renderAuthoringExport: the POST /docs/:docId/export route (authoring.router.ts:6651) and file-to-vault (authoring-file-to-vault.ts:426). git diff 92ccdba1 HEAD on the two audited files changes only the working-copy banner, the XML figure placeholders and PDF fallback tracking. Command: a tsx probe called renderAuthoringExport on an APPROVED doc (id D1, version 4) with a stub executor and unzipped the result. Controlled: headerParts [], footerParts [], tocField false, PAGE/NUMPAGES fields false, settings updateFields false, doc id and version not in document.xml, pgSz w:w=11906 w:h=16838 (A4). Working copy: header1.xml and footer1.xml present (banner only), still no TOC, no PAGE/NUMPAGES, A4. The audited version (git show 92ccdba1) had sections: [{ children }], so the original finding was correct. findings.remaining: Everything the finding names is still missing from the controlled (filing) DOCX: a header with title, document ID, version and status; a footer with confidentiality text and 'Page X of Y'; a TOC field; Template Library/house styles; and a Letter page size for an FDA pilot. The working copy added in 1a8ebb3ae has a header and footer, but they carry only the 'DRAFT — uncontrolled copy · id · vN · status' banner, with no page numbers and no TOC. That banner is an uncontrolled-copy marker, not a document-control header. The Template Library's style-driven generator (docxFactory.generateRegulatory with templateSpecToDocxStyle) already has header, footer and page-x-of-y logic, but authoring export does not use it.
findings.severityRationale: This is not a security, tenant-isolation or data-integrity exposure, so it is not P0. But every controlled export a pilot user produces lacks the per-page document identification and page numbering that ICH M4 CTD organisation expects, and it renders on A4 for a US FDA pilot. The user has to rework each file in Word. Once a controlled export is edited, its bytes no longer match the artifactSha256 the export record attests (authoring-export.ts §11.10(b) hash). So the file the customer circulates or files is no longer the controlled record. Pilot users would rely on this output in production, so it must be fixed before then.

findings.instructions: 1. Work on concept2cure-v2 only (Rule 0). Write the failing test first: add server/services/authoring/__tests__/authoring-export-docx-layout.test.ts. It calls renderAuthoringExport (authoring-export.ts:565) with a stub executor `{ query: async () => ({ rows: [], rowCount: 0 }) }`, doc `{ id:'D1', title:'Clinical Overview', status:'APPROVED', version:4 }`, two sections with codes 2.5.1/2.5.2, format 'docx' and signatures []. Unzip it with JSZip (as server/routes/__tests__/authoringWorkingCopy.test.ts:112-125 does) and assert: a word/header*.xml containing 'D1', 'Version 4' and 'APPROVED'; a word/footer*.xml containing both a PAGE and a NUMPAGES field; document.xml containing a TOC field instruction (`TOC \o "1-3"`); word/settings.xml containing updateFields; and ` · Document ID · Version · ', with spec.header.text appended when set. Footer: confidentiality text (spec.brand.confidentialityNotice or spec.footer.text), then a TextRun with children ['Page ', PageNumber.CURRENT, ' of ', PageNumber.TOTAL_PAGES] (docx 9.7.1 supports this). When a banner is passed (working copy), add the bold banner as its own paragraph in BOTH header and footer, so the assertions at authoringWorkingCopy.test.ts:112-125 keep passing. 5. In renderDocx, replace the sections ternary (authoring-export.ts:475-485) with ONE section that always has `properties: { page: { size from style.page, margin: style.margins, pageNumbers: { start: 1 } } }` and the helper's headers and footers, passing banner: args.workingCopy?.banner. Do not remove the working-copy banner, and keep the working copy's missing signature manifestation (lines 451-461) unchanged. 6. Still in renderDocx, insert a 'Table of Contents' paragraph and `new docxNs.TableOfContents('Table of Contents', { hyperlink: true, headingStyleRange: '1-3' })` after the title and notice paragraphs (after line ~401). Section headings are already HEADING_1 (authoring-blocks-to-docx.ts:263). Add `features: { updateFields: true }` to the Document at line 464 so Word fills the TOC and page fields on open. Also add `styles: { default: { document: { run: { font: style.fonts.body, size: style.fontSizes.body } } }, paragraphStyles: Heading1-3 from style.fonts.heading / fontSizes.heading1-3 }`. 7. PDF parity, so the DOCX and PDF of one record agree (the module's stated invariant at prepareShared, authoring-export.ts:225-231). Extend PdfRenderOptions (server/export/renderers.ts:356) with `headerLine?`, `footerLine?` and `pageNumbers?: boolean`, and `format: 'Letter'|'A4'`. In renderHtmlToPdfTracked (369-395), set displayHeaderFooter with the lines plus ` of `. In renderFallbackPdf, stamp 'Page i of n' with the existing bufferPages loop (renderers.ts ~511-522). Pass these from renderPdf (authoring-export.ts:498-561). 8. House-style selection (shared with CAT1-16): accept an optional `templateId` in the bodies of POST /docs/:docId/export (authoring.router.ts:6539), POST /docs/:docId/working-copy (~6700) and file-to-vault. Resolve it with getTemplate(tenantId, id) (server/services/templates/templateStore.ts:173), which is tenant-scoped. An unknown or other-tenant id fails closed with 404 TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND before any audit or export row is written; never fall back silently to the default. Pass the normalized spec as `formatting`. Record templateId and a SHA-256 of the normalized spec in logExport metadata (router ~6680) and in the WORKING_COPY audit payload (~6735). 9. Client: in client/src/concept2cure/v2/editor/DownloadMenu.tsx, offer the org's active templates (GET /api/c2c/templates) as an optional 'Formatting' choice. Send templateId with both the controlled export and the working copy. 'Default (Letter)' sends nothing. 10. Re-run the step-1 test (now green), authoringWorkingCopy.test.ts and authoring-export-xml-figures.test.ts. Add negative cases: another tenant's templateId gives 404 with no export row written, and a spec with bodyFont 'Arial' shows up in word/styles.xml. findings.acceptance: (a) Failing-first: the new authoring-export-docx-layout.test.ts is shown failing at HEAD (no header/footer parts, no PAGE/NUMPAGES field, no TOC, pgSz 11906x16838) before the change, and passing after it. (b) A controlled DOCX export of an APPROVED document has a header on every page with title, document ID, version and status, and a footer with confidentiality text and 'Page X of Y' (PAGE and NUMPAGES fields). It has a TOC field over Heading 1-3 that Word populates on open (settings updateFields=true), Letter page size by default, and default/heading fonts from the template spec. (c) The working-copy DOCX has the same header and footer plus the bold DRAFT banner top and bottom and no signature manifestation; authoringWorkingCopy.test.ts passes unchanged. Another tenant's or an unknown templateId returns 404 and writes no export or audit row. findings.title: Agency DTDs, stylesheets and the STF DTD are still not vendored, so no package is ever DTD-validated (the FDA region-conformance over-claim is gone)
findings.evidenceAtHead: At 94b4f9238, `git ls-files | grep -iE '[.](dtd|xsl)$'` returns nothing. assets/ectd-dtd/ holds only README.md, checksums.txt (every manifest entry is still a commented '# <sha256>' placeholder, lines 44-50) and fixtures/index-{valid,invalid}.xml. `git log 92ccdba1..HEAD -- assets/ectd-dtd` shows only b434c39e3, which fixed the fixture's xlink namespace. server/services/ectd/dtd-bundler.ts:85-111 (REGIONAL_DTD, requiredDtdsForRegion) still names no STF DTD. The packager only checks that DTD files are present: regional-packager.ts:1246-1278 calls assessDtdReadiness, which is report-only unless ECTD_REQUIRE_DTD=true in production. It never runs xmllint --valid. The only DTD validation is in the qualification harness (server/services/ectd/qualification/qualify.ts:286-311, validateBackboneFile). That harness checks only index.xml and the regional backbone (:429, :435), returns `dtdSkipped` when the DTD is absent, and never checks STF files. Every compile reports the gap: server/routes/ectd-compile.ts:1176-1180 pushes 'The package references eCTD DTDs that are not bundled under util/dtd/ — it is not self-contained'. FIXED PART: at 92ccdba1, regional-backbone-readiness.ts had CONFORMANT_REGIONS={'fda'} and returned regionConformant:true for the region alone. At HEAD, classifyRegionalBackbone (server/services/ectd/regional-backbone-readiness.ts:117-135) returns true only when fdaBackboneGaps (regional-packager.ts:465-474) is empty. fdaContactGaps (:477-489) always yields at least one gap: either no contact, or a phone with no telephone-number-type. So FDA is never reported conformant. regionConformant is still not derived from any DTD validation.
findings.fixedBy: 8f1c2ba5f (2026-10-01): server/services/ectd/regional-backbone-readiness.ts:117-135 and server/services/submission-gateways/regional-packager.ts:1416-1421. regionConformant now comes from the builder's reported gaps, so FDA is no longer conformant by region alone.
findings.remaining: (1) These files are not vendored or checksummed: ICH ich-ectd-3-2.dtd and ectd-2-0.xsl; FDA us-regional-v3-3.dtd and us-regional.xsl; ICH STF ich-stf-v2-2.dtd; and the FDA Module 1 valid-values file. (2) No xmllint --valid runs in assemble, compile or transmit. The qualification harness skips DTD validation when the DTD is absent and never checks STF files. (3) regionConformant comes from the builder's own report, not from a passing DTD validation. (4) The STF DTD is not in requiredDtdsForRegion, so the self-containment check ignores it. (5) The gate defaults stay report-only; this is tracked as CAT2-08.
findings.severityRationale: FDA validates every backbone against the agency DTDs and technically rejects invalid ones. With no DTD in the repo, nobody can know whether a pilot sequence would be accepted, and CAT2-02/03/04 show it would not be. The files are public agency downloads, so acquiring them is cheap. That is the precondition for fixing and proving CAT2-02 to CAT2-04, so this stays P0 for an FDA eCTD pilot.
findings.humanTestingNote: Every eCTD Compile result in Submission Center is 'not submission-ready' with the blocker 'The package references eCTD DTDs that are not bundled under util/dtd/ — it is not self-contained. On staging, pointing ECTD_DTD_DIR at a folder holding the official DTD and XSL files clears the message, but it does not prove the XML is valid. DTD validity is not visible anywhere in the product.
