- Related: CAT2-23.

findings.title: QMS approval signature still binds only the artifact pointer; the linked artifact's content is mutable after approval
findings.evidenceAtHead:
(1) The digest at server/services/qms/document-approval-signature.ts:128-146 covers `artifactId: row.artifact_id`. It covers no artifact version and no content hash. The function is unchanged except for APPROVABLE_STATES (`git diff 92ccdba1 HEAD`). The approval never reads concept2cure_artifacts.
(2) The audit marked mutability as UNVERIFIED. It is now verified: the artifact's content is rewritten in place on several paths:
- server/services/ana/artifactVersionStore.ts:350-355 (`UPDATE concept2cure_artifacts SET version, content, content_hash`, with no status check);
- server/services/ana/submission-chat-apply-rewrite.ts:651-660;
- server/services/module3-convergence-service.ts:651-660.
(3) The pointer can be set and is not tenant-checked: docCreate and docPatch accept artifactId (mdx-qms.ts:166, :459). The create INSERT (:368-380) stores it with no tenant check and no FK. migrations/20260511_qms_and_labeling.sql:39 is a plain integer.
(4) The append-only trigger for concept2cure_artifact_versions is in db/migrations/20260318_ga_immutability_hardening.sql. A grep finds no applier referencing that file at HEAD, so whether it is installed in a deployed DB is unverified.
(5) A command I ran confirms the binding. A tsx probe (scratchpad reverify/cat2-digest-probe.ts) shows the digest is a pure function of the row: artifact bytes are not an input.
findings.fixedBy: MR-12 Stage 3 bound-content half (2026-10-29): re-confirmed at head that the controlled text is never the artifact (approval signs authored sections or metadata.sections, both in the digest, and refuses a row with neither: QMS_CONTENT_REQUIRED); no qms_documents writer sets artifact_id; nothing serves the artifact as the document's text. The open point, concept2cure_artifact_versions on no applier, is closed by migrations/20261029k_artifact_versions_no_rewrite.sql (UPDATE and TRUNCATE refused; boot-required). No digest v2: the artifact is not the signed text (docs/evidence/MR-12/2026-10-29-artifact-versions-no-rewrite/)
findings.remaining:
- Bind the artifact version and the sha256 of its bytes into the signed digest.
- Serve or lock the bound version so that later edits do not change the controlled text.
- Validate artifact_id as same-tenant on create and PATCH.
- Make sure the artifact_versions append-only trigger is on an applier.
findings.severityRationale: Once an artifact is linked, the controlled text of an approved SOP can change with no new signature, which breaks the Part 11 §11.70 binding. The UI has no way to link an artifact today (REST only, editor role), so exposure is limited. It must still be closed before pilot users keep SOP content in linked artifacts.
findings.humanTestingNote: Testers cannot observe this. The Quality UI has no field to link an artifact and no view of the document body, so testers never reach the mutable-content case.
findings.instructions:
1. Work on concept2cure-v2: `git pull --ff-only`, merge and never rebase.
2. Failing tests first:
   (a) In server/services/qms/__tests__/document-approval-signature.test.ts: two rows identical except for the bound artifact content sha256 must give different v2 digests.
   (b) A DB-tier test in tests/db/: approve a document with artifact_id set, write a new artifact version through artifactVersionStore, then assert that GET /api/mdx/qms/documents/:id reports artifact_drift=true and still serves the bound version's content.
   (c) Approving with an artifact_id from another organization, or a missing one, → 409 QMS_ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND with nothing signed.
   All three must be red at 94b4f9238.
3. In approveQmsDocumentSigned (document-approval-signature.ts:316-327) and retireQmsDocumentSigned (:478-488), when row.artifact_id != null:
   - Read the head with `SELECT id, version, content FROM concept2cure_artifacts WHERE id=$1 AND organization_id=$2 FOR SHARE`. If no row, throw QmsApprovalRefusedError (new code 'ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND', mapped to 409 in approvalRefusal at mdx-qms.ts:596-600).
   - Compute sha256 of the content in the server; do not trust the content_hash column.
   - Read the concept2cure_artifact_versions row (artifact_id, version) and refuse if its content hash differs.
4. Add artifactVersion and artifactContentSha256 to the v2 digest recipe. This is the same bump as CAT2-19: binding basis 'qms-document-version-content-sha256/v2', with v1 kept for verifying old signatures. Also:
   - record both in metadata.approval and extraManifest (:371);
   - record them in the CAT2-18 snapshot (artifact_version, artifact_content_sha256);
   - update the binding note (:368-370) and tests/validation/lib/qms-digest.mjs.
5. Serve the controlled text of an effective version only from concept2cure_artifact_versions at the bound version. GET /qms/documents/:id and /versions return artifact_drift when the head's sha256 differs from the bound sha256.
6. Validate artifact_id on POST /qms/documents (mdx-qms.ts:361-399) and PATCH (:448-510) with `SELECT 1 FROM concept2cure_artifacts WHERE id=$1 AND organization_id=$2`; otherwise return 422.
7. Put the concept2cure_artifact_versions append-only trigger on an applier. Write a new additive file that uses CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION and creates the trigger only if pg_trigger lacks it, insert it into C2C_MIGRATION_FILES in scripts/db/migration-set.mjs before UUID_TENANT_ISOLATION_NONPUBLIC, and prove it with a dbtest where UPDATE of a version row is refused.
8. Go green. Show the gate failing: drop artifactContentSha256 from the recipe and confirm test (a) fails, then revert. File the evidence under docs/evidence/.
findings.acceptance:
- Tests (a), (b) and (c) are red at 94b4f9238 and green after the change.
- The stored electronic_signatures.bound_payload_digest recomputes from the snapshot plus the bound artifact version's bytes. Changing one byte of that version's content makes the recompute differ.
- A later AnA edit of the artifact leaves the effective version's served text unchanged and sets artifact_drift=true.
- A foreign or missing artifact_id: 422 on create or PATCH, 409 on approve, nothing written.
- UPDATE of a concept2cure_artifact_versions row as app_service is refused.
findings.dependencies:
- CAT2-19: share the single digest v2 bump.
- CAT2-18: the snapshot table stores the bound artifact version.
- CAT2-26: no UI to link content yet, which limits exposure but does not fix this.

findings.title: Read-and-understood training: the any-user /api/qms write is gone; acknowledgments are still version-blind, accepted on non-effective documents, unassigned, unsigned, and have no UI
findings.evidenceAtHead:
Fixed:
- server/routes/qms.ts and server/services/qms/qms.service.ts no longer exist (ls: no such file). c6f2028b2 deleted them and removed the mount in server/bootstrap/register-document-routes.ts.
- At 92ccdba1, `git show 92ccdba1:server/routes/qms.ts` :106-121 took `b.userId` from the body and wrote no audit row. That path is closed.

Refuted at audit time (AnA ack_training):
- The handler is still at server/services/ana/AnaToolExecutor.ts:14369-14404, but it is unreachable.
- server/services/ana/tool-authorization.register.json:4-13 classes it 'refuse'.
- preHandlerRefusal returns NOT_AN_ANA_ACTION before any handler runs (AnaToolExecutor.ts:513-516). It is wired into every handler by registerToolHandler (:565-575).
- The same 'refuse' entry exists at 92ccdba1 (`git show 92ccdba1:server/services/ana/tool-authorization.register.json`), so a model could not create training evidence even then.

Still open:
(1) Compliance counts acknowledgments of any version. The acks CTE at server/routes/mdx-qms.ts:838-845 groups by document_id only, with no document_version filter. Revise keeps the same document_id, so v1.0 acks count toward v2.0.
(2) training-ack (:757-792) checks only tenant and existence (:766-770). It accepts draft, in_review and retired documents. It also takes a client-chosen `method`, including 'electronic_signature' with no ceremony, and a client `quizScore` (:771-772).
(3) The denominator is the whole org roster (:835-837). No assignment table exists.
(4) There is no client caller of /training-ack: grep in client/src finds only the compliance read in hooks.ts:127. The 'Record training' button (SopRegister.tsx:543-555) hands off to AnA, which refuses ack_training.
findings.fixedBy: c6f2028b2. It deleted server/routes/qms.ts and server/services/qms/qms.service.ts and removed the /api/qms mount, pinned by server/routes/__tests__/qms-legacy-api-retired.test.ts. The AnA ack_training sub-point was already neutralised at 92ccdba1 by tool-authorization.register.json 'refuse' plus AnaToolExecutor.ts preHandlerRefusal :513-516.
findings.remaining:

- Refuse acknowledgments unless the document is effective and of a trainable type.

findings.humanTestingNote: Clicking 'Record training' in Quality opens AnA. AnA refuses (NOT_AN_ANA_ACTION) and tells the user to record it on the document's training record, but no such control exists, so a tester cannot complete the read-and-understood journey in the UI. Compliance bars show N of the whole org roster. After a revision is approved, v1.0 acknowledgments still count. Workaround for testing only: each tester sends POST /api/mdx/qms/documents/<id>/training-ack (body {}) from devtools against an approved document. Do not trust the resulting percentages.
findings.instructions:
1. Work on concept2cure-v2: `git pull --ff-only`, merge and never rebase.
2. Failing tests first, in a new server/routes/__tests__/qms-training-ack.test.ts (pattern: qms-governed-writes-audited.test.ts):
   (a) ack on draft, in_review or retired → 409 QMS_NOT_TRAINABLE with nothing written;
   (b) ack without password → 400 ESIGNATURE_COMPONENT_MISSING;
   (c) a quizScore or method in the body is refused with 422 under zod .strict();
   (d) compliance: v1.0 acks exist, then revise and approve v2.0 → current = 0 for that document;
   (e) the denominator equals the assigned users, not organization_users.
   All must be red at 94b4f9238.
3. training-ack (mdx-qms.ts:757-792):
   - Read version, status and doc_type, and refuse unless the document is in force (status 'effective', or the CAT2-18 snapshot in force) and doc_type is in the trainable list (:854).
   - Make it a signed act by the trainee: parse {password, mfaToken?, meaning:'RESPONSIBILITY', reason?} and run reverifySigner. Do not run checkSigningAuthority, because any member signs their own training.
   - In one transaction, write the qms_training_records INSERT with acknowledgment_method fixed to 'electronic_signature' and quiz_score NULL, recordGovernedAction (command 'sign', target 'qms-document:<id>'), and persistGovernedActionSignature (signatureType 'qms-training-acknowledgment', binding = the in-force version's content digest).
   - Add a manifest statement that the signer has read and understood v<version>.
4. Compliance (:826-860): count `COUNT(DISTINCT t.user_id) FILTER (WHERE t.document_version = <in-force version> AND (t.expires_at IS NULL OR t.expires_at > NOW()))`. Join the acks on (document_id, document_version) against the in-force version from CAT2-18 (or d.version until CAT2-18 lands). Fix the comments at :826-829 and in client/src/concept2cure/quality/hooks.ts:124-126.
5. Assignment. The founder chooses the role or curriculum model first. Then:

   - Add an assignments control for editors.
7. Delete the dead AnA path, naming the replacement by path in the commit (CLAUDE.md working agreement):

   - Run the registry-parity and ana-launch-scope tests.
8. Go green. Show the gate failing: remove the document_version filter and confirm test (d) fails, then revert. File the evidence under docs/evidence/.
findings.acceptance:

recheck.testerNote:
The read-and-understood journey completes in the UI only if document access is granted before approval. You need three accounts. seed-admin creates only the admin. Use Admin and access to add an editor (member or manager) and a reader (viewer). With no SMTP configured, the admin is shown a setup link to hand over.

Steps:
(0) Make sure a program exists in Projects. 'New controlled document' requires one.
(1) As the editor, go to Quality and use 'New controlled document' (SOP, WI or policy). Choose the program, give a reason, then click 'Create and open'. Type real text into the sections in the document workbench and save. 'Edit controlled text' does not appear on these documents; it applies only to legacy unbound register rows.
(2) Before review, open 'Access' in the workbench and grant the reader the Viewer document role, with a reason. If the approver is not an org admin, also grant them Approver. Once a revision is approved, its access is sealed and nobody can add grants, not even an admin.
(3) Back in the register, click 'Send for review' and give a reason.
(4) As an org admin who is not the author, or as an approver- or reviewer-role user holding the Approver grant, click Approve and sign with your password. On the docker-compose production stacks, the signer must first enrol an authenticator in Account and enter its code.
(5) As the reader, click 'Read and acknowledge' on the register row or 'My acknowledgement' on the coverage row. Read the text, tick 'I have read and understood this released revision.' and click 'Acknowledge this revision'. The receipt shows, and coverage moves for that exact version only.

Known issues:
- A member or viewer with no grant on the document gets 'You do not have permission to read this authored document' and cannot acknowledge. Coverage still counts them in 'N of the active organization roster'.
- Revise creates a new authored copy that only the reviser can access. Re-grant readers before approving v2. Acknowledgements of v1 stop counting once v2 is approved.
- The act is a personal attestation, not an e-signature.
- Asking AnA to record training returns a redirect to this reader.

Still open: the legal entity name and jurisdiction; counsel review and sign-off; the SCC module selection and UK Addendum (DPA Annex IV), or a counsel statement that a US-only FDA pilot has no restricted transfer; the named SMTP and uptime subprocessors; insurance actually held; governing law, venue and notice addresses; and removing the DRAFT banners. findings.severityRationale: A paid pilot cannot start lawfully without a signed pilot agreement and DPA. Every template in the repo is a self-declared non-binding draft that does not name the contracting entity. The defect is legal and commercial, not code, but nothing else in the catalog matters commercially until it closes.
findings.instructions:
1. Founder decides the contracting entity: exact legal name, entity type, jurisdiction and registered address. Replace '[CONCEPT2CURE LEGAL ENTITY NAME]' and the adjacent '[STATE/COUNTRY] [entity type] ... [ADDRESS]' in docs/commercial/MASTER_SUBSCRIPTION_AGREEMENT.md:14, DATA_PROCESSING_ADDENDUM.md:16, PILOT_AGREEMENT.md:16-17, ORDER_FORM.md:16 and PARTNER_HUB_APPLICATION.md:21. If the name is not 'Concept2Cure, Inc.', the product copy at client/src/concept2cure/auth/ZenSignup.tsx:778,854 must change too; GTM-02 removes that inline text anyway.
2. Name the transactional-mail and uptime subprocessors in DPA Annex III (:268-269), with region and DPA reference. Use the mailer chosen under GTM-05 (one mailer). If Sentry session replay stays enabled (client/src/utils/sentry.ts), disclose it in the Sentry row (GTM-16).
3. Counsel completes DPA Annex IV (:275-279): SCC module, Annex I.A/I.B/I.C, supervisory authority and the UK Addendum tables. Alternatively, counsel states in the annex that the pilot processes data only in us-east-1 with no restricted transfer, and that the annex applies only if one occurs.
4. Fill insurance in MSA §18 (:361-364) and Pilot §14 (:350-353) with coverage actually bound (technology E&O and cyber, with limits). If none is bound, counsel decides whether to delete the section. Never state coverage that is not held.
5. Fill governing law, venue and notice addresses (MSA:368-370; Pilot:376-390) and resolve every '[Counsel: …]' note (DPA:142,189; Pilot:255,317,352,378).
6. Counsel reviews the Pilot Agreement, DPA, Order Form and Support Policy. After sign-off, replace the 'DRAFT — FOR LAWYER REVIEW' banner on each with a version line ('v1.0, approved by <counsel> on <date>'), and record the approval outside docs/evidence (a signed PDF in the company records) so that it is not only a repo claim.

It fails if PILOT_AGREEMENT.md, DATA_PROCESSING_ADDENDUM.md, MASTER_SUBSCRIPTION_AGREEMENT.md or ORDER_FORM.md contain 'DRAFT — FOR' or any '[' placeholder outside an allowlist of deal fields ([DATE], [CUSTOMER LEGAL NAME], [CUSTOMER], [C2C-OF-YYYY-NNN], [NAME, TITLE, EMAIL], [90]). Run it at HEAD first and show it failing on the entity placeholder, then wire it into package.json as a non-blocking report until step 6 is done.

(c) The entity name in the templates matches any entity name shown in the product. (d) The company holds a counsel sign-off and a pilot agreement plus DPA executed by both parties. (1) POST /api/auth/signup without acceptedAgreements returns 400 TERMS_NOT_ACCEPTED and writes no users, organizations or organization_users row. At HEAD the field is silently ignored and the account is created.
(2) A successful signup writes exactly one append-only license_acceptances row per required agreement with acceptance_hash, ip_address and user_agent, plus a chained audit row, in the signup transaction. An injected acceptance failure rolls back the whole signup.
(3) GET /concept2cure/legal/terms, /privacy and /aup render the counsel-approved text with its version and do not redirect to /concept2cure.

(6) license_agreements and license_acceptances are created by a file in C2C_MIGRATION_FILES, and eula-service.ts contains no CREATE TABLE.

findings.title: Full tenant export is still database rows only, with no stored document files; purge accepts its receipt and then deletes the tenant's vault objects
findings.evidenceAtHead:
The export service has no file path:
- server/services/tenant-export/tenant-full-export.service.ts (516 lines at HEAD) discovers tables in the 'public' and 'vault' schemas (:71) and exports rows only. It never imports a storage provider and never reads object bytes. Its only sha256 is digestOf over the canonical JSON of rows (:294-296).
- recordExportReceipt (:436-491) stores digest, table_count and row_count only. The receipts table (migrations/20260813b_tenant_export_receipts.sql) has no file columns.
The route is still synchronous JSON:
- GET /api/tenant-export/full (server/routes/tenant-export.ts:172-238) builds the payload in-request and sends one JSON body.
The purge still trusts that receipt and then erases files:
- assertPurgePermitted (server/services/tenant/tenant-offboarding.ts:294-352) accepts any receipt matching the digest.
- purgeTenant (:807-870) then collects storage_version_id/storage_provider from public.purge_tenant_vault_records (:505-529; migrations/20260926_vault_documents_record_immutability.sql:195-237).
- It deletes each object through eraseStoredObjects → getStorageProviderFor(provider).delete (:622-633, :845).
There is no UI for it: no client code calls /api/tenant-export/full. The only client caller of tenant-export is the attestation (ComplianceAttestation.tsx).
The changes since the audit (66b5bb282 withholds credentials from the export; a3fbd6ff3, 7cbea4130, 2ab30c93e and c59ebc813 widen what the purge erases; 6a54db14c classifies columns) do not add files to the export or to the receipt.
findings.remaining:
All of it:
- The export must include every stored object (vault uploads, rendered eCTD leaf files at server/services/ectd/rendered-leaf-files.ts:97, module attachments at server/routes/moduleIntegrationRoutes.ts:465) with a per-file SHA-256 manifest.
- It must run as an async job that survives large tenants and is delivered through a pre-signed link.
- The receipt must attest file coverage, and the purge must refuse a rows-only receipt.
- Org admins need an 'Export all data' control.
findings.severityRationale: The pilot can start, and offboarding is platform-admin-only and founder-run, so it is not P0. But the first pilot that ends, or a customer exercising its data-return right, can today be purged against a receipt that never contained the customer's uploaded Vault documents. That irreversibly destroys customer files in breach of the data-return clauses. It must be fixed before pilot data is relied on in production.
findings.humanTestingNote: The six launch apps do not reach it, and org admins have no export button. If a tester is given offboarding to test via the API, GET /api/tenant-export/full downloads a single JSON file with database rows only. Uploaded Vault files are missing, yet its digest still authorises a purge. Do not run a purge on any tenant whose files matter.
findings.acceptance:
(1) Failing first at HEAD: a DB-tier test that seeds a tenant with Vault objects, takes the digest from GET /api/tenant-export/full and calls purgeTenant expects a refusal (EXPORT_MISSING_FILES). At HEAD the purge succeeds and deletes the objects. After the fix, it is refused.
(2) The archive job's ZIP contains every stored object for the org, and manifest.json lists each one with a sha256 that matches its bytes. An org with N stored objects yields file_count = N.
(3) If any object cannot be read, the job ends 'failed' with a message and writes no receipt.
(4) Purge succeeds only with a covers_files = true receipt whose file_count is at least the org's stored-object count at purge time.
(5) An org admin can start the export from the UI and download it through a pre-signed link that expires.
(6) A tenant of about 1 GB exports on staging with no request timeout.
findings.dependencies: An S3 export prefix or bucket with KMS in the production Terraform stack. GTM-01: the data-return clause wording should cite the archive format and the link expiry once built.

recheck.testerNote:
Unchanged since 94b4f9238.

Local (NODE_ENV=development): what happens depends on your .env.
- With ALLOW_DEV_AUTH=1, which scripts/setup-local-db.sh writes, password sign-in skips the code entirely.
- Otherwise, with SMTP unset, the code appears only as a debug-level JSON log line ("[email-service] Dev OTP code", field "code"). That line is hidden when LOG_LEVEL=info, which is what .env.example sets. If your .env was copied from .env.example, set LOG_LEVEL=debug or ALLOW_DEV_AUTH=1. Otherwise you will wait on the code screen.
- If you do set SMTP locally, the code is emailed instead of logged. With SMTP_FROM left blank, it comes from noreply@concept2cure.pro.

Docker-compose stacks: both refuse to start unless SMTP_HOST, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASS and SMTP_FROM are set (docker-compose.yml:219-223, docker-compose.beta.yml:221-225), so the .pro default never applies there. They only check that the values are present, not that they work.
- The send is not awaited. A wrong host, port or password, a sender address your provider will not send from (for example an unverified SES identity), or an SES-sandbox recipient fails after the screen has already said the code was sent. Resend says the same.
- The only trace is "Failed to send login OTP email" in the server log.
- If SMTP works but the sender domain has no SPF, DKIM or DMARC, the code can go to spam or be quarantined.

Workaround:
- Use a sender address on a domain verified with your SMTP provider.
- Before the session, run `node scripts/ops/verify-otp-delivery.mjs <inbox>` once per tester inbox, from the repo root with the same .env the stack uses.
- Testers should check spam. Personal Gmail is more forgiving than corporate M365 gateways.

findings.title: Public self-serve signup is still always on: no kill switch or domain allowlist, column-default limits instead of the free plan, and no AI cost cap
findings.evidenceAtHead: `grep -rnE 'SELF_SERVE_SIGNUP|SIGNUP_ENABLED|PUBLIC_SIGNUP|SIGNUP_MODE|ALLOW_SIGNUP|signupEnabled|SIGNUP_DOMAIN|INVITE_ONLY|inviteOnly|DISABLE_SIGNUP' server client/src shared terraform docker-compose*.yml .env.example` finds nothing. server/routes/auth.ts:887 `router.post('/signup', signupLimiter, …)` is open to anyone. The only refusals are no SMTP or no public origin in production (:928-955), the tenant-isolation admission check (assertCanAdmitNewTenant at about :1007, which needs RLS_ENFORCE=on from the second org onward but does not restrict who may sign up), and a duplicate email. auth.ts:1018 inserts the org with only `tier: 'free'`, so the column defaults apply (shared/schema.ts:172-179: seats_purchased 5, max_users 5, max_projects 10, max_storage 5 GB) instead of the published free plan in server/services/billing.ts:104-117 DTC_PRICING (maxUsers 1, maxProjects 2, maxStorageGB 1). provisionLaunchModules then grants the whole launch catalog (auth.ts about :1090-1100). server/services/tenant/tenant-lifecycle.ts:110-118 lists 'incomplete' and 'incomplete_expired' among the allowed payment statuses, with no time limit. AI spend: server/bootstrap/register-ai-routes.ts:19-24 says weekly limits are 'Strictly opt-in per org — with no configured limit the check is a no-op — and fail-open'. Only the 'requests' metric is wired (enforceWeeklyLimit('requests') on /api/ana, /api/ana-ri and /api/chat; public-api.ts:398), and the cost_cents metric (weekly-usage-limits.ts:37) is enforced nowhere. server/services/ai-gateway/policy.ts:420-428 checks only per-request maxTokens. Client: client/src/concept2cure/router/ZenRouter.tsx:210-214 serves /concept2cure/signup, and :230 redirects /signup to it. No commit since 92ccdba1 touches any of this, and no candidate fix exists in `git log 92ccdba1..HEAD --grep`.
findings.remaining: 1) There is no way to switch public signup off or limit it to invited orgs or allowlisted domains in production. 2) Self-serve orgs get schema-default limits (5 seats, 5 users, 10 projects, 5 GB) and the full launch catalog instead of the free plan's 1 user, 2 projects and 1 GB. 3) No default AI cost cap is provisioned at org creation, and cost_cents is not enforced on any route or at the gateway. 4) A free or incomplete org is allowed indefinitely. Terms acceptance at signup is tracked separately (GTM-02).
findings.severityRationale: The pilot is sales-led on one production AWS environment. While /api/auth/signup stays open, anyone who finds the URL can create a tenant, get the whole launch catalog, upload data under unrecorded terms (GTM-02) and spend model budget without limit. HEAD has mitigations: production signup requires email verification (auth.ts:928-955), a rate limiter, and RLS_ENFORCE=on before a second org can exist. They limit abuse but give no way to close the door, so this must be fixed before pilot users rely on production. Not P0, because it does not break a launch journey or expose another tenant's data.
findings.humanTestingNote: Testers will not see this as a defect. Signup works where SMTP and a public origin are configured. A self-signed-up org shows 5 seats and allows 10 projects rather than the published free plan's 1 user and 2 projects, which only shows if someone compares it with the pricing copy. Note for test setup on a deployed environment: a second self-serve org is refused unless RLS_ENFORCE=on (tenant admission). Create tester orgs through the platform-admin path (POST /api/tenants, server/routes/tenants-simple.ts:160) or invite testers into one org.
findings.instructions: 1. Founder: confirm whether self-serve is in scope at launch (an audit open question) and set the free-plan AI cost cap (GTM-12). The defaults below work without that decision: off in production, and a conservative cost_cents cap. 2. In server/config (the module that already exports config.billing; add a typed field there), add selfServeSignup: 'off' | 'allowlist' | 'open', read from SELF_SERVE_SIGNUP. It defaults to 'off' when NODE_ENV==='production' and to 'open' otherwise, and an unknown value is treated as 'off'. Also add signupAllowedDomains from SIGNUP_ALLOWED_DOMAINS (comma-separated, lowercased). 3. In server/routes/auth.ts POST /signup (:887), straight after signupSchema.safeParse and before password policy or any DB call, return 403 {success:false, error:{code:'AUTH_SIGNUP_CLOSED', message:'Sign-up is by invitation. Ask your organisation administrator for an invitation.'}} when the mode is 'off', or when it is 'allowlist' and the email's domain is not in signupAllowedDomains. Log one info line without the email address. Invited users are not affected: invitations go through password-setup tokens and POST /api/tenant-users/invitations/:invitationId/accept (server/routes/tenant-users.ts:202), not /signup (see the emailService.ts:425-435 note). Sales-led tenants are created through POST /api/tenants (server/routes/tenants-simple.ts:160, requirePlatformAdmin). 4. Add GET /api/auth/signup-availability, public and data-free, returning {mode:'off'|'allowlist'|'open'}. In client/src/concept2cure/auth/ZenSignup.tsx, call it on mount and render an honest 'Sign-up is by invitation' state with a link back to login when the mode is 'off'. Also handle AUTH_SIGNUP_CLOSED from the POST. Hide any 'Create account' link on the login page when the mode is 'off'. Keep the /concept2cure/signup route (ZenRouter.tsx:210-214) so no capability is deleted. 5. Terraform: add variable self_serve_signup (default "off", validation on the three values) and signup_allowed_domains (default "") to terraform/stack/variables.tf, and render them in the env list in terraform/stack/main.tf next to SMTP_FROM (about :288). Add them to docker-compose.yml and docker-compose.beta.yml. 6. Apply plan limits at creation. Next to DTC_PRICING in server/services/billing.ts:104, export limitsForTier(tier), which returns {seatsPurchased, maxUsers, maxProjects, maxStorage} from that table. Use it in the signup insert at auth.ts:1018 (`.values({ …, tier: 'free', ...limitsForTier('free') })`) and in the org insert in server/routes/tenants-simple.ts POST / (honouring an explicit platform-admin override). Do NOT change the shared/schema.ts:172-179 column defaults. If the defaults must change, amend the migration that creates them in place, with a dated header note (CLAUDE.md Rule 1). 7. Default AI cost cap: inside the runWithTenantScope block after provisionLaunchModules (auth.ts about :1090-1100), call setWeeklyLimit(result.org.id, {metric:'cost_cents', weeklyLimit:<free cap>, overageCapPct:0, overageHardCap:null, warnThresholdPct:80, weekStartDow:1, enabled:true}, {userId: result.user.id}, 'Plan default at provisioning: free') from server/services/weekly-usage-limits.ts:278. Do the same in tenants-simple.ts with the plan the operator picks. 8. Enforce cost at the single choke point: in server/services/ai-gateway/gateway.ts, just before or after this.policyEngine.evaluate(request) (:1418) and before the provider call, call checkWeeklyLimit(orgId, 'cost_cents', 0). If decision.allowed===false, refuse with a typed USAGE_LIMIT_REACHED error that routes map to 429, and audit the refusal. This covers every AI route, not only /api/ana, /api/ana-ri and /api/chat. Keep the existing fail-open behaviour on a metering outage, but raise reportSecurityAlert so it is visible. 9. Verify every gate by making it fail first: write the tests in Acceptance against HEAD, show them failing, then implement. Work on concept2cure-v2 only and merge, never rebase.

findings.title: RLS kill-switch still honoured for the runtime role (rls_enforce / app_super_admin / bypass_rls / is_admin); only the pooled-connection carry-over is closed
findings.evidenceAtHead: Unchanged policy shape: db/migrations/20260801_tenant_isolation_sweep.sql:184-198 (final sweep in C2C_MIGRATION_FILES) and migrations/0021_enable_rls_everywhere.sql:190-220 still lead USING/WITH CHECK with `NULLIF(current_setting('app.rls_enforce', TRUE), '') IS DISTINCT FROM 'on'` and end with `OR current_setting('app.current_user_role', TRUE) = 'app_super_admin'`. server/db/rlsEnforcement.ts has no commits in 92ccdba1..HEAD. identity.can_* still return TRUE on `app.bypass_rls='true'` (db/migrations/069_gcc_multitenant_rls_expansion.sql:95,128,167,222). No role default: grep for `ALTER ROLE ... SET app.rls_enforce` over *.sql/*.mjs/*.ts/*.tf returns nothing; scripts/db/provision-app-role.mjs sets none. Mitigation added after the audit: ac688076e (2026-10-08) server/db/sessionScope.ts:39-82 pins app.rls_enforce to the deployment mode and empties app.bypass_rls/app.is_admin whenever a scope is applied, and clears them on release; scripts/ci/check-session-scoped-rls-bypass.mjs:150-185 counts every server write of the three switches against an allowlist (wired .husky/pre-push:340, .github/workflows/ci.yml:571). sessionScope.ts:20-23 records that the policies 'are not a boundary against injected SQL'. Seven innovation services still issue session-level `SET app.bypass_rls='true'`/`SET app.is_admin='true'` (baseline at check-session-scoped-rls-bypass.mjs:57-65), e.g. server/services/innovation/submission-readiness-twin-service.ts:483-484, reachable from AnA tools (server/services/ana/AnaToolExecutor.ts) and cleared on release by server/services/innovation/rlsBypassSession.ts.
findings.fixedBy: ac688076e: server/db/sessionScope.ts:39-82 (switch pins on apply, clear on release; used by establishRequestTenantScope, lazyRequestDbClient, withTenantConnection, poolInstrumentation) and scripts/ci/check-session-scoped-rls-bypass.mjs:150-185 (writer allowlist). Closes only the 'setting left on a pooled connection' vector.
findings.remaining: Any app_service session that can run its own SQL (injection, psql/script, a second driver that omits the startup options) can still `SET app.rls_enforce='off'`, `SET app.current_user_role='app_super_admin'`, or `SET app.bypass_rls='true'` and read every tenant. There is no role-level default of app.rls_enforce=on, nothing in the database stops production enforcement from being switched off, and no DB test proves the switches are inert for app_service. The 'hard isolation at the database' claim to GxP buyers still does not hold; the code now says so explicitly.
findings.severityRationale: The pilot has one customer tenant, and the primary isolation is at the app layer (global /api auth gate plus JWT-derived org scope). After D3 a switch set in one request cannot reach the next, and every server write of a switch is CI-gated. What remains is defence-in-depth against injected SQL or a new connection path. That is needed before enterprise GA, or before more than a handful of tenants share the cluster, but it does not stop a sales-led single-tenant pilot.
findings.humanTestingNote: Not observable through the UI; testers see correct tenant scoping in normal use.
findings.instructions:
1. Role default for paths that skip the startup packet. In scripts/db/provision-app-role.mjs (the grant recipe deploy-migrate runs), when RLS_ENFORCE resolves to 'on' (same rules as server/db/rlsEnforcement.ts readEnforcementMode), execute `ALTER ROLE <quote_ident(appRole)> IN DATABASE <current_database()> SET app.rls_enforce = 'on'`; when it resolves to off, `ALTER ROLE ... IN DATABASE ... RESET app.rls_enforce`. Extend the existing grant audit in that file to read pg_db_role_setting and fail deploy-migrate in production when the setting is absent.
2. Make production enforcement non-switchable by a session. Add `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.c2c_rls_floor() RETURNS boolean LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE AS 'SELECT <true|false>'`, owned by the owner role. deploy-migrate writes the body from RLS_ENFORCE (true in production). It must run before any policy that references it: add it at the top of the first set file, and to install-fresh before the overlay. app_service has CREATE on no schema, so it cannot replace the function. Change the leading clause of every tenant policy to `(NOT public.c2c_rls_floor() AND NULLIF(current_setting('app.rls_enforce', TRUE), '') IS DISTINCT FROM 'on')`. CLAUDE.md Rule 1 applies: amend the creators in place, each with a dated header note naming this change. Start with db/migrations/20260801_tenant_isolation_sweep.sql:184-198, db/migrations/20260801_uuid_tenant_isolation_nonpublic.sql, db/migrations/20260813_child_table_parent_scoped_rls.sql and migrations/0021_enable_rls_everywhere.sql:190-220, then every other file on an applier returned by `grep -rl "IS DISTINCT FROM 'on'" migrations db/migrations`. The sweeps DROP POLICY IF EXISTS and re-create on every deploy, so the change converges.
3. Do not let the runtime role grant itself cross-tenant reach (GA scope). Replace the `app.current_user_role='app_super_admin'` clause and the `app.bypass_rls`/`app.is_admin` short-circuits (069_gcc_multitenant_rls_expansion.sql:95-222) with `pg_has_role(current_user, 'c2c_platform', 'MEMBER')`. Create c2c_platform as a NOLOGIN role and grant it to a separate LOGIN role used only by the system-scope pool. That pool serves server/middleware/establishRequestTenantScope.ts:185, server/services/memory-consolidation-job.ts:110, server/services/audit/tenant-chain-verdict.ts:80 and server/services/audit/compliance-reports/integrity-checks.ts:38. app_service must not be a member.
4. Convert the seven session-level bypass writers in BASELINE (scripts/ci/check-session-scoped-rls-bypass.mjs:57-65) to SET LOCAL inside an explicit transaction, or remove them. They are outside the launch catalog (CLAUDE.md Rule 2), but submission-readiness-twin-service.ts is reachable from AnA tools, so removing it needs the replacement named by path (working agreement). Lower the baseline to lock each one in.
5. Add tests/db/rls-switches-inert.dbtest.ts. Seed two tenants' rows in one FORCE-RLS public table and in vault.documents. As app_service with tenant A scoped and the production floor, assert that each of SET app.rls_enforce='off', SET app.current_user_role='app_super_admin', SET app.bypass_rls='true' and SET app.is_admin='true' still returns only tenant A's rows. Also assert that a connection opened without startup options returns 0 rows with no scope. Run it against HEAD first and file the red output (2 of 2 rows), then make it green.
findings.acceptance: 1) On a production-provisioned DB, `psql` as app_service with no PGOPTIONS shows current_setting('app.rls_enforce')='on', and an unscoped SELECT on a tenant table returns 0 rows (red at HEAD: all rows). 2) With tenant A scoped, each of the four switch SETs returns 1 of 2 rows on the generic table and 0 tenant-B rows on vault.documents (red at HEAD: 2 of 2 / 1 extra). 3) deploy-migrate exits non-zero in production when pg_db_role_setting lacks the default, shown by deleting it first. 4) The new dbtest runs in the ci.yml dbtest job, and its filed red/green output is attached. 5) The ci:session-scoped-rls-bypass BASELINE is empty, or each remaining entry is SET LOCAL in a transaction.

findings.title: API and worker tasks still receive the RDS owner DATABASE_URL; boot DDL and /api/tenants still run as the owner
findings.evidenceAtHead: terraform/stack/main.tf:95 composes database_url from module.rds.master_username. main.tf:315-317 puts DATABASE_URL (owner) and APP_DATABASE_URL into boot_secrets, which api_secrets (main.tf:431) and worker_secrets (main.tf:440) both use. main.tf:43-47 documents it as 'A known exposure'. .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml:74-79 and 756-787 derive the migrate task from the API task definition, so the API task must carry DATABASE_URL; the preflight at deploy-aws.yml:514 requires DATABASE_URL in the API container. server/startup/env.ts:66-68 requires DATABASE_URL at boot. server/routes/tenants-simple.ts:67-75 still builds a postgres.js client on process.env.DATABASE_URL, mounted at /api/tenants (server/bootstrap/register-tenant-routes.ts:51). Its 12 queries run as the owner with no tenant GUCs, outside RLS. Commits since the audit (78d316062, 2ab30c93e, 06152498b, 1596454a9) changed authorization and purge only, not the connection. Boot DDL as the owner: server/startup/services.ts:129-131 calls ensureCoreTables(process.env.DATABASE_URL), whose auto-create runs CREATE TABLE (server/db/ensureCoreTables.ts:458-583) with no production guard. server/db/bootstrap/index.ts:30-44 opens an owner pool for ensureAuthTables (schema migrations, org and demo seeds, module catalog DDL). The boot posture probe (server/db/rlsEnforcement.ts:186-300) checks only the runtime pool's role.
findings.remaining: All of it. DATABASE_URL must be removed from the API and worker tasks, with a separate migrate task definition. Boot DDL and seeds must move into deploy-migrate. tenants-simple must move onto the app pool under a system or platform scope. A boot assertion must refuse an owner URL in production.
findings.severityRationale: Requests are served by app_service (NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS) and the posture probe holds, so tenant isolation works in normal operation and the pilot can start. Any API compromise (RCE, env or log leak), however, yields the RDS master. With it an attacker can run DDL, read every non-FORCE table, and DISABLE the Part 11 append-only triggers. /api/tenants already runs outside RLS. This must be closed before pilot users rely on production records.
findings.humanTestingNote: Not observable in testing. /api/tenants and boot behave normally; this is credential and infrastructure posture.
findings.instructions:
1. Write the failing check first. In terraform tests/boot_contract.tftest.hcl, add assertions that the api and worker container definitions contain no secret or env named DATABASE_URL. Run `terraform test` against the current terraform/stack/main.tf and file the red output.
2. terraform/stack/main.tf: split boot_secrets (lines 315-330) into runtime_secrets (no DATABASE_URL, no APP_SERVICE_DB_PASSWORD) and migrate_secrets (runtime_secrets plus DATABASE_URL and APP_SERVICE_DB_PASSWORD). Set api_secrets (line 431) to runtime_secrets plus SETUP_TOKEN, and worker_secrets (line 440) to runtime_secrets. Add a Terraform-managed migrate task definition (family c2c-production-migrate) with the same image variable, execution role, log config and migrate_secrets. Update the main.tf:35-60 comment.
3. .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml: in the migrate step (around lines 756-800), derive the one-off task from the migrate family instead of the API revision. Alternatively, extend scripts/ops/ecs-one-off-task.sh to accept an extra secrets list and inject the database_url secret ARN. Remove DATABASE_URL from the API preflight list (line 514), and add a preflight that fails when the API container definition contains DATABASE_URL. Apply the same change to provision-database.yml.
4. server/startup/env.ts:66-68: when NODE_ENV=production, require APP_DATABASE_URL and refuse boot if DATABASE_URL is set. Keep the dev fallback.
5. server/startup/services.ts:129-131: in production call ensureCoreTables() with no connection string, so it uses the runtime pool in verify-only mode. In server/db/ensureCoreTables.ts:458-590, skip autoCreateTables when NODE_ENV=production and report a missing table as a readiness failure. If `documents` still needs creating, put it in a C2C_MIGRATION_FILES file (IF NOT EXISTS, before the final sweep pair, per Rule 1).
6. server/db/bootstrap/index.ts:22-71: in production, open no owner pool. Move applyAuthSchemaMigrations, applyModuleCatalogSchema and seedOrganizations into deploy-migrate, as a set migration or a new deploy-migrate step that runs as the owner. Leave a read-only verification at boot. Do not seed the GA demo user in production.
7. server/routes/tenants-simple.ts:66-75: delete the postgres.js client and cleanDatabaseUrl. Use `pool` from '../db' (already imported at line 14). Run the platform-admin cross-tenant list and the purge, deletion and cancel paths under runWithSystemTenantScope, and member reads under the request scope. Confirm the organizations policy admits both.
8. Boot assertion: in server/db/rlsEnforcement.ts assessRlsCatalogPosture, add a failure when current_user owns any relation in a non-system schema. Add another when process.env.DATABASE_URL is set under NODE_ENV=production.
9. Have the founder or ops run `terraform apply` and a deploy. Then confirm the running API task definition has no DATABASE_URL.
findings.acceptance: 1) The tftest asserting no DATABASE_URL in the api/worker containers was red on the old main.tf and is green after. 2) The CI production boot smoke boots with APP_DATABASE_URL only and /readyz=200. Setting DATABASE_URL in production refuses boot, shown failing first. 3) An integration test of GET /api/tenants shows a platform admin gets every org, a member gets only their orgs, and `SELECT current_user` on the serving connection is app_service. 4) Booting against a DB where app_service has no CREATE logs no DDL and no 'Could not auto-create'. 5) The deploy-aws.yml preflight fails on an API task definition that contains DATABASE_URL. 6) After apply, `aws ecs describe-task-definition` for the API and worker shows no DATABASE_URL.
findings.dependencies: An AWS terraform apply and deploy by the founder or ops. Moving boot DDL into deploy-migrate overlaps DATA-05 and DATA-07 (migration set discipline).

findings.title: Authoring signatures and authoring audit trail are now append-only in the database; section-version history is still rewritable, and the new triggers are not checked at boot
findings.evidenceAtHead: Fixed after the audit. Commit 00f94ee9f (2026-10-01): migrations/20261001_domain_history_append_only.sql:166-181 adds BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE (row) and BEFORE TRUNCATE (statement) triggers on public.authoring_signatures, and on workflow_history, document_audit_logs, regulatory_audit_logs and c2c_ana_actions. The file is in the set at scripts/db/migration-set.mjs:2883. scripts/db/provision-app-role.mjs:199-250 lists authoring_signatures (line 244) and authoring_audit_trail (line 212) in APPEND_ONLY_TABLES, and withholdAppendOnlyPrivileges (lines 486-515) REVOKEs UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE from app_service on every deploy. Commit 7863cf830 (2026-09-29, after the audit) amended db/migrations/20260725_authoring_audit_trail.sql:69-110 with append-only and no-truncate triggers (AUTHORING_SUBSYSTEM_FILES). QMS controlled-document approvals write electronic_signatures (server/services/qms/document-approval-signature.ts:349), which is trigger-protected. I ran: clone of the audit-state DB c2c_cold_eval (92ccdba1) into a scratch DB. As app_service in tenant 9001, the audit's `UPDATE authoring_signatures SET signer_name='Someone Else', meaning='reviewed', signed_at=now()-'30 days'` gave UPDATE 1 and the DELETE gave DELETE 1 (red). After applying HEAD's 20261001 file and the HEAD revoke, both gave 'permission denied for table authoring_signatures'. As owner, the trigger raised 'IMMUTABILITY_VIOLATION: authoring_signatures is append-only ... UPDATE refused', and TRUNCATE was refused too (green). Scratch DB dropped. Still open, on the same DB: has_table_privilege(app_service, c2c_document_section_versions, UPDATE/DELETE) = t/t with 0 user triggers. At HEAD no file on any applier creates a trigger on c2c_document_section_versions (the only `ON` match is an index), and the table is not in APPEND_ONLY_TABLES. It is the section's 'Part-11 history' read by server/routes/c2c/documents.ts:411-431 and server/services/governance/separation-of-duties.ts:152, and it cascades from c2c_document_sections (migrations/20260528_phase9_document_schema.sql:127). server/services/audit/audit-immutability-triggers.ts:44-93, the boot, securityHealth and sweep check, does not list trg_authoring_signatures_* or the other 20261001 triggers. No CI gate enumerates signature, audit or history tables that lack a trigger. submission_leaves has no DB guard for frozen or dispatched sequences (service-level only). authoring_audit_events has no writer in server/ (dead).
findings.fixedBy: 00f94ee9f migrations/20261001_domain_history_append_only.sql:166-181 (authoring_signatures triggers); scripts/db/provision-app-role.mjs:212,244 and 486-515 (UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE withheld from app_service, DP-66); 7863cf830 db/migrations/20260725_authoring_audit_trail.sql:69-110 (authoring_audit_trail triggers)
findings.remaining: c2c_document_section_versions, the per-change section snapshot used as the Part 11 history on the AnA document/canvas Authoring path, is still UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE-able by app_service and has no trigger. trg_authoring_signatures_* and the other domain-history triggers are not in EXPECTED_AUDIT_IMMUTABILITY_TRIGGERS, so a disabled trigger would not fail boot or the sweep. There is no CI gate that catches the next unprotected signature, audit or history table. Frozen or dispatched submission_leaves are protected only in application code.
findings.severityRationale: The demonstrated P0 is closed at HEAD: Authoring e-signature rows can no longer be rewritten or deleted by the app role. The residual section-history gap is still a 21 CFR Part 11 §11.10(e) audit-trail weakness on a launch-catalog journey (Authoring). It must be closed before pilot users rely on those records, but it does not stop the pilot starting.

findings.instructions:
1. Write the failing test first. Extend tests/db/domain-history-append-only.dbtest.ts with a case that, as app_service in its own tenant, runs UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE on c2c_document_section_versions and expects each to be refused (42501 or IMMUTABILITY_VIOLATION). Run it at HEAD and file the red output.
2. Census before adding the trigger. grep confirms no server or script path UPDATEs or DELETEs c2c_document_section_versions, c2c_document_sections or c2c_documents. Check server/services/tenant/tenant-offboarding.ts PURGE_CHILD_TABLES (line 907) and the GDPR erasure path. If either must erase the history through the ON DELETE CASCADE from c2c_document_sections, add an owner-run door function as 06152498b did for turn records.
3. Add migrations/20261014_section_version_history_append_only.sql to C2C_MIGRATION_FILES right after 'migrations/20261001_domain_history_append_only.sql' (scripts/db/migration-set.mjs:2883) and before the final sweep pair. It reuses public.domain_history_append_only(), is guarded by to_regclass('public.c2c_document_section_versions'), and does DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS of its own names, then creates trg_c2c_document_section_versions_append_only (BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE, FOR EACH ROW) and trg_c2c_document_section_versions_no_truncate (BEFORE TRUNCATE, FOR EACH STATEMENT). Give the file a header with the census. It creates no table and drops nothing another file creates (Rule 1).

findings.severityRationale: A pilot production DB provisioned fresh from HEAD starts correct. The first release after go-live, though, can leave production on a schema that differs from what the code expects, with 500s or failed writes, while the deploy reports green and nothing detects it. That is a data-integrity and availability risk that must be closed before pilot users rely on production. The new deploy-path gate removes the most common cause but not the class.

2. Add an `upgrade-convergence` job to .github/workflows/ci.yml, using the same postgres16+pgvector service as the dbtest job at ci.yml:1501-1560. (a) Resolve BASE from a new file deploy/production-baseline.sha. deploy-aws.yml writes it after a successful production migrate; until then use the newest v* tag. (b) Run `git archive $BASE | tar -x -C "$RUNNER_TEMP/base"`, a read-only export with no branch or worktree (Rule 0). Run `npm ci` there and its `node scripts/db/provision.mjs` into db c2c_upgrade. (c) Run HEAD's `node scripts/db/deploy-migrate.mjs` against c2c_upgrade. (d) Run HEAD's `npm run db:provision` into c2c_fresh. (e) Diff the two fingerprints. Fail unless the diff is empty or every line is in scripts/ci/upgrade-convergence-baseline.json with a non-empty reason. Prove it red first with BASE=54927bde: it must list the assumption_records, decision_records, governance_boundary_* and cmc_comparability_assessments.tenant_id lines. 3. Add migrations/20261014_retired_shape_convergence.sql to C2C_MIGRATION_FILES, after the creators and before the final sweep pair; ci:migration-set-order must pass. If it has rows, RAISE EXCEPTION naming the table and the row count; fail closed, and data mapping becomes a founder decision. For cmc_comparability_assessments, when tenant_id has data_type 'text', run ALTER COLUMN tenant_id TYPE integer USING NULLIF(tenant_id,'')::integer, after a RAISE if any value is non-numeric. 4. Extend scripts/ci/check-migration-deploy-path.mjs so it also fails when a baselined off-deploy-path file differs from `git merge-base HEAD origin/concept2cure-v2`. Such a change must go in a set file. Add a selftest case and show it red.

findings.title: Atom semantic search (Authoring AI draft, AnA data-room grounding) loses recall once lumen_data_atoms grows: the HNSW index is scanned first and the tenant/project filter applied after
findings.evidenceAtHead: Code unchanged since 92ccdba1 (git log 92ccdba1..HEAD on db/migrations/20260730_fix_atom_embedding_dimension.sql is empty). In that file, search_atoms_hybrid (line 138), semantic_results (163-171) does `WHERE ... AND (filter_atom_ids IS NULL OR a.id = ANY(filter_atom_ids)) ORDER BY a.embedding <=> query_embedding LIMIT match_count*3` over idx_lumen_atoms_embedding_hnsw (line 83). The live caller is server/services/enhancedEmbeddingService.ts:581-592 (searchHybrid), which passes ARRAY(SELECT id FROM org_atoms). There is no hnsw.ef_search or iterative_scan setting anywhere in server/, scripts/ or migrations/ (grep: 0 hits), and local pgvector is 0.6.0. I ran the HEAD migration file in a scratch DB on local PG16 (dropped afterwards). At 5,000 rows the app path returned 10/10 for a tenant with 20 atoms, because the planner used the PK. So the audit's literal 'small tenant' claim does not reproduce on custom plans. At 50,000 rows: filters of 500/1000/2500/5000 ids (1-10% of rows) returned 1/0/1/8 of 10. The semantic arm's GENERIC plan for the 20-id tenant chose `Index Scan using idx_lumen_atoms_embedding_hnsw ... Rows Removed by Filter: 40, actual rows=0`. The searchSimilar shape (enhancedEmbeddingService.ts:434-503, caller cortexQueryRoutes.ts:305) returned 1 of 5. Launch callers: authoring.router.ts:3842 (Authoring AI draft, minSemanticScore 0.65, so keyword-only hits are dropped), data-room-retrieval.ts:61, chat/send-message.ts:319, evidence-ask.ts:212, advancedRAGPipeline.ts:771. tests/db/atom-search.dbtest.ts never forces the ANN plan. Not affected: the vault passage arm (advancedRAGPipeline.ts:1196-1262, MATERIALIZED scope-then-exact, already present at 92ccdba1), so the empty-built ivfflat on vault.document_chunks (migrations/20260905b_vault_document_chunks.sql:70-72) is unused by its reader. vault.document_catalog has no ANN index, so its search is an exact scan.
findings.remaining: 1. The semantic arm of search_atoms_hybrid ranks over the HNSW index (ef_search 40) and then filters. 2. searchSimilar has the same shape. 3. Recall collapses for any tenant or project holding about 1-5% of atoms, and for every caller once plpgsql switches to its generic plan. 4. The NULL-filter branch of the function is still callable and ranks across tenants under RLS. 5. No recall test forces the ANN plan for atoms. 6. Housekeeping: the ivfflat index on vault.document_chunks was built on an empty table and is now dead weight.
findings.severityRationale: A launch journey silently gets the wrong answer. Authoring's AI section draft and AnA's data-room grounding drop sources that exist, and a miss reads as 'no evidence', not as an error. It needs production-scale data (tens of thousands of atoms), which one pilot uploading an IND's worth of documents across several projects can reach. The audit's mechanism is right; its trigger was misdescribed: on custom plans it is a mid-share tenant or project that fails, while a 20-atom tenant fails only on a generic plan.
findings.humanTestingNote: Testers will not see this at seed or test volumes (under about 10k atoms), because the planner does an exact scan. On a staging database with tens of thousands of atoms: an Authoring 'AI draft' of a CTD section reports zero or few retrieved sources, and AnA data-room answers cite nothing even though matching uploaded documents exist. There is no tester workaround; log it as a retrieval recall defect, not as missing data.
findings.instructions:
1. Work on concept2cure-v2 only (Rule 0). Amend db/migrations/20260730_fix_atom_embedding_dimension.sql IN PLACE (Rule 1: it re-runs on every deploy). Add a dated header block, e.g. 'AMENDED IN PLACE 2026-10-xx (DATA-06): atom search scopes first, then ranks exactly; HNSW+filter returned 0-1 of 10 at 50k rows.' Do not append a new migration.
2. In search_atoms_hybrid (line 138), first statement of the plpgsql body: `IF filter_atom_ids IS NULL THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'search_atoms_hybrid requires filter_atom_ids (tenant scope)' USING ERRCODE = '42501'; END IF;`. This fails closed. The only caller, enhancedEmbeddingService.searchHybrid:581-592, always passes the array.
3. Replace semantic_results (lines 163-171) with a scope-first form, mirroring advancedRAGPipeline.ts:1196-1262: `scoped AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT a.id, a.embedding FROM lumen_data_atoms a WHERE a.id = ANY(filter_atom_ids) AND a.embedding IS NOT NULL AND a.status = 'active' AND (filter_atom_type IS NULL OR a.atom_type = filter_atom_type)), semantic_results AS (SELECT s.id, 1 - (s.embedding <=> query_embedding) AS score FROM scoped s ORDER BY s.embedding <=> query_embedding LIMIT match_count * 3)`. Leave keyword_results and combined unchanged. The existing DROP/CREATE pair in the file already replaces the function on re-run.
4. search_atoms_semantic (line 97) has no caller in server/ (grep 'search_atoms_semantic('). Either give it the same scoped form plus a required scope argument, or stop creating it: keep its `DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS` in this same file and note the removal in the header. Before removing it, confirm that no client, AnA tool or script calls it.
5. server/services/enhancedEmbeddingService.ts searchSimilar (434-517): rewrite the query as `WITH scoped AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT a.* FROM lumen_data_atoms a JOIN organizations o ON a.organization_id = o.id WHERE o.uuid = $4 AND a.embedding IS NOT NULL AND <eligibility/filters>) SELECT ... FROM scoped ORDER BY embedding <=> $1 LIMIT $3`. Alternatively, move cortexQueryRoutes.ts:305 onto searchHybrid and delete searchSimilar (zero duplication); the commit must name searchHybrid as the replacement and the test that reaches it.
6. Add tests/db/atom-search-recall.dbtest.ts. Seed at least 20,000 atoms with random 1536-d vectors across two orgs: drop idx_lumen_atoms_embedding_hnsw, bulk insert, recreate the index, ANALYZE. Include (a) an org with 20 atoms and (b) an org/project holding about 2% of rows. Assert searchHybrid({limit:10}) returns 10 results with semanticScore > 0 for both, once with plan_cache_mode=force_generic_plan and once with the default. Run it against the current function first and record the failure (expected 0-1 of 10) in the commit message. Then apply steps 2-5 and show it passing.
7. Optional: the empty-built ivfflat index idx_vault_document_chunks_embedding has no reader that uses it. If you remove it, do so by amending migrations/20260905b_vault_document_chunks.sql in place (its creator), with a dated header. Run `npm run ci:migration-drop-safety` and its selftest.
8. Alternative to steps 3 and 5, once production runs pgvector 0.8 or later (see DATA-13 engine pin): `SET LOCAL hnsw.iterative_scan = strict_order` in the search transaction. The recall test in step 6 must still pass.
findings.acceptance: 1. The new dbtest at 20k+ atoms FAILS on the current HEAD function: the 2%-share filter returns 0-1 of 10, and the generic plan shows `Index Scan using idx_lumen_atoms_embedding_hnsw ... Rows Removed by Filter`. 2. It PASSES after the amendment, under both plan_cache_mode settings. 3. EXPLAIN of the function's semantic arm with filter_atom_ids set shows no HNSW Order By node. 4. `SELECT search_atoms_hybrid('x', v, 0.7, 0.3, 10, NULL, NULL)` raises SQLSTATE 42501. 5. tests/db/atom-search.dbtest.ts still passes, including its cross-tenant test. 6. On a 50k-atom staging DB, an Authoring AI draft for a section whose evidence was uploaded reports sourcesRetrieved > 0. 7. ci:migration-drop-safety is green.
findings.dependencies: None required. Optional: DATA-13 (production RDS engine/pgvector version), if iterative_scan is chosen instead of scope-first exact ranking.

findings.evidenceAtHead: The pooling code is unchanged since 92ccdba1 (git log 92ccdba1..HEAD on server/services/intelligence/ana-failure-learning.ts and server/routes/regulatory-intelligence.ts is empty). extractFailurePatterns (ana-failure-learning.ts:300-345) groups correction_text across organization_id. getSuggestedCorrections (439-470) reads intelligence.failure_patterns with no organization filter. POST /patterns/extract (regulatory-intelligence.ts:303-315) accepts caller-supplied minTenantCount/minFailureCount, with no clamp against MIN_TENANT_COUNT=3 (line 35). recordInteraction stores promptSummary/responseSummary/correctionText (routes :253-287), with no consent check. scripts/db/rls-coverage-check.sql:89-95 still allowlists intelligence.ana_interactions, pattern_warnings and template_validations as a 'cross-tenant analytics carve-out', and no RLS DDL exists for them in migrations/ or db/migrations/. The router is still mounted unconditionally (server/bootstrap/register-advanced-platform-routes.ts:88-96). Production containment: shared/constants/ui-surface-registry.ui-v2.ts:828 attributes /api/regulatory-intelligence only to surface 'reg-change', which is not in LAUNCH_SURFACE_IDS (shared/constants/launch-scope.ts). I ran a tsx script against HEAD: launchScopeApiVerdict('/api/regulatory-intelligence/interactions'|'/corrections'|'/patterns/extract') returns 'out-of-scope'; readLaunchScopeMode({NODE_ENV:'production'}) returns 'on'; readLaunchScopeMode({NODE_ENV:'development'}) returns 'off'. moduleEntitlementGate refuses out-of-scope paths with 403 (moduleEntitlementGate.ts:113-117) and is mounted at server/startup/routes.ts:108, before registerAdvancedPlatformRoutes at :199. That containment already existed at 92ccdba1. Since then, .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml:633-655 (commit 471e5a4cd, 2026-10-01) refuses a production task definition with LAUNCH_SCOPE_ENFORCE other than 'on' or set from a secret. No client code (client/src), AnA/MCP service, or scheduler calls recordInteraction, extractFailurePatterns, getSuggestedCorrections or buildPromptHints. Their only entry points are the out-of-scope routes.
findings.fixedBy: No change to the pooling itself. Production containment comes from server/middleware/moduleEntitlementGate.ts:113-117 together with server/services/entitlements/launch-scope.ts:42-58 (both pre-date the audit) and the deploy guard .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml:633-655 (471e5a4cd, post-audit).
findings.remaining: 1. The database layer is unchanged: intelligence.ana_interactions holds tenant free text with RLS off, and it is explicitly allowlisted. 2. There is no per-tenant consent or opt-in. 3. Cross-tenant reads (/corrections, /templates/prompt-hints) are unscoped. 4. Any authenticated org can force promotion with minTenantCount=1. 5. The out-of-scope router is mounted and fully reachable wherever launch scope is off: every non-production environment by default, including local and staging deployments that do not set NODE_ENV=production. 6. findings.severityRationale: Lowered from P1. In the pilot's production deploy the HTTP surface returns 403. The default is on in production and the deploy refuses 'off'. No UI, AnA tool or job writes or reads these tables, so no pilot customer's text can reach another tenant. The remaining problem is a latent confidentiality and contract defect, plus out-of-scope surface (Rule 2) and a database table without RLS. It must be closed before enterprise GA or before reg-change is promoted. The audit overstated the production impact even at 92ccdba1, because the launch-scope gate (added 2026-09-25) already refused these paths.
findings.humanTestingNote: No launch screen calls these endpoints, so click-through testers never touch them. On a local or dev deployment, launch scope is off by default (NODE_ENV not production). There, an API-level tester can POST /api/regulatory-intelligence/interactions with correctionText as tenant A, call POST /patterns/extract with {minTenantCount:1,minFailureCount:1}, and read A's text as tenant B via GET /corrections. Workaround for staging: run with NODE_ENV=production or LAUNCH_SCOPE_ENFORCE=on, which returns 403 LAUNCH_SCOPE.
findings.instructions:
1. Founder: decide whether cross-tenant learning ships and under what customer contract or consent (the audit's open question). Until a yes, the code path is OFF everywhere, not only in production. Work on concept2cure-v2 (Rule 0).
2. server/routes/regulatory-intelligence.ts: add one guard ahead of the cross-tenant endpoints: POST /interactions (:253), GET /corrections (:289), POST /patterns/extract (:303), GET /agency-requirements (:317), POST /patterns/:id/promote (:330), POST /warnings/replay (:429), POST /patterns/maintenance (:448). The guard returns 404 unless env CROSS_TENANT_LEARNING === 'on'. Unset means off in every environment, and production refuses to boot on any value other than 'on'/'off', matching readLaunchScopeMode. No client or AnA caller exists (grep client/src, server/services/ana*, server/mcp), so no user-facing capability is removed. Say so in the commit and name the route test from step 7.
3. server/services/intelligence/template-registry.ts:405-415 (buildPromptHints): treat includeCorrections as false unless CROSS_TENANT_LEARNING is on. In regulatory-intelligence.ts:563, stop defaulting it to true.
4. Consent: add `cross_tenant_learning_opt_in BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE` to public.organizations through a new additive migration listed in C2C_MIGRATION_FILES (scripts/db/migration-set.mjs), inserted before the final RLS sweep pair (ci:migration-set-order). In recordInteraction (ana-failure-learning.ts:195), do not persist promptSummary, responseSummary or correctionText for orgs not opted in. In extractFailurePatterns (300-345), restrict the `failures` CTE to `organization_id IN (SELECT id FROM organizations WHERE cross_tenant_learning_opt_in)`.
5. Clamp extraction: in extractFailurePatterns, use Math.max(opts.minTenantCount ?? 0, MIN_TENANT_COUNT) and Math.max(opts.minFailureCount ?? 0, MIN_FAILURE_COUNT). Require a platform-admin role on /patterns/extract, /patterns/:id/promote and /patterns/maintenance.
6. RLS: enable and FORCE row-level security on intelligence.ana_interactions, intelligence.pattern_warnings and intelligence.template_validations, with organization_id policies matching the canonical tenant policy. Do this by amending db/migrations/20260520_ana_failure_learning.sql and 20260520_document_templates.sql in place, each with a dated header note (they are in the set at migration-set.mjs:698-699). Then remove those three entries from scripts/db/rls-coverage-check.sql:89-95. Run the cross-tenant aggregation through a SECURITY DEFINER function owned by a NOLOGIN role that returns only aggregated, opted-in rows, with `SET search_path` pinned.
7. Verify by failing first. (a) A route test: with CROSS_TENANT_LEARNING unset, POST /api/regulatory-intelligence/interactions must return 404. Show it returning 201 before the change. (b) A dbtest as app_service scoped to org A: SELECT org B's ana_interactions row must return 0 rows. Show it returning 1 before step 6. (c) Run rls-coverage-check with the allowlist entries removed: it must fail before step 6 and pass after.
findings.acceptance: 1. With CROSS_TENANT_LEARNING unset, in every NODE_ENV, the seven cross-tenant endpoints return 404 and /templates/prompt-hints returns no corrections. With the flag on, an org without opt-in gets no correction_text persisted and is excluded from extraction. 3. minTenantCount=1 in the request body no longer promotes a single-tenant pattern. 4. As app_service in org A, `SELECT count(*) FROM intelligence.ana_interactions WHERE organization_id = <B>` returns 0 (1 before). 5. scripts/db/rls-coverage-check.sql has no intelligence.ana_interactions, pattern_warnings or template_validations allowlist entries and passes on a fresh provision. 6. findings.title: Email-verification link still lands behind the protected shell; self-serve signup cannot complete on any non-dev deployment
findings.evidenceAtHead: client/src/concept2cure/router/ZenRouter.tsx:175-176 auth-route regex is still /^\/(concept2cure\/)?(login|signup|password-reset)(\/|\?|$)/. The only diff to this file since 92ccdba1 is the returnTo query at :88-95. Evaluated under node at HEAD: '/concept2cure/verify-email authRoute=false v2Owns(protected)=true'. The <Route path="/concept2cure/verify-email"> at :220 is dead code because the uiV2Owns branch at :181-188 returns <ProtectedZenApp/> first. server/services/email-verification.ts:26,64 still mails `${base}/concept2cure/verify-email#token=...`. server/routes/auth.ts:936 sets verificationRequired = !isDevAuthAllowed(), which is true unless NODE_ENV=development AND ALLOW_DEV_AUTH=1 (server/auth/dev-auth-policy.ts:24-29). auth.ts:1144-1162: signup returns 201 with no session. auth.ts:512-526: login refuses with 403 AUTH_EMAIL_UNVERIFIED. Concept2CureLogin.tsx:479-482: the 'verify' button calls setLocation('/concept2cure/verify-email'), which loops back into the same redirect. Reproduced at HEAD with a scratch vitest file outside the repo, using the same mocks as v2/__tests__/deepLinkKeepsProgram.test.tsx: <ZenRouter/> signed out at /concept2cure/verify-email#token=... printed PATH_AFTER=/concept2cure/login?returnTo=%2Fconcept2cure%2Fverify-email and VERIFY_PAGE_RENDERED=false. The token fragment is dropped. auth/__tests__/VerifyEmail.test.tsx mocks wouter and tests the component in isolation, so it cannot catch the routing defect. tests/e2e has no verify-email spec. The invite path is unaffected: server/services/password-setup-token.ts:50 builds /concept2cure/password-reset?token=, which matches the regex.
findings.remaining: Whole finding. The mailed link /concept2cure/verify-email#token=... is routed to the protected shell, so it redirects to sign-in and drops the token. Every self-serve account stays pending_verification for good, and the login page's 'verify' button loops. No test proves the route is public.
findings.severityRationale: Not P0 for this pilot. It is sales-led, and invitees activate through /concept2cure/password-reset?token=, which is inside the public-route regex, so the pilot can start. It is P1 because self-serve signup is always mounted in production (no flag on POST /api/auth/signup, auth.ts:887). A pilot user's colleague or a prospect who uses 'Create account' gets an org and a pending admin that can never activate, and lands in a sign-in loop. The fix is S.
findings.humanTestingNote: Where it shows: any deployment with dev-auth off (NODE_ENV not 'development' or ALLOW_DEV_AUTH not '1') and SMTP configured. The tester signs up, gets the e-mail and clicks the link. They land on the sign-in page with returnTo=/concept2cure/verify-email and the account is not confirmed. Signing in then says the address is unverified, and the 'verify' button returns to sign-in. Without SMTP, signup instead answers 'Sign-up is not available right now.' Locally with NODE_ENV=development and ALLOW_DEV_AUTH=1, signup skips verification and the bug cannot be seen. Workaround: provision testers through Admin > invite member. The activation link /concept2cure/password-reset?token=... works.
findings.instructions:
1. Work on concept2cure-v2 only (CLAUDE.md Rule 0). Pull with --ff-only or merge, never rebase.
2. Write the failing test first: client/src/concept2cure/router/__tests__/publicAuthRoutes.test.tsx (jsdom). Copy the mocks from client/src/concept2cure/v2/__tests__/deepLinkKeepsProgram.test.tsx:17-28: useAuth unauthenticated, ../../auth with VerifyEmail rendering a test id, Concept2CureLogin, IdleSessionGuard and V2App. Call window.history.replaceState(null,'','/concept2cure/verify-email#token=<60+ char token>'), render <ZenRouter/>, wait, then assert that window.location.pathname stays '/concept2cure/verify-email' and the VerifyEmail test id is rendered. Run it at HEAD and confirm it FAILS: the path becomes /concept2cure/login?returnTo=%2Fconcept2cure%2Fverify-email. Keep that red output for the commit message.
3. Create shared/constants/public-auth-paths.ts. Export PUBLIC_AUTH_SEGMENTS = ['login','signup','password-reset','verify-email'] as const, VERIFY_EMAIL_PATH = '/concept2cure/verify-email', PASSWORD_SETUP_PATH = '/concept2cure/password-reset', and isPublicAuthPath(location) built from the segments: ^/(concept2cure/)?(seg1|seg2|...)(/|\?|$).
4. client/src/concept2cure/router/ZenRouter.tsx:175-176: replace the inline regex with isPublicAuthPath(location) imported from '@shared/constants/public-auth-paths'. Leave the existing <Route path="/concept2cure/verify-email"> at :220 as it is; it becomes reachable.
5. server/services/email-verification.ts:26: re-export VERIFY_EMAIL_PATH from shared/constants/public-auth-paths instead of declaring it. server/services/password-setup-token.ts:50: build the URL from PASSWORD_SETUP_PATH. After this, the client router and the mailed links read one list.
6. Add a parity case to the same test file: isPublicAuthPath(VERIFY_EMAIL_PATH) and isPublicAuthPath(PASSWORD_SETUP_PATH) are true, and so is '/concept2cure/login', the SSO handoff base in server/routes/sso.ts:111. Show that removing 'verify-email' from the list makes it fail.
7. Re-run the step-2 test and confirm it passes. Also run client/src/concept2cure/auth/__tests__/VerifyEmail.test.tsx and client/src/concept2cure/v2/__tests__/deepLinkKeepsProgram.test.tsx and confirm both still pass.
8. Add an end-to-end proof: tests/e2e/signup-verify.e2e.spec.ts, run in a CI job with NODE_ENV=production-like (ALLOW_DEV_AUTH unset) and a Mailpit service container (SMTP_HOST/SMTP_USER/SMTP_PASS pointed at it). Steps: sign up through /concept2cure/signup, read the captured mail through the Mailpit HTTP API, open the link, see the confirmed state, sign in and land on /concept2cure. Negative case: a tampered token shows the not-confirmed message and offers a new link.
9. Commit with the red/green outputs and push to concept2cure-v2.
findings.acceptance: (a) The new router test fails at HEAD (redirect to /concept2cure/login) and passes after the change. (b) The parity test fails if 'verify-email' is removed from PUBLIC_AUTH_SEGMENTS. (c) With dev-auth off and a mail sink, the Playwright spec signs up, opens the captured link, sees 'confirmed', signs in and lands on the shell; a tampered token shows the expired or invalid message. (d) The server's VERIFY_EMAIL_PATH and the client router import the same constant (grep shows one definition).
findings.dependencies: A mail-capture service (e.g. Mailpit) in the e2e CI job, for step 8 only. Founder decision on whether self-serve signup is offered during the pilot: if not, also gate POST /api/auth/signup and the signup link behind an explicit setting (separate change).

recheck.testerNote:
Fixed at 8ca7e74ca. You need a stack that requires verification and can send mail.

- Compose: docker-compose.yml or docker-compose.beta.yml. APP_URL must be an https address that your TLS proxy actually serves, and ALLOWED_ORIGINS must include it. A plain-http APP_URL boots, but sign-up answers "Sign-up is not available right now."
- Local: NODE_ENV=development without ALLOW_DEV_AUTH=1, and SMTP_HOST, SMTP_USER and SMTP_PASS all set (SMTP_PORT defaults to 465 with implicit TLS). Without SMTP, the docs/LOCAL_TESTING.md recipe gives the same 503 at sign-up.

Steps:
1. In a signed-out or private browser window, sign up at /concept2cure/signup.
2. Open the e-mailed link /concept2cure/verify-email#token=… in a browser that is still signed out. A browser signed in as another account goes to the app and does not verify.
3. Expected: "Your e-mail address is confirmed" and a Sign in button. There is no redirect to the login page, and the token is cleared from the address bar.
4. Sign in. Like every sign-in on these stacks, this needs the 6-digit code e-mailed to you.

Also check: before verifying, a sign-in attempt shows the unverified error with a "Request a new confirmation link" button. That button opens the verify page with a "Send a new link" form; the page text reads "This link is not valid or has expired…". It must not loop back to sign-in.

Limits: 5 sign-ups and 10 verify or resend requests per hour per IP in production.

With NODE_ENV=development and ALLOW_DEV_AUTH=1, including the Codespaces guide, sign-up skips verification by design and this path does not appear. Do not judge it on the Vite dev server (npm run dev): React StrictMode runs the verify page twice there, so the account is activated but the page then shows 'This link is not valid or has expired'. That is a development-build artifact, not a failure of the fix.
