findings.title: About 2,600 native nested CSS rules still ship unlowered (no build.cssTarget); five nested @keyframes are also dropped
findings.evidenceAtHead: vite.config.ts has no commits since the audit (`git log 92ccdba1..HEAD -- vite.config.ts` returns nothing). At HEAD it still sets `build.target: 'es2022'` (:76) and has no `cssTarget`, `cssMinify: 'lightningcss'` or `css.lightningcss`. postcss.config.js runs only @tailwindcss/postcss and autoprefixer, and there is no browserslist. Vite 6.4.3 defaults `cssTarget` to `target` (node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/dep-Dm0c1Wj2.js:46102) and passes it to esbuild's CSS minify (:44347). @tailwindcss/postcss 4.2.2 quick-bails on any sheet without an import, reference, theme, variant, config, plugin, apply or tailwind at-rule. None of the affected sheets has one (grep count 0 for all ten). Commands run: (1) A postcss walk of every git-tracked client/src CSS file (scratchpad/reverify-ux06/count-nest.cjs) counts 2,607 nested rules in 10 sheets, up from 2,443 at the audit: misc-surfaces-v2 418, research-v2 386, authoring-v2 353, rbm-v2 348, ana-v2 237, device-v2 219, insights-v2 213, translation-v2 202, ectd-v2 183, protocol-dev-editing 48. (2) Vite's own esbuild 0.25.12 (node_modules/vite/node_modules/esbuild) run on authoring-v2.css with minify and target 'es2022' keeps 353 nested rules (output begins `.c2c-v2{.shell[data-editor=true]{...`). With target [chrome107, edge107, firefox104, safari16] it keeps 0. (3) A scan (scratchpad/reverify-ux06/kf.cjs) finds 5 @keyframes nested inside the `.c2c-v2{}` wrapper with no top-level definition anywhere: ana-v2.css acspin, authoring-v2.css dc-open, ectd-v2.css ecRise, research-v2.css pg-fade and pg-pop. esbuild leaves them nested even with browser targets. No CI gate, browser matrix or Playwright project for older browsers exists: playwright.config.ts has a single 'chromium' project, and no ci:* script checks built CSS for nesting. No built dist/ exists in the checkout, so built output was not observed directly; the esbuild run reproduces the exact Vite code path.
findings.remaining: All of it. (1) Set build.cssTarget (or switch to lightningcss with targets) for an agreed browser matrix. (2) Add a CI gate on the built CSS. (3) Publish the supported-browser matrix. Also, outside the original finding: hoist the five @keyframes that are nested inside `.c2c-v2 {}`. Per the CSS Nesting spec, @keyframes is not a permitted nested at-rule, so those animations are likely dropped in every browser. This is inferred from the spec, not observed in a browser.
findings.severityRationale: Downgraded from P1 for this pilot. The breakage only appears on Chrome/Edge before 112 (Apr 2023), Safari before 16.5 (May 2023) or Firefox before 117 (Aug 2023), all more than three years old in Oct 2026. A small or mid-size US biotech on managed evergreen browsers is unlikely to run them. The exposure is real for enterprise GA (pharma VDI and Windows Server 2012 images pinned to Edge 109), and a GxP customer's validation package will ask for a supported-browser statement. The fix is small. The founder should confirm the pilot customer's browser baseline at kickoff. If any pilot seat is below those versions, treat this as P1.
findings.humanTestingNote: Testers on current Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox will see nothing. On an older managed browser (Chrome/Edge < 112, Safari < 16.5, Firefox < 117) the nested rules are discarded, and the editor (authoring-v2), Vault (misc-surfaces-v2), eCTD (ectd-v2) and research layouts collapse or lose styling. Workaround: test on a current evergreen browser and record the browser version in each bug report. Separately, in every browser, five animations (AnA 'acspin', editor 'dc-open', eCTD 'ecRise', research 'pg-fade' and 'pg-pop') probably do not run, because their @keyframes are nested in a style rule. A spinner or entrance animation may appear static. This is cosmetic only.
findings.instructions:
1. Agree the supported-browser matrix with the founder. Proposed: Chrome/Edge >= 109, Firefox ESR >= 115, Safari >= 15.4. Confirm it covers the pilot customer's managed images.
2. In vite.config.ts, inside `build` (:70-76), add `cssTarget: ['chrome109', 'edge109', 'firefox115', 'safari15.4']`, matching step 1. Leave the JS `target: 'es2022'` unless the matrix needs lower. With esbuild, Vite's default minifier, this lowers nesting: verified with Vite's esbuild 0.25.12 on authoring-v2.css, 353 nested rules become 0. The lightningcss route (`build.cssMinify: 'lightningcss'` plus targets) is an acceptable alternative.
3. Hoist the five nested @keyframes out of their `.c2c-v2 { }` wrappers to top level, keeping their names: client/src/concept2cure/v2/styles/ana-v2.css `acspin`, authoring-v2.css `dc-open`, ectd-v2.css `ecRise`, research-v2.css `pg-fade` and `pg-pop`. esbuild does not hoist them even with browser targets.
4. Add scripts/ci/check-built-css-nesting.mjs. It parses every dist/public/assets/*.css with postcss and fails, printing file and selector, on any rule whose ancestor is a style rule, and on any @keyframes whose ancestor is a style rule. Like ci:component-class-coverage, it refuses a stale build or a missing dist (non-zero exit). Add a `--self-test` mode that feeds `.a{.b{color:red}}` and `.a{@keyframes k{to{opacity:1}}}` and asserts both fail. Add `ci:built-css-nesting` and `ci:built-css-nesting:selftest` to package.json.
5. Wire the gate into the `build` job of .github/workflows/ci.yml directly after the 'Build' step (:2284-2285), next to 'Component class coverage'. Run the self-test in the lint job.
6. Prove the gate fails first. Run `npm run build` before step 2 and run the gate: it must exit non-zero and report about 2,600 nested rules (source count at HEAD: 2,607 across 10 sheets). Apply steps 2-3, rebuild, and confirm it exits 0. Do this on a machine that may run a full build, not the shared 4-CPU audit box.
7. Publish the matrix in a supported-browsers section of the customer-facing validation and system-requirements material, and in docs/LAUNCH_DEFINITION_OF_DONE.md evidence if that file references client requirements. Optionally run a one-off manual or Playwright smoke with `executablePath` pointing at a Chromium 109 build over Vault, the Authoring editor and eCTD compile, and file screenshots.
8. Commit on concept2cure-v2 and push there. Merge, never rebase.
findings.acceptance:
1. vite.config.ts sets build.cssTarget (or cssMinify 'lightningcss' with targets) to the published matrix.
2. `npm run ci:built-css-nesting` exits non-zero on a build made without the target and reports about 2,600 nested rules, and exits 0 after. Its self-test fails on both fixtures.
3. The ci.yml build job runs the gate after `npm run build`.
4. A source scan finds 0 @keyframes nested inside a style rule.
5. Vault, the Authoring editor and eCTD render the same layout on Chromium 109 (or Safari 16.0) as on current Chrome, with screenshots filed.
6. The supported-browser matrix is published.

findings.title: AWS stack never applied and never deployed: 0 deploy-aws and 0 provision-database runs at HEAD
findings.evidenceAtHead: GitHub API, queried 2026-10-13: actions/workflows/deploy-aws.yml/runs total_count=0 and provision-database.yml total_count=0. The only remote tag is still v1.0.0 (8d56db74). terraform-tests.yml is 'Terraform tests (offline)' (terraform init -backend=false, mocked providers). Its last run, 37265039179 on 5b45c168e (2026-10-05), succeeded and already contains every terraform/ commit up to HEAD. deploy-aws.yml is production-only: env block at lines 29-81 and `environment: production` at 399, 821 and 959. No staging deploy path exists. Since the audit, CI builds Dockerfile.optimized and boots it on an empty database with sign-in (the 'Production Image Boot' job), so the image path has some proof. That job has been red on every trunk run since a8fd98a23 (2026-10-12 17:27); see OPS-02. Still blocked by OPS-03: the state bucket name is still taken (re-probed 403, eu-west-1). Also blocked by OPS-02: the ci-verdict job in deploy-aws.yml (lines 94-145) refuses any SHA without a successful ci.yml, semgrep.yml and codeql.yml push run, and 0 of the last 1000 trunk ci.yml runs succeeded.
findings.remaining: Everything. No real apply of bootstrap, staging or production has happened. The database has never been provisioned and no deploy or smoke test has run. There are no apply or deploy logs, and no second plan showing zero drift. Every AWS-side control is unproven in AWS: CloudFront-only ALB, KMS vault key, SES login codes, RDS TLS verify-full, the ECS boot contract and the GitHub OIDC roles.
findings.severityRationale: The pilot is defined as one AWS production environment. None exists, and no deploy has ever executed, so the pilot cannot start. A customer date cannot be committed until a first apply and deploy succeed.
findings.humanTestingNote: Testers will not see this on a local deployment. There is no AWS staging or production, so human testing has to run on a local or docker install (scripts/db/install-fresh.mjs plus the dev server). AWS-only behaviour stays untested by testers: CloudFront routing of /mcp, SES delivery of login codes, KMS-encrypted vault objects in S3, and the boot refusals that apply only to the ECS task. Note that HEAD itself cannot provision a fresh database (see OPS-02).
findings.instructions:
1. Founder supplies the inputs: AWS account ID(s); confirmation of us-east-1 (hard-coded in deploy-aws.yml:29 and provision-database.yml env AWS_REGION); the domain and DNS control; an ACM certificate for the ALB (regional) and one for CloudFront (us-east-1); SES production access with DKIM/SPF on the sending domain; AI provider keys plus the AI_PROVIDER_PLACEMENT_APPROVALS JSON; a budget. Fill terraform/environments/production/terraform.tfvars from terraform.tfvars.example and never commit it.
2. Land OPS-03 (rename the state bucket) first. Bootstrap cannot be applied until it is done.
3. Run terraform -chdir=terraform/bootstrap init and apply in the real account. Save the full log.
4. Land OPS-02 until one trunk SHA has a successful ci.yml, semgrep.yml and codeql.yml push run. deploy-aws.yml ci-verdict (lines 94-145) refuses anything else, and the `test` job (lines 148-166) reruns npm run lint and npm test.
5. Production root: run terraform init with the OPS-03 backend config, then terraform plan -out tfplan with a placeholder image_tag. If the account already has a GitHub OIDC provider, set create_github_oidc_provider=false (terraform/environments/production/main.tf:79). Review the plan, then run terraform apply tfplan. The API service will stay unhealthy until the first deploy; that is expected.
6. Run terraform plan again and require 'No changes'. This proves that engine_version '15', auto_minor_version_upgrade and the boot contract do not drift. File both logs.
7. Point the DNS alias(es) at the cloudfront_domain output (production/main.tf:113).
8. From terraform output, set the repo secrets AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN, AWS_BUILD_ROLE_ARN (github_deploy_role_arn and github_build_role_arn, main.tf:149-153) and CLOUDFRONT_DISTRIBUTION_ID (main.tf:157). Create the GitHub environment `production` with required reviewers and a deployment tag policy of v*.
9. Fail first: dispatch deploy-aws.yml on a SHA whose CI is red. Confirm that job 'CI passed for this commit' fails with 'Refusing to deploy a commit whose CI did not pass', and file the run URL.
10. Dispatch provision-database.yml with confirm='provision production database' and file the run URL.
11. Tag the green SHA v<x.y.z>. Require build-push, migrate, deploy-api, deploy-frontend and smoke-test to be green, with /readyz returning 200 through CloudFront.
12. Run npm run pilot:verify-otp (scripts/ops/verify-otp-delivery.mjs) against a real inbox, then sign in through the CloudFront alias.
13. File the apply logs, plan-no-change log and run URLs under docs/evidence/D1/<date>-first-apply/.
findings.acceptance:
- GitHub API shows deploy-aws.yml total_count >= 1, with a run that concludes success for every job, including smoke-test.
- provision-database.yml has one successful run.
- A deploy-aws dispatch on a red SHA was shown failing at ci-verdict before the green deploy.
- terraform plan after the apply reports no changes.
- curl https://<alias>/readyz returns 200.
- pilot:verify-otp delivers a code to a real inbox, and a person signs in.
- The logs are filed under docs/evidence/D1/.
findings.dependencies: OPS-03 (open, state bucket); OPS-02 (open, green SHA required by ci-verdict); founder inputs (account, domain, ACM, SES, AI keys); OPS-08 and OPS-09 (worker_desired_count = 0 in the tfvars examples, and Dockerfile.optimized:172 now copies workers/artifact-compute; neither re-verified in this batch); OPS-11 launch config.

findings.title: Canonical branch still red: 0 green in the last 1000 CI runs, HEAD cannot provision a fresh database, nothing gates landing (deploy-time CI gate added)
findings.evidenceAtHead: GitHub API, 2026-10-13: the last 1000 ci.yml runs on concept2cure-v2 (2026-09-25T03:10 to 2026-10-13T16:34) are 993 failure, 7 queued or in progress, and 0 success. Run 38358525641 is on 9a59bc8f9 (HEAD^; HEAD 94b4f9238 only edits docs/work-orders/README.md). In it, Lint fails at 'Proof tier' (ci.yml:301-310, npm run test:proof-tier) and at 'every in-scope AnA tool reads from its register entry' (ci.yml:604-612). Test, Coverage (ratchet) and Integration Tests also fail. So do three provisioning jobs: Blank DB Provisioning ('Deploy migration succeeds on the provisioned database'), Production Boot Smoke ('Provision the schema from scratch') and Production Image Boot ('Provision the empty database with the provision image'). Build, Assemble Release Evidence and Release evidence gate are skipped. HEAD's own run, 38429984856, already fails the same two Lint steps. Reproduced locally at HEAD: npm run ci:step-presentation reports 'FAILED, 10 finding(s)', meaning 10 tools have no `present` block in server/services/ana/tool-authorization.register.json (answer_intelligence_question, assess_recorded_batch_poolability, assess_recorded_process_capability, assess_recorded_stability_trend, commit_intelligence_flow, compare_recorded_dissolution, estimate_recorded_shelf_life, list_cmc_registers, resume_intelligence_flow, start_intelligence_flow). There is also a fresh-database regression at HEAD. In db/migrations/20260813_knowledge_graph_tenant_keys.sql:146-156, the citation backfill reads knowledge_graph_nodes.organization_id before the loop that adds that column. The blank-DB, boot-smoke and image-boot jobs have been red on every trunk run from a8fd98a23 (after 15af6bc4b, 2026-10-12) and were green up to a2acf90b2. Tier 5's authenticated browser smoke and golden journey failed at HEAD (run 38429985184) and are green at 4c03bc548, after the post-HEAD commit 2ef129e54 added the column guard. Nothing gates landing: GET branches/concept2cure-v2 returns protected:false with required_status_checks contexts [], rules/branches returns [], and the only ruleset ('JMSMITH') has enforcement disabled. .husky/pre-push (707 lines) has no vitest, jest or npm test call. repo-health-baseline-refresh.yml:17-20,56-65 still commits a refreshed baseline to concept2cure-v2 after every push. One mitigation landed: deploy-aws.yml:94-145 adds a `ci-verdict` job that requires success of the ci.yml, semgrep.yml and codeql.yml push runs on the exact SHA. build-push (:260) and deploy-frontend (:950) need it, and tests/ci/deploy-refuses-unproven-sha.contract.test.ts pins it. A red SHA therefore can no longer be deployed by tag. CI latency: run 38358525641 was created at 06:45, Lint started at 12:08, and Test finished at 15:28 (about 8.7 h to verdict). The audit's named failing file tests/routes/export-governance-fail-closed.test.ts now passes locally (2/2), so the failure set has churned rather than been cleared.
findings.remaining: Lint has 2 failing steps, plus Test, Coverage and Integration. HEAD cannot provision a fresh database (fixed only after HEAD, in 2ef129e54). No branch protection, ruleset or merge queue exists. Pre-push runs no tests. The bot auto-refresh of the repo-health baseline is still active. No deployable (green) SHA exists, so the release path is closed.
findings.severityRationale: The deploy refuses every SHA (ci-verdict plus the in-workflow npm test), so no release can reach the pilot. At HEAD, a new environment cannot even be provisioned. A validated state cannot be claimed for GxP while trunk has had no green run for 18 days.
findings.humanTestingNote: Symptom at HEAD 94b4f9238: setting up a NEW test environment fails at deploy-migrate with 'column n.organization_id does not exist' in db/migrations/20260813_knowledge_graph_tenant_keys.sql. CI's authenticated browser sign-in smoke and the WO-06 golden journey also fail at this SHA. Workaround: merge origin/concept2cure-v2 at or after 2ef129e54, where Tier 5 sign-in and the golden journey are green (4c03bc548, 28f7bd63b). Alternatively, test against a database provisioned before 15af6bc4b, since replays pass. Because trunk is never green, testers should record the exact SHA under test with every defect report.
findings.instructions:
1. Bring the fresh-DB fix in by merging, never rebasing: git fetch origin && git merge origin/concept2cure-v2 (it must include 2ef129e54). Fail-first evidence already exists: CI run 38358525641 has a red 'Blank DB Provisioning + Deploy Migration'. Require that job, Production Boot Smoke and Production Image Boot to be green on the merged SHA.
2. Fix the Lint step at ci.yml:604-612. In server/services/ana/tool-authorization.register.json, add a `present` block, with a verb and a source taken from shared/ana/step-verbs.ts, to each of the 10 tools that npm run ci:step-presentation lists. Run npm run ci:step-presentation:selftest && npm run ci:step-presentation and require exit 0.
3. Fix the Lint step at ci.yml:301-310. Run npm run test:proof-tier (vitest over tests/schema-contract, tests/golden-journeys and tests/export-contract), then fix each failing spec at the source. Never loosen an assertion.
4. Fix the Test job. Enumerate the failing files from the uploaded test-results artifact of the latest trunk run (vitest.json and jest.json), or run npx vitest run --config vitest.config.ts <dir> one directory at a time. Fix the code, then re-run each file on its own.
5. Re-run Coverage (ratchet) and Integration Tests and fix whatever remains. Do not lower the coverage baseline to pass.
6. Stop the bot from rewriting the gate's baseline. Remove the commit-and-push step at .github/workflows/repo-health-baseline-refresh.yml:56-65; the workflow is a maintenance job, not a user capability. Baseline changes then go through a human commit that the Lint repo-health step checks.
7. Gating under Rule 0 is a founder decision; record it in docs/ and CLAUDE.md. A ruleset with required status checks would refuse every direct push, because a commit has no checks before it is pushed, so it is incompatible with Rule 0 unless a merge queue is adopted. The in-rule options are (a) and (b):
   (a) In .husky/pre-push, add a bounded test step: npx vitest related --run on the files changed versus @{u}, plus npm run test:proof-tier. Add a selftest that commits a deliberately failing test and shows pre-push refusing it.
   (b) A red-trunk freeze: a workflow_run workflow on CI for concept2cure-v2 that, on failure, sets a repository variable TRUNK_RED=sha. pre-push reads it through the GitHub API and refuses pushes whose message does not reference the fix.
8. Keep deploy-aws.yml ci-verdict (lines 94-145) and prove it fails first: dispatch deploy-aws.yml on a red SHA and file the refusal run URL.
9. Reduce CI queueing (see OPS-25) so a verdict lands within deploy-aws.yml CI_VERDICT_WAIT_MINUTES=90 (line 105). Run 38358525641 waited about 5 h for runners.
findings.acceptance:
- At least 10 consecutive ci.yml push runs on concept2cure-v2 conclude success, with Build, Assemble Release Evidence and Release evidence gate executed, not skipped.
- Blank DB Provisioning, Production Boot Smoke, Production Image Boot and Tier 5 are green on trunk.
- npm run ci:step-presentation exits 0, and its selftest exits non-zero when one `present` block is removed.
- No github-actions[bot] commits land on concept2cure-v2 after the change (git log --author=github-actions --since=<date> is empty).
- A deliberately failing test is refused by pre-push (shown), and deploy-aws ci-verdict refuses a red SHA (run URL filed).
findings.dependencies: Founder decision on the gating model versus Rule 0 (OPS-18); OPS-25 (CI capacity and latency); merge of 2ef129e54.

findings.title: Terraform state bucket name c2c-terraform-state is still taken (eu-west-1) and still hard-coded in bootstrap and both backends
findings.evidenceAtHead: terraform/environments/production/main.tf:19-23 and terraform/environments/staging/main.tf:19-23 still declare backend s3 { bucket = 'c2c-terraform-state', region = 'us-east-1', dynamodb_table = 'c2c-terraform-lock' }. terraform/bootstrap/variables.tf:6-9 still defaults state_bucket_name to 'c2c-terraform-state'. No commit in 92ccdba1..HEAD changes either the backend blocks or that default. Re-probed on 2026-10-13: curl https://c2c-terraform-state.s3.amazonaws.com/ returned HTTP 403 AccessDenied with x-amz-bucket-region: eu-west-1. The other planned global names (c2c-prod-part11-evidence, c2c-prod-frontend, c2c-prod-vault, c2c-stg-part11-evidence, c2c-stg-frontend, c2c-stg-vault) return 404 NoSuchBucket, so they are still free but carry no suffix (terraform/stack/main.tf:9-10, terraform/stack/vault_storage.tf:29) in a public repository.
findings.remaining: Rename the state bucket (account-suffixed) in bootstrap and in both backends, with a guard. Optionally, account-suffix the evidence, frontend and vault bucket names before the first apply.
findings.severityRationale: Bootstrap apply fails with BucketAlreadyExists, and terraform init in both roots fails (access denied, or a region mismatch if the bucket is the founder's). No AWS environment can be created until this is fixed. Trivial effort, but it hard-blocks OPS-01.
findings.instructions:
1. Ask the founder whether the eu-west-1 bucket c2c-terraform-state is theirs. Default plan regardless: a new account-suffixed name, because reusing it forces an eu-west-1 backend for a us-east-1 stack.
2. terraform/bootstrap/main.tf: add data "aws_caller_identity" "current" {} and a local, state_bucket = coalesce(var.state_bucket_name, "c2c-tfstate-${data.aws_caller_identity.current.account_id}-${var.region}"). Use local.state_bucket at line 22 (aws_s3_bucket.tfstate.bucket) and at lines 43 and 49 (KMS description and alias). terraform/bootstrap/variables.tf:6-10: change the default to null. The output at main.tf:118-119 already exposes the name.
3. In both roots (production/main.tf:20, staging/main.tf:20), delete the literal bucket line from backend "s3" and keep key, region and dynamodb_table, making it a partial backend configuration. Add terraform/environments/{production,staging}/backend.hcl.example containing bucket = "c2c-tfstate-<ACCOUNT_ID>-us-east-1". Once the account is known, commit the real backend.hcl; an account ID is not a secret.
4. In terraform/README.md, sections 1-3 (lines 24-50): change the init steps to terraform init -backend-config=backend.hcl, and get the name from terraform -chdir=terraform/bootstrap output -raw state_bucket.
5. Add scripts/ci/check-terraform-backend.mjs plus package.json scripts ci:terraform-backend and ci:terraform-backend:selftest, and run them in terraform-tests.yml. The check refuses any backend "s3" block in terraform/environments/* that carries a literal bucket, and refuses a bootstrap default other than null. Selftest (fail first): feed it git show 92ccdba1:terraform/environments/production/main.tf and require a refusal, then require HEAD to pass after steps 2-3.
6. Optional, and only before the first apply, because renaming a created bucket means recreating it: account-suffix local.evidence_bucket and local.frontend_bucket (stack/main.tf:9-10) and local.vault_bucket (vault_storage.tf:29). Replace deploy-aws.yml:80 FRONTEND_BUCKET: c2c-prod-frontend with ${{ vars.FRONTEND_BUCKET }}, set from the frontend_bucket output (stack/outputs.tf:86). Update terraform/modules/github-deploy-roles/tests/roles.tftest.hcl:36, and confirm that boot_contract.tftest.hcl:689 still excludes FRONTEND_BUCKET.
7. In the real account: terraform -chdir=terraform/bootstrap init/apply, then terraform init -backend-config=backend.hcl in each root. File the logs.
findings.acceptance:
- The backend guard refuses the 92ccdba1 production main.tf (shown) and passes at the new HEAD.
- No file under terraform/ contains the string c2c-terraform-state.

ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, with epoch-aligned windowKeyOf. The table is migrations/20261001d_scheduled_job_claims.sql (public, organization_id INTEGER NOT NULL, IF NOT EXISTS only), listed in C2C_MIGRATION_FILES at scripts/db/migration-set.mjs:3022. 2) Coordinated at HEAD: retention sweep (server/jobs/retentionCron.ts:409, default ON in production); external intelligence (externalIntelligenceSweep.ts:50, default ON); audit-chain sweep (auditChainIntegritySweep.ts:612); 5-minute chain monitor (services/audit/chainIntegrityMonitor.ts, per window); sentinel (services/sentinel/scheduler.ts:149); schedule-of-events (scheduleOfEventsSweep.ts:101 lease, plus a per-schedule guarded claim at :117); digest heartbeat (digest-heartbeat.ts:179 lease plus a DB per-day check); memory consolidation and citation pruner (lease). Caveat (tracked elsewhere, OPS-02/D1): the same CI job is red at its later 'Provision the empty database' step, so the image is built but not yet boot-proven end to end.
findings.fixedBy: 2eda0ed0f (Dockerfile.optimized:79-95,171-172; scriptWorker.ts:65; workerClient.ts:51; scripts/ci/check-image-document-runtime.mjs + __tests__/image-document-runtime.test.mjs); a3df3cb0c (ci.yml production-image-boot builds Dockerfile.optimized --target production in CI)

findings.title: Deploy now requires a green CI verdict for the SHA and pins/scans the digest, but there is still no staging stage, production rebuilds instead of promoting, and nothing rolls back automatically
findings.evidenceAtHead: Closed part: .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml:94-145 job ci-verdict reads the newest push run on concept2cure-v2 of ci.yml, semgrep.yml and codeql.yml for the exact SHA and refuses anything but success (pinned by tests/ci/deploy-refuses-unproven-sha.contract.test.ts); build-push needs it (:258-260); Trivy image scan blocks the ECR push on HIGH/CRITICAL (:329-341); deploy-api registers a task def pinned to <repo>@sha256:<digest> (:835-905); deploy-frontend runs only after deploy-api succeeds (:948-966); CI's production-image-boot builds the same Dockerfile target at the same SHA (ci.yml:2114-2121). None of this existed at 92ccdba1 (`git show 92ccdba1:.github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml | grep -c ci-verdict` -> 0). Still open: the workflow is named 'Deploy to AWS (Production)' and the env block hard-codes production names (:29-81: AWS_REGION us-east-1, ECR_API_REPO c2c-prod-api, ECS_CLUSTER c2c-production, FRONTEND_BUCKET c2c-prod-frontend); `environment: production` is literal at :399, :821, :959; triggers are only `v*` tags and dispatch (:17-19); build-push rebuilds from source (`docker build -f Dockerfile.optimized --target production` :319-327) and deploy-frontend re-runs `npm ci && npm run build` (:967-974) instead of promoting the CI-tested artifact; terraform/environments/staging is targeted only by terraform-compliance.yml, which is pull_request-only and runs `terraform validate`; cerv2-staging-deploy.yml targets docker-compose/Vercel, not AWS; smoke-test (:1016-1072) has no rollback job (rollback is a manual `aws ecs update-service` per comments at :845-850). Recent CI runs on concept2cure-v2 (e.g. 38358525641, 38355530765) conclude failure, so ci-verdict would refuse every deploy today (OPS-02).
findings.fixedBy: 8060c28bc (deploy-aws.yml ci-verdict gate + Trivy image scan before push); efdb0fb7b (frontend publishes after the API); a3df3cb0c (CI builds and boots the production image target)
findings.remaining: 1) No AWS staging stage: deploy-aws.yml is production-only and no workflow applies or deploys terraform/environments/staging. 2) The production deploy rebuilds the image and the frontend from source rather than promoting the digest/bundle CI or staging tested (Debian apt packages in Dockerfile.optimized:64-77 are unpinned, so two builds of one SHA can differ). 3) No automated rollback when the post-deploy smoke test fails. 4) Dead cerv2-staging-deploy.yml is a parallel 'staging' path that deploys nothing to AWS.
findings.severityRationale: The pilot target is a single AWS production environment, and the most dangerous half of the original finding (any tag deploys an unproven SHA) is closed by the ci-verdict gate plus CI building and boot-testing the same Dockerfile target at that SHA. What remains (staging rehearsal of migrations/terraform against a populated database, build-once-promote, automated rollback) is CSV/GxP release-discipline work expected before enterprise GA, not a blocker for a founder-supported pilot.
findings.humanTestingNote: Not observable as a defect in the apps. Context for the test plan: the pipeline provides no AWS staging, so human testing runs on a local or docker-compose stack, which does not exercise CloudFront routing, the S3 vault, the KMS signer or the ECS task definition; AWS-only defects will not surface in this round.
findings.instructions:
All work on concept2cure-v2 (Rule 0), merge never rebase.
1. Founder: decide staging topology (separate AWS account recommended, or same account with distinct stack names) and region; record it where terraform/environments/staging/main.tf backend and tfvars can use it. Apply terraform/environments/staging once (depends on OPS-01/03/04).
2. In .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml add a first job `resolve` that outputs `target`: `staging` for `rc-*` tags, `production` for `v*` tags, and a new workflow_dispatch choice input `target` (staging|production). Add `rc-*` to the push.tags list at :17-19. Rename the workflow 'Deploy to AWS'.
3. Create GitHub environments `staging` and `production`, each with vars AWS_REGION, ECR_API_REPO, ECS_CLUSTER, ECS_API_SERVICE, ECS_API_TASK_FAMILY, ECS_MIGRATE_TASK_FAMILY, FRONTEND_BUCKET and secrets AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN, AWS_BUILD_ROLE_ARN, CLOUDFRONT_DISTRIBUTION_ID; give `production` required reviewers. Delete the hard-coded values in the workflow-level env block (:29-81) and read them from `vars.*`/`secrets.*` at job level; replace the literal `environment: production` at :399, :821, :959 (and add it to build-push and smoke-test) with `environment: ${{ needs.resolve.outputs.target }}`.
4. Build once: make build-push (:258-385) run only when target=staging. Keep its Trivy scan and digest capture; tag the image `sha-${GITHUB_SHA::12}` (ECR tags are immutable). The frontend is already inside the image (production stage copies /app/dist, which contains dist/public), so deploy-frontend must stop rebuilding: replace :967-974 (`npm ci`, `npm run build`) with `docker pull <repo>@<digest>`, `docker create`, `docker cp <id>:/app/dist/public ./dist/public`.
5. On staging smoke-test success (:1016-1072) add a step that writes an additional ECR tag `staging-verified-${GITHUB_SHA::12}` onto the same manifest (`aws ecr batch-get-image` then `aws ecr put-image --image-tag ... --image-manifest ...`).
6. Production path (target=production): add a `promote` job that does NOT run docker build. It looks up `staging-verified-${GITHUB_SHA::12}` with `aws ecr describe-images`, refuses (exit 1, fail closed) when absent, and outputs its imageDigest; wire migrate, deploy-api (IMAGE_DIGEST at :839-840) and deploy-frontend to that output instead of build-push. If staging and production are separate accounts, add ECR cross-account pull or registry replication in terraform/modules/ecr and grant the production deploy role ecr:BatchGetImage on the staging repo.
7. Rollback: in deploy-api, before update-service (:907-916), capture `aws ecs describe-services --cluster $ECS_CLUSTER --services $ECS_API_SERVICE --query 'services[0].taskDefinition' --output text` as output `previous_td_arn`. Add job `rollback` with `needs: [deploy-api, smoke-test]`, `if: always() && needs.deploy-api.result == 'success' && needs.smoke-test.result == 'failure'`, that runs `aws ecs update-service --task-definition <previous_td_arn>` and `aws ecs wait services-stable`. Comment that this is safe because migrations in C2C_MIGRATION_FILES are additive (Rule 1); a non-additive migration requires a manual decision.
8. Delete .github/workflows/cerv2-staging-deploy.yml in the same change (zero duplication); the commit message names deploy-aws.yml's staging target as its replacement and the contract test in step 9 as the reachability proof. It is a workflow, not a user-facing capability.
9. Extend tests/ci/deploy-refuses-unproven-sha.contract.test.ts with assertions that (a) no job reachable when target=production contains `docker build` or `npm run build`; (b) production resolves its digest only via `staging-verified-`; (c) a rollback job exists conditioned on smoke-test failure; (d) no literal `environment: production` remains. Run it against HEAD's deploy-aws.yml first and keep the failing output, then make it pass.
findings.acceptance: 1) Failing first: the new assertions in tests/ci/deploy-refuses-unproven-sha.contract.test.ts fail on HEAD's deploy-aws.yml (docker build at :319-327, npm run build at :973-974, no rollback job, literal environment: production) and pass after the change. 2) An `rc-*` tag deploys to staging, the staging smoke test reports /readyz ready through the staging CloudFront alias, and ECR shows `staging-verified-<sha12>` on the built digest. 3) A `v*` tag on the same SHA runs no build step, and `aws ecs describe-task-definition` shows the production API container image digest equal to the staging one. 4) A `v*` tag on a SHA without `staging-verified-` is refused before migrate. 5) Forcing the staging smoke test to fail (e.g. a dispatch with a deliberately broken readiness URL) triggers the rollback job and the service returns to the previous task-definition revision.
findings.dependencies: OPS-01 (first apply/deploy), OPS-02 (CI must be green or ci-verdict refuses every deploy), OPS-03 (state bucket names), OPS-04 (RDS version), founder decision on staging AWS account/topology and budget.

findings.title: Launch config in IaC: MCP connector, Anthropic key and the PDF/A rule are now settled; SENTRY_DSN is optional and there is still no REDIS_URL (rate limits are per replica)
findings.evidenceAtHead: Closed: terraform/stack/main.tf:275-277 sets MCP_ENABLED=true, MCP_PUBLIC_URL=local.app_origin, MCP_CLIENT_REDIRECT_ALLOWLIST in boot_environment (absent at 92ccdba1); server/index.ts:120 still mounts only on 'true'; .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml:514-522 preflight requires MCP_ENABLED, MCP_PUBLIC_URL, MCP_CLIENT_REDIRECT_ALLOWLIST and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, and :695-705 checks MCP values (exactly 'true', https origin, non-empty allowlist). ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is a required boot secret (main.tf:326; terraform/stack/variables.tf:351-356 validates sk-ant-); OpenAI is opt-in per Order Form (variables.tf:328-340). ECTD_REQUIRE_PDFA: server/services/ectd/pdfa-requirement.ts:1-20 makes PDF/A required only when the deployment or the organisation opts in; the per-org setting settings.submission.requirePdfA has a UI (client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/PdfARequirementSetting.tsx) and is enforced before transmit (server/services/submission-gateways/index.ts:230, resolvePdfARequirement throws when the setting cannot be read). FDA accepts plain PDF 1.4-1.7, so the absent env flag is now a deliberate rule, not a gap. Still open: SENTRY_DSN defaults to "" (terraform/environments/production/variables.tf:181-184), observability_environment is empty when unset (main.tf:338) and SENTRY_DSN is not in the preflight list (deploy-aws.yml:514-522). REDIS_URL: `grep -rni redis terraform/` -> nothing; server/startup/env.ts:104-110 only warns; server/middleware/redisRateLimiter.ts:96-101 falls back to a per-process Map, with api_desired_count=2 (environments/production/variables.tf:48-51), so auth and documents limits are per task and reset on every deploy.
findings.fixedBy: 42842480f (MCP_* in terraform/stack/main.tf:275-277 + deploy preflight); c3e9e4930 (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY boot secret); 19d2be04a (Sentry configurable, OpenAI key validated); 4fdafc362 (PDF/A rule: pdfa-requirement.ts, per-org setting, transmit guard)
findings.remaining: 1) SENTRY_DSN can be omitted: no validation requires it and the deploy preflight does not check it, so production can ship with no error reporting (overlaps OPS-06). 2) No Redis or other shared store in terraform/: REDIS_URL is never set, so rate limiting (including the fail-closed auth and documents buckets) is per process across the 2 API tasks and resets on each deploy; boot only warns.
findings.severityRationale: The items that turned launch features off silently are closed: the remote MCP connector is mounted and preflight-enforced, a drafting-approved Anthropic key is required, and PDF/A is now an explicit per-org/per-deployment rule. The residual is observability (already carried as OPS-06 at P1) and per-replica rate limiting, which doubles brute-force thresholds on a login that still requires the mandatory email OTP. That is hardening before enterprise GA, not a pilot blocker.
findings.instructions:
All work on concept2cure-v2 (Rule 0).
1. Founder decisions, recorded before code: (a) Sentry as a subprocessor (DPA, data region, PII scrubbing) or CloudWatch-only error reporting under OPS-06; (b) shared rate-limit store: ElastiCache (Redis/Valkey) is recommended. A Postgres table keyed by IP/email would conflict with CLAUDE.md Rule 1's `organization_id INTEGER NOT NULL` requirement for pre-authentication keys.
2. If ElastiCache: add terraform/modules/elasticache-redis/ with aws_elasticache_subnet_group (module.vpc.private_subnet_ids), a security group admitting 6379 only from module.ecs.ecs_tasks_security_group_id, and aws_elasticache_replication_group with transit_encryption_enabled=true, at_rest_encryption_enabled=true, kms_key_id, auth_token from random_password, automatic_failover_enabled=true, multi_az_enabled=true, num_cache_clusters=2. Instantiate it in terraform/stack/main.tf.
3. Add a `redis_url` entry to module "secrets" (terraform/stack/main.tf:116 onward) with value `rediss://:<auth_token>@<primary_endpoint_address>:6379`, and add `{ name = "REDIS_URL", value_from = module.secrets.secret_arns["redis_url"] }` to local.boot_secrets (main.tf:316-331).
4. Sentry (if chosen): change terraform/stack/variables.tf:424-430 validation to require a non-empty https DSN, remove the "" default in terraform/environments/production/variables.tf:181-184 and the staging equivalent, document it in terraform.tfvars.example, and confirm server/utils/sentry.ts scrubs request bodies and user identifiers before send. If CloudWatch-only is chosen instead, remove 'SENTRY_DSN' from the recommended list in server/startup/env.ts:105 and record the decision under OPS-06.
5. Add REDIS_URL (and SENTRY_DSN if chosen) to the preflight loop in .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml:514-522 and extend the ::error:: text at :541.
6. Fail closed at boot: in server/startup/env.ts:104-110, when NODE_ENV=production and neither REDIS_URL nor REDIS_TLS_URL is set, refuse to start unless RATE_LIMIT_ACCEPT_MEMORY=true (same pattern as STORAGE_ACCEPT_LOCAL_DISK). Add RATE_LIMIT_ACCEPT_MEMORY=true to the CI single-container boot envs (ci.yml production-boot-smoke env and the production-image-boot app.env heredoc around ci.yml:2163-2190) so those jobs keep booting.
7. Tests, each shown failing on HEAD first: (a) a terraform test in terraform/stack/tests/boot_contract.tftest.hcl asserting REDIS_URL is in the API container secrets (and SENTRY_DSN in its environment if chosen); (b) a contract test under tests/ci/ asserting the deploy preflight list contains REDIS_URL; (c) a unit test that production boot without REDIS_URL and without RATE_LIMIT_ACCEPT_MEMORY exits non-zero; (d) a rate-limiter test with two limiter instances sharing one Redis (ioredis-mock or a container) showing the auth bucket counts across both.
findings.acceptance: 1) Failing first: the new terraform test, the preflight contract test and the boot-refusal test all fail against HEAD and pass after the change. 2) `terraform test` in terraform/stack passes in terraform-tests.yml. 3) The deploy preflight refuses a task definition without REDIS_URL (and without SENTRY_DSN if Sentry is chosen). 4) On a deployment with 2 API tasks, failed sign-in attempts against one account spread across both tasks are refused at the configured auth limit (not twice that), and the count survives a rolling deploy. 5) If Sentry is chosen, a deliberately thrown test error in staging appears in Sentry with no request body or email in the event.

findings.title: VPC: S3 and KMS endpoints now carry traffic, but there is still one NAT gateway in AZ-a and no ECR/Secrets Manager/Logs/STS endpoints
findings.evidenceAtHead: Closed: terraform/modules/vpc-secure/main.tf:92-98 S3 gateway endpoint now has `route_table_ids = [aws_route_table.private.id]` (at 92ccdba1 it had none); :102-110 KMS interface endpoint has `private_dns_enabled = true` in every private subnet; :112-130 endpoint SG admits tcp/443 from the VPC CIDR only (at 92ccdba1 it had no ingress). terraform/modules/vpc-secure/tests/private_paths.tftest.hcl asserts each of these and runs in .github/workflows/terraform-tests.yml (matrix entry terraform/modules/vpc-secure, :55). Still open: one aws_eip.nat and one aws_nat_gateway.this in aws_subnet.public[0] (:57-67); a single aws_route_table.private routes 0.0.0.0/0 to that NAT for all private subnets (:69-82); no aws_vpc_endpoint for ecr.api, ecr.dkr, secretsmanager, logs or sts anywhere in terraform/modules/vpc-secure; terraform/modules/vpc-secure/variables.tf has no per-AZ NAT option. ECS task SG egress is 0.0.0.0/0 through the NAT (terraform/modules/ecs-fargate/main.tf:117-125).
findings.fixedBy: a9157e682 (terraform/modules/vpc-secure/main.tf:84-130 and tests/private_paths.tftest.hcl)
findings.remaining: Single NAT gateway in AZ-a carrying all private egress for both AZs: losing AZ-a (or that NAT) stops ECR API calls (new tasks cannot pull), Secrets Manager fetches (new tasks cannot start), CloudWatch Logs delivery, SMTP (login OTP, so no one can sign in) and AI-provider calls in both AZs. ECR/Secrets Manager/Logs/STS traffic also pays NAT data-processing charges.
findings.severityRationale: What remains is availability during a rare AZ-level failure plus NAT cost. It is not security, tenant-isolation or data-integrity exposure, and a founder-supported single-customer pilot can accept an AZ-outage window. The billed-but-dead endpoints and NAT-routed Vault/KMS traffic are fixed. Per-AZ egress belongs before enterprise GA and any availability SLA.
findings.instructions:
All work on concept2cure-v2 (Rule 0).
1. In terraform/modules/vpc-secure/variables.tf add `variable "nat_gateway_per_az" { type = bool, default = true }` and `variable "interface_endpoints" { type = list(string), default = ["kms", "ecr.api", "ecr.dkr", "secretsmanager", "logs", "sts"] }`.
2. In terraform/modules/vpc-secure/main.tf:57-67 give aws_eip.nat and aws_nat_gateway.this `count = var.nat_gateway_per_az ? length(var.public_subnets) : 1`, with subnet_id = aws_subnet.public[count.index].id and per-index Name tags.
3. Replace the single aws_route_table.private (:69-76) with `count = length(var.private_subnets)`, each routing 0.0.0.0/0 to `aws_nat_gateway.this[var.nat_gateway_per_az ? count.index : 0].id`, and point aws_route_table_association.private (:78-82) at aws_route_table.private[count.index].id. This assumes private_subnets[i] and public_subnets[i] share azs[i], which the module already does via element(var.azs, count.index); add a validation that the two lists have equal length.
4. Add `moved` blocks (aws_eip.nat -> aws_eip.nat[0], aws_nat_gateway.this -> aws_nat_gateway.this[0], aws_route_table.private -> aws_route_table.private[0]) so a plan against any existing state does not destroy and recreate the egress path.
5. Change the S3 gateway endpoint (:96) to `route_table_ids = aws_route_table.private[*].id`.
6. Replace the single aws_vpc_endpoint.kms (:102-110) with `resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "interface" { for_each = toset(var.interface_endpoints) ... service_name = "com.amazonaws.${var.region}.${each.key}", vpc_endpoint_type = "Interface", subnet_ids = aws_subnet.private[*].id, security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.endpoint.id], private_dns_enabled = true }` plus `moved { from = aws_vpc_endpoint.kms  to = aws_vpc_endpoint.interface["kms"] }`. Update the KMS assertions in tests/private_paths.tftest.hcl to the new address.
7. Expose nat_gateway_per_az in terraform/stack/variables.tf and pass it into module "vpc" at terraform/stack/main.tf:15-24; set true in terraform/environments/production and allow staging to set false for cost.
8. Extend terraform/modules/vpc-secure/tests/private_paths.tftest.hcl, running it against HEAD's main.tf first and keeping the failing output: length(aws_nat_gateway.this) == length(var.public_subnets); each aws_route_table.private[i] routes to the NAT whose subnet is public[i]; the S3 endpoint is associated with every private route table; aws_vpc_endpoint.interface contains ecr.api, ecr.dkr, secretsmanager, logs and sts with private_dns_enabled = true. terraform-tests.yml already runs this module.

findings.title: API still runs on 1 vCPU, now shared with clamd, with no autoscaling, no converter concurrency cap, no stopTimeout/initProcessEnabled/NODE_OPTIONS
findings.evidenceAtHead: Repo-wide grep for appautoscaling/aws_appautoscaling in *.tf/*.yml/*.ts: no hits. terraform/environments/production/variables.tf:36-46: api_cpu=1024, api_memory=6144 (2048 at 92ccdba1). staging/variables.tf:36-47: 1024/6144 (was 512/1024). The memory increase came from 9c335454d, which added a clamav container to the same task: terraform/modules/ecs-fargate/main.tf:213-268, with a hard limit var.scanner_memory=4096 (variables.tf:59-63). terraform/stack/main.tf:226 only guarantees the app 2048 MiB, the same floor as before. The single vCPU is now shared by Node, clamd scans and freshclam reloads, LibreOffice, ocrmypdf/tesseract and the veraPDF JRE (Dockerfile.optimized:52-76). The API container (ecs-fargate/main.tf:142-212) has no stopTimeout, no linuxParameters.initProcessEnabled and no NODE_OPTIONS; NODE_OPTIONS appears nowhere in terraform/ or deploy-aws.yml. Dockerfile.optimized:272 is CMD ["npm","run","start"], so npm runs as PID 1. Converters spawn a process on every call with no cap: server/services/pdf-converter.ts:117-138 (runLibreOffice), server/services/docx-pdf-pipeline.ts:44-74, server/integrations/ocrmypdf/client.ts, server/services/ectd/pdfa-pipeline.ts; grep for concurren/semaphore/queue in them finds nothing. The aws_ecs_service.api lifecycle (main.tf:361-363) ignores task_definition only, not desired_count. gh api repos/.../actions/workflows/deploy-aws.yml/runs reports total_count=0: the stack has never been deployed.
findings.remaining: Everything in the original fix. Production and staging are still 1 vCPU, now shared with a co-located clamd, so CPU headroom is worse than at the audit. The app's memory floor is still 2048 MiB. There is no autoscaling target or policy, no converter semaphore, no stopTimeout, no initProcessEnabled and no NODE_OPTIONS heap cap, and npm is PID 1.
findings.severityRationale: Pilot traffic is small, so autoscaling alone could wait for GA (P2). The CPU part cannot. One vCPU now carries clamd plus uncapped LibreOffice, OCR and veraPDF children. One submission-package PDF/A pass or OCR job can starve the event loop. The container health check (node http GET /healthz, 10 s timeout, 3 retries) then fails, and ECS replaces the task mid-job, dropping every live session on it. Right-sizing to 2 vCPU, capping converters and setting stopTimeout are cheap and must land before pilot users rely on it.
findings.humanTestingNote: Testers will not see this locally or on docker-compose staging. The ECS sizing applies only to the AWS stack, which has never been deployed (deploy-aws.yml has 0 runs). The missing converter cap can show on any small shared box: when several testers run DOCX->PDF, OCR or PDF/A conversions at once, every page slows down or conversions time out. Workaround: stagger conversion-heavy test cases.
findings.instructions:
1. terraform/environments/production/variables.tf:36-39 and staging/variables.tf:36-41: set api_cpu default to 2048. Keep api_memory at 6144, or raise it to 8192 so the app gets 4096 beside clamd's 4096. Mirror both values in each env's terraform.tfvars.example (production lines 43-46). In terraform/stack/main.tf, beside the scanner precondition at line 226, add a precondition: var.environment != "production" || var.api_cpu >= 2048.
2. terraform/modules/ecs-fargate/main.tf API container (line 142 onward):
   a. Add stopTimeout = 60. That covers server/startup/shutdown.ts FORCE_EXIT_MS 12 s plus the ALB deregistration_delay of 30 s (modules/alb/main.tf:112).
   b. Add linuxParameters = { initProcessEnabled = true } so soffice and ocrmypdf zombies are reaped and SIGTERM is forwarded.
   c. Add memoryReservation = var.api_memory - var.scanner_memory.
   d. Prepend { name = "NODE_OPTIONS", value = "--max-old-space-size=${floor((var.api_memory - var.scanner_memory) * 0.6)}" } to environment.
3. Dockerfile.optimized:272: replace CMD ["npm","run","start"] with ENV NODE_ENV=production plus CMD ["node","dist/index.js"], so node gets SIGTERM directly. Keep package.json:40 for local use.
4. Create one canonical limiter, server/services/conversion-slots.ts, exporting withConversionSlot<T>(kind, fn). It is a FIFO semaphore sized by CONVERTER_MAX_CONCURRENCY (default 2), with a bounded queue wait (CONVERTER_QUEUE_TIMEOUT_MS, default 120000). When the wait expires it throws a typed ConversionCapacityError, which routes map to 503 with Retry-After. Fail closed: never drop the request silently and never return an empty result. Wrap every child-process converter in it: runLibreOffice (pdf-converter.ts:117), the python3 spawn in docx-pdf-pipeline.ts:59, the ocrmypdf client (server/integrations/ocrmypdf/client.ts, also pass --jobs 1), and the veraPDF/ghostscript calls in server/services/ectd/pdfa-pipeline.ts. Do not add a second limiter anywhere.
5. Autoscaling in modules/ecs-fargate:
   a. Add aws_appautoscaling_target (service/${cluster}/${service}, min_capacity = var.api_desired_count, max_capacity = new var.api_max_count with default 6).
   b. Add two aws_appautoscaling_policy TargetTrackingScaling policies: ECSServiceAverageCPUUtilization target 60, and ALBRequestCountPerTarget. The second needs resource_label from new outputs alb_arn_suffix and api_target_group_arn_suffix in terraform/modules/alb/outputs.tf.
   c. Change the lifecycle at main.tf:361-363 to ignore_changes = [task_definition, desired_count].
   d. Before raising max above 2, confirm that every in-process scheduler goes through server/db/scheduledOnce.ts (OPS-07), because each added task starts every scheduler.
6. Tests, made to fail first:
   a. Add runs to terraform/stack/tests/boot_contract.tftest.hcl asserting production api_cpu >= 2048, API stopTimeout = 60, initProcessEnabled = true, NODE_OPTIONS present, and the autoscaling target min = 2 and max = 6. Run terraform test in terraform/stack at HEAD and record the failures, then implement.
   b. Add server/services/__tests__/conversion-slots.test.ts. With CONVERTER_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2, fire 5 concurrent conversions against a mocked spawn and assert that no more than 2 children are ever alive and that a wait past the timeout rejects with ConversionCapacityError. Show it failing against HEAD's uncapped path first.
7. All work on concept2cure-v2; merge, never rebase.
findings.acceptance: (a) terraform test in terraform/stack fails at HEAD on the new boot_contract runs (cpu 1024; no stopTimeout, initProcessEnabled, NODE_OPTIONS or autoscaling target) and passes after the change. (b) conversion-slots.test.ts fails against HEAD and passes after: peak concurrency is at most CONVERTER_MAX_CONCURRENCY, and a queue timeout returns 503 with Retry-After, never an empty result. (c) On the first AWS staging or prod deployment, a load test of 20 concurrent DOCX->PDF conversions plus 2 OCR jobs: no task stops with OutOfMemory or a failed health check (aws ecs describe-tasks stoppedReason), /healthz stays 200, and the service scales out by at least one task within 5 minutes.
findings.dependencies: First AWS deploy (deploy-aws.yml has never run) for the load-test part. OPS-07 scheduler singleton (server/db/scheduledOnce.ts adoption) before max_capacity > 2. OPS-17 async long jobs reduce the pressure but are not required.

findings.title: Disaster recovery still unproven: no AWS Backup or cross-region copy, no vault replication or lock, no signing-key replica, RPO/RTO TBD, drill uses a fixture
findings.evidenceAtHead: Repo-wide grep for aws_backup/aws_backup_plan/replication_configuration/aws_s3_bucket_replication/aws_kms_replica/aws_db_instance_automated_backups_replication: no hits. terraform/stack/vault_storage.tf:76-150: the vault bucket is versioned and SSE-KMS, with no object lock and no replication; the task role holds s3:DeleteObject. terraform/stack/release_signing.tf:45 has multi_region = true and no replica resource anywhere. terraform/stack/database_keys.tf:36-42: the new RDS CMK is single-region, so a cross-region snapshot copy would need a destination-region key that does not exist. terraform/modules/rds/main.tf:46-54: Multi-AZ, deletion protection, final snapshot, backup_retention 35 d in prod (environments/production/main.tf:60), and nothing beyond in-region automated backups. scripts/ops/dr-restore-drill.sh:73-112 still seeds and restores scripts/ops/dr-fixture.sql (dr_proof.* schema). .github/workflows/database-dr-restore-proof.yml:30-32 runs it against a postgres:16 service container, while RDS runs major 15 (environments/production/main.tf:55). docs/operations/database-disaster-recovery.md:72-76 lists Production RPO, RTO, PITR policy and KMS break-glass as 'TBD'. The vault key policy (vault_storage.tf:37-67) still denies humans decrypt, and no break-glass SOP exists.
findings.remaining: Every item of the original fix. RDS has in-region automated backups/PITR (35 d), Multi-AZ, deletion protection and a final snapshot, but no restore has ever been exercised against RDS. There is no AWS Backup plan or vault lock, no cross-region copy, no CRR for the vault or evidence buckets, no vault object lock, no replica for the multi-region signing key and no KMS break-glass SOP. RPO/RTO are undefined.
findings.severityRationale: GxP buyers ask for tested backup and restore (21 CFR 11.10(c) records protection; Annex 11 section 7.2 requires periodically tested backups). The pilot needs a demonstrated RDS PITR restore plus vault-object recovery and stated RPO/RTO before customers rely on it. Cross-region copy, CRR and an AWS Backup vault lock can follow at GA (P2), but the tested-restore core is P1.
findings.instructions:
1. Founder decisions first, recorded in docs/operations/database-disaster-recovery.md:66-78: DR region, production RPO and RTO, backup retention and legal hold, service owner, drill operator, and key-access approvers.
2. Before the first terraform apply (the stack has never been applied; changing an RDS storage key later replaces the instance, as database_keys.tf:13-15 notes):
   a. Set multi_region = true on aws_kms_key.database (database_keys.tf:36) and aws_kms_key.vault (vault_storage.tf:33).
   b. Add a provider alias aws.dr (var.dr_region) in terraform/environments/{production,staging}/main.tf and pass it into terraform/stack via configuration_aliases in stack/versions.tf.
   c. Add aws_kms_replica_key resources in the DR region for database, vault and release_signing (release_signing.tf:41). Each replica carries the same key policy as its primary.
3. Create terraform/modules/backup:
   a. aws_backup_vault (primary region, KMS = database key) with aws_backup_vault_lock_configuration (COMPLIANCE after a changeable_for_days grace period, min_retention_days = the approved retention).
   b. A DR-region aws_backup_vault, also locked.
   c. aws_backup_plan with a daily rule, lifecycle delete_after = the approved retention, and copy_action to the DR vault.
   d. aws_backup_selection naming the RDS instance ARN (module.rds output) and the vault and evidence bucket ARNs. AWS Backup for S3 requires versioning, which both buckets have.
   e. An IAM role for AWS Backup.
   Wire the module from terraform/stack/main.tf.
4. Add aws_s3_bucket_replication_configuration:
   a. For the vault bucket (vault_storage.tf) and, inside modules/compliance-evidence, for the evidence bucket.
   b. Destination buckets in the DR region: versioned, SSE-KMS under the replica keys, and for evidence, object lock COMPLIANCE with the same retention. The evidence bucket's Deny statements must not block the replication role.
   c. A replication IAM role.
   Decide with the records owner whether the vault bucket gets object lock in GOVERNANCE mode. It can be enabled on the existing versioned bucket with aws_s3_bucket_object_lock_configuration.
5. Write docs/operations/kms-break-glass.md. It names the dual-control key-policy change that temporarily grants a named restore role kms:Decrypt on the vault key (vault_storage.tf:37-67), how CloudTrail records it, and how it is reverted. Reference it from the DR runbook.
6. Add a real restore drill as .github/workflows/staging-rds-pitr-drill.yml (workflow_dispatch plus quarterly schedule), using an OIDC role from modules/github-deploy-roles scoped to the staging RDS identifier. It must:
   a. Run rds restore-db-instance-to-point-in-time into a temporary instance, timing it.
   b. Run scripts/db/deploy-migrate.mjs in check-only mode and a read probe under app_service against the restored instance (extend scripts/ops/dr-application-readiness.mjs so it is not limited to dr_proof.*).
   c. Restore one noncurrent vault object version and verify its SHA-256 against vault.documents.
   d. Record measured RPO/RTO and delete the temporary instance in an always() step.
   Also align the fixture drill's container to postgres:15 to match RDS.
7. Tests, made to fail first: add terraform tests (terraform/stack/tests/dr.tftest.hcl) asserting the backup plan has copy_action to the DR region, the vault lock exists, both buckets have replication rules, and replica keys exist for database, vault and release_signing. Run them at HEAD and record the failures.
8. All work on concept2cure-v2; merge, never rebase.
findings.acceptance: (a) The new terraform tests fail at HEAD (no backup plan, replication or replica keys) and pass after. (b) The staging PITR drill workflow completes green and uploads evidence with restore start and finish timestamps, observed RPO and RTO, the migration level of the restored DB, an app_service read probe result, and one restored vault object whose hash matches vault.documents. (c) The drill is shown failing once by pointing it at a nonexistent restore time or a corrupted object hash. (d) The RPO/RTO and owner rows in docs/operations/database-disaster-recovery.md are filled and approved. (e) aws backup list-recovery-points-by-backup-vault in the DR region shows copies within 24 h of first apply.
findings.dependencies: Founder: DR region, RPO/RTO, retention, approvers. A first AWS apply and a staging environment in AWS (deploy-aws.yml has 0 runs; WO-4 staging promotion). Key multi-region changes must land before the first apply.

findings.title: SOC 2 AWS baseline still absent: no GuardDuty, Security Hub, Config, VPC flow logs, ALB/CloudFront/S3 access logs, WAF or budgets
findings.evidenceAtHead: Repo-wide grep for aws_guardduty, aws_securityhub, aws_config_, aws_flow_log, aws_wafv2, aws_budgets, logging_config and aws_s3_bucket_logging in *.tf: no hits. terraform/modules/alb/variables.tf:40-43: access_logs_bucket still defaults to "" (alb/main.tf:41-44 enabled = var.access_logs_bucket != ""), and terraform/stack/main.tf:363-374 module "alb" does not pass it. terraform/modules/cloudfront/main.tf:149-156 still says 'No WAF yet: a founder decision', with #trivy:ignore:AWS-0011 on the distribution and no logging_config. terraform/modules/vpc-secure/main.tf resources (lines 4-132) include no flow log. terraform/bootstrap/ holds only main.tf and variables.tf, with none of these. The only detective controls at HEAD are the CloudTrail multi-region trail (compliance-evidence/main.tf:316), RDS logs and pgaudit (rds/main.tf:61, 116-120). Both existed or are DB-level and are not part of this finding.
findings.remaining: All listed controls: GuardDuty (including ECS runtime, S3 and RDS protection), Security Hub with FSBP and CIS, AWS Config recorder, VPC flow logs, ALB access logs, CloudFront and S3 server access logging, WAF (count mode first) and budgets with alerts.
findings.severityRationale: A design partner's security questionnaire will ask for threat detection and edge or access logs. More concretely, without ALB, CloudFront or flow logs and GuardDuty, a pilot-era incident cannot be scoped, which is a data-integrity and legal exposure for GxP records. GuardDuty, access logs, flow logs and budgets are cheap and are P1. Security Hub and Config scoring, and switching WAF from count to block, can be P2 for GA.
findings.instructions:
1. Founder decisions: whether staging and prod share one AWS account (this decides where account-level resources live), WAF budget and posture, budget ceiling and alert recipients.
2. Account-level controls go in terraform/bootstrap/main.tf, or in a new terraform/modules/security-baseline instantiated once per account behind var.manage_account_baseline. Do not instantiate them per environment in a shared account. They are:
   a. aws_guardduty_detector with features S3_DATA_EVENTS, RDS_LOGIN_EVENTS and RUNTIME_MONITORING (ECS_FARGATE_AGENT_MANAGEMENT).
   b. aws_securityhub_account plus aws_securityhub_standards_subscription for AWS Foundational Security Best Practices and CIS AWS Foundations.
   c. aws_config_configuration_recorder (all supported resources), aws_config_delivery_channel to a dedicated, KMS-encrypted log bucket, and aws_config_configuration_recorder_status enabled.
   d. aws_budgets_budget, monthly COST, with 80% and 100% notifications to the named recipients.
3. VPC flow logs: in terraform/modules/vpc-secure/main.tf, add an aws_cloudwatch_log_group (KMS-encrypted, 365-day retention), an IAM role and aws_flow_log { vpc_id = aws_vpc.this.id, traffic_type = "ALL" }.
4. ALB access logs:
   a. In terraform/stack, create a log bucket. Use SSE-S3, because ALB access logs do not support SSE-KMS. Add a public-access block, lifecycle retention, and a bucket policy allowing logdelivery.elasticloadbalancing.amazonaws.com (or the region's ELB account) to PutObject under AWSLogs/<account>/.
   b. Pass access_logs_bucket into module "alb" at terraform/stack/main.tf:363-374.
   c. Add a stack precondition that production sets it.
5. CloudFront and S3 logging:
   a. Add a logging_config block to aws_cloudfront_distribution.this (cloudfront/main.tf:157). Its target bucket needs ACLs enabled (BucketOwnerPreferred). Alternatively use CloudFront v2 logging via aws_cloudwatch_log_delivery_source/destination/delivery.
   b. Add aws_s3_bucket_logging for the vault bucket (vault_storage.tf) and the frontend bucket to a separate log bucket.
   c. Never set the evidence bucket's logging target to itself. compliance-evidence/main.tf:1-15 documents the recursive-logging loop already fixed once.
6. WAF:
   a. Add aws_wafv2_web_acl with scope CLOUDFRONT, created through a us-east-1 provider alias. Include AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet with override_action { count {} }, AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputsRuleSet, and a rate-based rule on /api/auth/*.
   b. Set web_acl_id on the distribution.
   c. Delete the #trivy:ignore:AWS-0011 and the 'No WAF yet' comment at cloudfront/main.tf:149-156 in the same change.
   d. Only after reviewing counted matches against document uploads (bodies over 8 KB) and AnA turns, switch to block with a SizeRestrictions_BODY scope-down exclusion.
7. Tests, made to fail first:
   a. Add tftest runs: modules/vpc-secure/tests asserting the flow log, modules/alb/tests asserting access_logs.enabled = true when a bucket is passed, the stack test asserting production passes a non-empty access_logs_bucket, cloudfront tests asserting logging_config and web_acl_id, and a security-baseline module test.
   b. Run them at HEAD and record the failures.
   c. Move terraform-compliance.yml (Checkov) to trigger on push to concept2cure-v2 (Rule 0 means no PRs), so these controls stay gated.
8. All work on concept2cure-v2; merge, never rebase.
findings.acceptance: (a) The new tftest runs fail at HEAD and pass after the change. (b) After apply: aws guardduty create-sample-findings produces a finding visible in Security Hub, and the Security Hub FSBP and CIS scores are exported to docs/evidence. (c) Flow-log, ALB and CloudFront log objects appear within 15 minutes of a smoke test. (d) A budget notification test fires to the named recipient. findings.title: API task still carries the RDS master (owner) DATABASE_URL and APP_SERVICE_DB_PASSWORD; boot DDL and one route still run on the owner connection
findings.evidenceAtHead: terraform/stack/main.tf:39-48 calls DATABASE_URL the owner role, used by migrations and by the API at boot, and labels it 'A known exposure'. main.tf:93 builds database_url from module.rds.master_username and random_password.db_master. main.tf:315-316: DATABASE_URL is in local.boot_secrets, which feeds both api_secrets (line 431) and worker_secrets (line 440). main.tf:432 adds APP_SERVICE_DB_PASSWORD to the API task. .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml:514 preflight REQUIRES DATABASE_URL in the API container. scripts/ops/ecs-one-off-task.sh:68-92 derives the migrate task by cloning the API's checked revision, which is why the owner secrets sit in the API definition. Runtime owner use: server/startup/services.ts:130 ensureCoreTables(process.env.DATABASE_URL) runs CREATE SCHEMA/EXTENSION/TABLE (server/db/ensureCoreTables.ts:348-541). server/startup/services.ts:278-279 ensureAuthTables opens an owner Pool (server/db/bootstrap/index.ts:33-43) for DDL plus seeds. server/routes/tenants-simple.ts:67-75 builds a postgres() client on DATABASE_URL that serves /api/tenants requests outside RLS. server/startup/env.ts:66-68 makes DATABASE_URL mandatory at boot. Rotation (5ef2787a5, var.db_credentials_rotation) changes the password, not who holds it.
findings.remaining: The API (and worker) task definitions still receive the master or owner URL and the app_service password. The API still runs DDL at boot and serves tenants-simple routes through an owner client. The deploy preflight still requires the owner URL in the API task, and the migrate task is still derived from the API definition.
findings.severityRationale: An RCE or SSRF-to-env leak in the web tier yields the RDS master credential: owner of every table, RLS bypassed, able to drop the audit tables. That defeats tenant isolation and Part 11 audit immutability in one step. The tenants-simple route also runs live requests through the owner connection, so a logic bug there bypasses RLS without needing RCE. It needs a preceding compromise or bug, so P1 rather than P0, but it must be closed before pilot data lands.
findings.instructions:
1. Move boot DDL into the migration set (Rule 1).
   a. Translate every CREATE SCHEMA/EXTENSION/TABLE IF NOT EXISTS in server/db/ensureCoreTables.ts (about lines 395-541) and in server/db/bootstrap/auth-schema.ts (applyAuthSchemaMigrations, applyModuleCatalogSchema) into additive, IF NOT EXISTS-guarded migration files.
   b. Append them to C2C_MIGRATION_FILES in scripts/db/migration-set.mjs, before the final RLS sweep pair (ci:migration-set-order enforces that).
   c. Tables that already exist keep their shape. Any genuinely new table goes in public with organization_id INTEGER NOT NULL.
   d. Move seedOrganizations into a migration using INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING with a row-count assertion. Make seedGaDemoUser (server/db/bootstrap/seed-default-org.ts:138) refuse to run when NODE_ENV=production.
   e. Run npm run ci:migration-drop-safety and ci:migration-set-order.
2. Make API boot read-only on the runtime role.
   a. server/startup/services.ts:130: call a verify-only variant of ensureCoreTables (no DDL) on getRuntimeDatabaseUrl().
   b. server/startup/services.ts:278-279: replace ensureAuthTables() with a schema-presence check that reports readiness 'error' when columns are missing.
   c. Keep the DDL paths reachable only from scripts/db/deploy-migrate.mjs.
   d. server/startup/env.ts:66-68: in production require APP_DATABASE_URL and do NOT require DATABASE_URL.
3. server/routes/tenants-simple.ts:67-75: delete the module-level postgres() owner client and serve the routes through the runtime pool. Use runWithSystemTenantScope for platform-admin estate reads and the org-scoped connection for tenant reads, as the rest of server/routes does. Keep server/__tests__/security/tenant-isolation-tenants-simple.contract.test.ts passing. server/services/ana-cortex-service.ts:57 only inspects the string: change it to report APP_DATABASE_URL presence.
4. Terraform.
   a. terraform/stack/main.tf:315-316: remove DATABASE_URL from local.boot_secrets. Add local.owner_secrets = [DATABASE_URL, APP_SERVICE_DB_PASSWORD].
   b. Remove APP_SERVICE_DB_PASSWORD from api_secrets (line 432).
   c. In terraform/modules/ecs-fargate, add aws_ecs_task_definition.migrate (family ${cluster_name}-migrate, one container, no clamav sidecar) whose secrets are boot_secrets plus owner_secrets.
   d. Give the migrate definition its own execution role, allowed GetSecretValue on the owner secret ARNs. Remove those ARNs from the API execution role's policy (ecs-fargate/main.tf:51-73) by splitting var.secret_arns into api and migrate lists.
   e. Add the migrate execution role to pass_role_arns and the migrate family to one_off_task_families in modules/github-deploy-roles (main.tf:104-112).
   f. Add ignore_changes on the image field only if the deploy registers revisions of it.
5. scripts/ops/ecs-one-off-task.sh:68-92: derive the one-off task from the Terraform-owned migrate family's latest revision with only the image replaced by the checked digest, instead of from the API revision. Keep the ARN race check in deploy-aws.yml.
6. .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml:514-541 preflight:
   a. Remove DATABASE_URL from the required list for the API container.
   b. Add a refusal when the API container carries DATABASE_URL or APP_SERVICE_DB_PASSWORD.
   c. Add a separate check that the migrate family carries both.
   d. Update the comment at lines 443-449.
