findings.title: CloudFront and the ALB now both wait 60 s, but eCTD compile/assemble still run synchronously and 7 SSE producers plus the MCP transport send no heartbeat, so anything over 60 s is still cut off
findings.evidenceAtHead: FIXED half (commit 9cb30bda8, 2026-10-01): terraform/modules/cloudfront/main.tf:186 `origin_read_timeout = 60` on the alb-api custom origin; terraform/modules/alb/main.tf:36 `idle_timeout = 60` (now explicit); server/index.ts:247-248 keepAliveTimeout 65 s / headersTimeout 66 s sit above both. terraform/modules/cloudfront/tests/alb_origin.tftest.hcl:149-164 asserts origin_read_timeout == 60, and terraform-tests.yml runs modules/cloudfront on push (latest run 2026-10-05 success, mocked provider). No test asserts the ALB idle_timeout (terraform/modules/alb/tests has only cloudfront_only.tftest.hcl). The env roots (terraform/environments/{staging,production}/main.tf:42-43) both use ../../stack, so staging gets the same values. OPEN half: (1) Long work is still synchronous in the request. server/routes/ectd-compile.ts:532 POST /:projectIdent/compile assembles the package inline, including PDF/A normalization of every PDF leaf (comment at :1181), and answers only at res.json(result) :1276. server/routes/submission-ops.ts:2345 POST /packages/:packageId/assemble builds leaf PDFs and the zip inline (:2621, :2728, :2974-3091) and answers at :3278. server/routes/submissions.ts:1701 POST /sequences/:seqId/assemble is also inline. server/routes/ectd-export.ts:567 is inline. server/services/docx-pdf-pipeline.ts:14 defaults to 120_000 ms, which is longer than the 60 s edge. No route returns 202 for these; the commit itself says the route half was 'handed on'. The v2 client calls them synchronously: client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/EctdCompile.tsx:1039, GatewayTransmittals.tsx:681, SequenceAssembleTestPackage.tsx:132. (2) SSE heartbeats. 10 server files produce text/event-stream. Three keep the stream alive: ana-ri/stream.ts:845-858 (15 s ': heartbeat'), services/ai-actions/sse-stream.ts:36,114-121 (15 s keepalive, which was already present at 92ccdba1, so the audit's 'only ana-ri' was slightly understated), and contentAssembly.routes.ts:271 (5 s updates). Seven have no heartbeat: ana-features.ts:4948 (submission-chat/stream), ana-intelligence.ts:213 (draft/stream), cortex-unified.ts:526, deep-research.ts:137 (job progress stream), fieldSync.routes.ts:326, ind.ts:372, submissions.ts:1295 (sections/generate). A grep of client/src found no v2 caller for any of the seven; DeepResearch.tsx polls GET /jobs/:id instead. (3) The remote MCP connector: server/mcp/index.ts:174 uses a stateless StreamableHTTPServerTransport, which answers with an SSE stream by default. Its model-backed tools (server/mcp/tools/drafting.ts:27,70; intelligence.ts:14) send no progress notifications and have no timeout (a grep of server/mcp found neither). Durations are still UNVERIFIED: no measured compile or assemble time exists for a pilot-sized package on the production image.
findings.fixedBy: 9cb30bda8: terraform/modules/cloudfront/main.tf:186 (origin_read_timeout = 60), terraform/modules/alb/main.tf:36 (idle_timeout = 60), terraform/modules/cloudfront/tests/alb_origin.tftest.hcl:149-164
findings.remaining: Any request whose response takes more than 60 s still returns a CloudFront 504, and the server keeps going and records the work anyway. 60 s is CloudFront's ceiling without an AWS quota increase. Exposed paths: eCTD compile (inline PDF/A per leaf), package assemble, sequence assemble, eCTD export, and any DOCX→PDF on a route, whose pipeline limit is 120 s. None of these is async yet, so the 504 discards the compile verdict and blockers, which arrive only in the response body. A retry recompiles and records again. The seven SSE producers without a heartbeat are cut after 60 s of silence, but none has a v2 client caller today. MCP drafting/premortem tool calls over 60 s are cut at the edge. The ALB idle_timeout has no test. Real durations have not been measured.
findings.severityRationale: The 30–60 s band the audit worried about is closed. What remains sits on the core Submission Center journey (compile and assemble of a real IND, with PDF/A normalization of every leaf inline), so a pilot user who hits a 504 loses the compile verdict, and a retry produces duplicate recorded compilations. Durations are UNVERIFIED. If timing a 50- and 200-leaf package on the production image shows p95 well under 45 s, this drops to P2.
findings.humanTestingNote: Local runs have no CloudFront or ALB, so testers will not see this there. On a staging deployment behind CloudFront: in the Submission Center, 'Compile' (eCTD Compile surface), 'Assemble test package' or Gateway package 'Assemble' on a package big enough to take more than 60 s shows a Gateway Timeout or generic request error. The server finishes and records the compile anyway. Workaround: use small packages (a few leaves) when testing on staging. After a timeout, open the compile history (GET /api/ectd-compile/:projectIdent/history, shown on the compile surface) rather than re-running. Log a timeout as 'edge timeout', not as a compile failure. AnA chat is not affected because its stream (ana-ri) sends a heartbeat every 15 s.
findings.instructions:
1. Measure before building. Build the production image (Dockerfile.optimized) and run it against a seeded database with Ghostscript and veraPDF present. Time POST /api/ectd-compile/:projectIdent/compile, POST /api/submission-ops/packages/:packageId/assemble, POST /api/submissions/sequences/:seqId/assemble and POST /api/ectd-export/:submissionId for an FDA IND sequence with 50 leaves and with 200 leaves. Record p50 and p95 for each, plus the image digest, under docs/evidence/D1/<date>-edge-timeouts/. If every p95 is under 45 s, record that, skip steps 3-5, and keep steps 2 and 6-8.
2. Pin the ALB half. Add a run to terraform/modules/alb/tests/cloudfront_only.tftest.hcl, or a new alb_timeouts.tftest.hcl, that asserts `aws_lb.this.idle_timeout == 60`. Make it fail first: temporarily set terraform/modules/alb/main.tf:36 to 59, run `terraform test` in terraform/modules/alb, see it fail, restore 60 and see it pass. Add a stack-level assertion that server keepAliveTimeout (server/index.ts:247, 65_000) > ALB idle_timeout. A small vitest in tests/ci/ that reads both files is enough.
3. Make compile asynchronous. Do not create a new job table; reuse the existing tenant-scoped public.artifact_compute_jobs (db/migrations/20260326_artifact_compute_plane.sql:18, already in C2C_MIGRATION_FILES at scripts/db/migration-set.mjs:792; organization_id INTEGER NOT NULL), with surface_key 'ectd-compile' and a runtime_profile_key seeded in that same file's profile INSERT. Any seed change is an in-place amendment with a dated header note (Rule 1). Split server/routes/ectd-compile.ts:532 so the handler validates and resolves the anchor/spine exactly as today. It then inserts the job row with organization_id and the requesting user, starts the existing compileFromSpine/assembly body detached from the response, and returns 202 {jobId}. On finish, the job writes the full CompilationResult (the object built at :1242-1270) into result_summary and sets status 'completed' or 'failed'. A thrown error is stored as status 'failed' with the error and never as an empty result (fail closed). Add GET /api/ectd-compile/:projectIdent/jobs/:jobId. It reads the row filtered by organization_id from the session, never from the request, and returns 404 for a foreign tenant's job.
4. Apply the same 202+poll split to server/routes/submission-ops.ts:2345 (packages/:packageId/assemble) and server/routes/submissions.ts:1701 (sequences/:seqId/assemble, dry run), and to server/routes/ectd-export.ts:567 if step 1 shows it can exceed 45 s. Keep one implementation per capability (Zero duplication): move the existing inline body into a service function that both the job runner and any test call; delete the inline copy.
5. Update the v2 callers to post, then poll every 2 s until a terminal state, showing elapsed time and keeping the existing result rendering: client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/EctdCompile.tsx:1039, GatewayTransmittals.tsx:681 and SequenceAssembleTestPackage.tsx:132. A poll error renders as an error state, never as an empty result. Add a stale-job sweep: a running row older than timeout_seconds becomes 'failed: abandoned (task restarted)'. Run the sweep under the advisory-lock pattern used for background jobs (commit 03dbeaf51) so two API replicas do not both run it.
6. SSE: create one helper, e.g. server/utils/sse-stream.ts openSseStream(req, res). It sets Content-Type text/event-stream, Cache-Control no-cache no-transform, X-Accel-Buffering no; flushes headers; writes ': heartbeat\n\n' every 15 s; clears the interval on req/res 'close'. Use the logic already in server/services/ai-actions/sse-stream.ts:36-142 and server/routes/ana-ri/stream.ts:837-859. Migrate all 10 producers onto it, including those two, and delete their private copies (Zero duplication): ana-features.ts:4948, ana-intelligence.ts:213, contentAssembly.routes.ts:256, cortex-unified.ts:526, deep-research.ts:137, fieldSync.routes.ts:326, ind.ts:372, submissions.ts:1295. If a producer turns out to be unreachable and is deleted instead, the commit must name the replacement path, per the CLAUDE.md working agreement.
7. Add a guard scripts/ci/check-sse-heartbeat.mjs (npm script ci:sse-heartbeat, plus a :selftest). It fails when any server file outside the helper sets text/event-stream. The selftest feeds it a fixture that sets the header directly and asserts exit 1. Wire the guard into ci.yml's lint job and .husky/pre-push next to the other static guards (around line 560).
8. MCP: for tools that can exceed 45 s (server/mcp/tools/drafting.ts c2c_draft_cover_letter and c2c_draft_agency_response; intelligence.ts c2c_run_crl_premortem), send notifications/progress every 15 s when the request carries _meta.progressToken. Give each a 50 s server-side deadline that returns an isError tool result such as 'did not finish within the connector's time limit; continue in the app', never a partial draft presented as complete.
9. Optional, founder/AWS: if step 1 shows the work cannot be made async before the pilot, request the CloudFront 'response timeout per origin' quota increase. Then raise origin_read_timeout and the ALB idle_timeout together, and raise server/index.ts keepAliveTimeout and headersTimeout above both. Update the two tftests.
10. All work lands on concept2cure-v2 directly; merge, never rebase (Rule 0).
findings.acceptance: (a) docs/evidence holds measured p50/p95 for compile, package assemble, sequence assemble and export at 50 and 200 leaves on the production image, with the image digest. (b) The new ALB test fails with idle_timeout = 59 and passes with 60; the cloudfront alb_origin test stays green. (c) A route test (vitest, supertest) mocks the assembly service to take 70 s with fake timers and asserts POST /api/ectd-compile/:ident/compile answers 202 with a jobId in under 1 s. This test is written first and seen failing against the current synchronous route (it gets 200 after the mocked delay, or times out). GET .../jobs/:jobId then returns the full CompilationResult with status 'completed'. A second org's session gets 404 for the same jobId. A thrown assembly error yields status 'failed' with the message and never an empty result. (d) The same 202 test passes for submission-ops packages/:packageId/assemble and submissions sequences/:seqId/assemble. (e) ci:sse-heartbeat:selftest exits 1 on the fixture and ci:sse-heartbeat exits 0 on the tree. A vitest on openSseStream with fake timers sees ': heartbeat' written at 15 s and the interval cleared on close. (f) An MCP tool test with a stubbed 70 s model call returns an isError result at the 50 s deadline and emits progress notifications when a progressToken is supplied. (g) On staging behind CloudFront, a 200-leaf compile completes with no 504 in the CloudFront access log.
findings.dependencies: OPS-01 (a CloudFront/ALB deployment to measure on), OPS-09 (the production image's document/PDF-A runtime determines real durations), OPS-13 (task sizing affects durations), OPS-07 (job sweep must run once across replicas).

findings.title: Nothing still gates landing on concept2cure-v2: the branch is unprotected, the pre-push hook runs no tests, Checkov and schema validation are PR-only, the bot still refreshes the baseline, and trunk CI has not been green since 2026-09-23
findings.evidenceAtHead: GitHub API (run 2026-10-13): `gh api repos/concept2cure/ClinicalSageAI-2-replit/branches/concept2cure-v2` → protected=false, required_status_checks enforcement_level 'off'. `.../rulesets` → one ruleset, 11855901 'JMSMITH', enforcement 'disabled', rules deletion and non_fast_forward only. `.../rules/branches/concept2cure-v2` → []. No merge queue is possible without an active ruleset. PR-only workflows have the same triggers as at 92ccdba1: terraform-compliance.yml:3-6 (Checkov, `on: pull_request` paths terraform/**), db-schema-validation.yml:13-18 (drizzle push on an empty DB, pull_request only, and nothing in ci.yml runs drizzle-kit push), test-assembly.yml:3-4, danger.yml, neon-preview-db.yml, pr-checks.yml and ops-audit-plan.yml (PR plus dispatch). pr-checks.yml's gates are all mirrored in ci.yml (checked per script name). Trivy config (ci.yml:2391-2404) does scan IaC on push. .husky/pre-push (707 lines) runs about 35 static guards from line 93 to 697: migration order and drop safety, tenant scope, RLS bypass, SQL interpolation, repo-health ceiling (:587), pushed-file ESLint errors and warnings (:652, :671) and pushed typecheck (:697). It runs no test runner: no vitest, jest or npm test. It is also client-side and bypassable with --no-verify. repo-health-baseline-refresh.yml is unchanged: :17-20 on push to concept2cure-v2, :61-65 commits and pushes the baseline with [skip ci]. `git log --author=github-actions 92ccdba1..HEAD` counts 342 such commits, the latest 696a1d4c8 on 2026-10-13. Partial mitigation added after the audit (f80dc2934): ci.yml:1026-1040 and package.json:363 add audit:repo-health:ceiling, which the bot cannot refresh. It covers oversized files only; other repo-health deltas are still absorbed by the refresh. The nightly-governance job (ci.yml:2459-2558) still ends `exit $failed` over strict gates whose own comment says they are 'EXPECTED to fail', so every scheduled CI run on trunk is red. A post-audit mitigation that gates releases, not landing: deploy-aws.yml:84-143 (ci-verdict, commit 8060c28bc) refuses to deploy a SHA unless ci.yml, semgrep.yml and codeql.yml push runs on it succeeded. Result: `gh api .../actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs?branch=concept2cure-v2&status=success` shows the last green run at 2026-09-23T08:36Z (35838048262). The latest completed push run, 38358525641 (9a59bc8f9, 2026-10-13T06:45Z), failed Lint, Test, Coverage, Integration Tests, Blank DB Provisioning + Deploy Migration ('Deploy migration succeeds on the provisioned database'), Production Boot Smoke ('Provision the schema from scratch') and Production Image Boot; Build and Release evidence were skipped. All 50 completed push runs in the latest 60 failed.
findings.remaining: Everything in the audit's fix list is still open: no server-side pre-land gate (branch unprotected, ruleset disabled, no merge queue), no tests before a push lands, Checkov and drizzle schema validation never run on trunk, the bot baseline auto-refresh still absorbs repo-health regressions, and the nightly strict job still turns CI red by design. A new interaction makes this worse: the bot's [skip ci] commits often become the branch tip, and no CI run exists for such a SHA. A v* tag on the tip therefore makes deploy-aws.yml's ci-verdict wait 90 minutes and refuse. Trunk has had no green CI run for about 3 weeks, so no SHA is deployable today.
findings.severityRationale: This is not itself a pilot-blocking defect: deploy-aws.yml's ci-verdict now keeps a red SHA out of production. But it is the structural reason trunk stays red (OPS-02, P0). The pilot needs a deployable green SHA that stays green while agents push directly to trunk many times a day. Without a pre-land gate, every fix to OPS-02 is undone by the next push.
findings.humanTestingNote: Testers cannot see the missing gate directly, but it decides what they test: a regression can land on trunk between two test builds without anything stopping it. Pin each test environment to one recorded SHA and put that SHA in every bug report. Note that trunk CI currently fails 'Blank DB Provisioning + Deploy Migration' and 'Production Boot Smoke: provision the schema from scratch'. If a fresh test database fails to provision, report it under OPS-02 rather than as a product bug, and reuse an already-provisioned database for that session.
findings.instructions:
1. Founder decision first, written into CLAUDE.md. GitHub required status checks, whether through branch protection or a ruleset, refuse a direct push unless the SHA already has green checks from another ref. A merge queue needs PRs. Both conflict with Rule 0 as written. Choose either (A) amend Rule 0 to allow a merge queue into concept2cure-v2 (short-lived queue refs only) and update .husky/pre-push's agent-branch refusal to match, or (B) keep Rule 0 and make the pre-push hook the pre-land test gate (steps 3-4), with server-side protection limited to history (step 2). Do not ship a change that silently contradicts Rule 0.
2. In GitHub settings (founder/admin; the session token gets 403 on branch protection), enable ruleset 11855901, or create a new one, targeting refs/heads/concept2cure-v2 with 'Restrict deletions' and 'Block force pushes'. This is consistent with Rule 0 (merge, never rebase). Under option A, also add the required checks (Lint, Test, Build, Release evidence gate) and enable merge_group, which ci.yml already listens for (ci.yml:8). Verify with `gh api repos/concept2cure/ClinicalSageAI-2-replit/rules/branches/concept2cure-v2` returning non-empty.
3. Under option B, add scripts/ci/check-pushed-tests.mjs, modelled on scripts/ci/check-pushed-lint-errors.mjs. Take the push range from scripts/ci/lib/push-range.mjs (resolvePushBase, changedSince) and run `vitest related --run --config vitest.config.ts <changed files>`, plus `jest --config scripts/jest.config.js --findRelatedTests <changed files>` for jest-owned paths. Fail closed when the runner exits non-zero, crashes, or produces no parseable JSON report. If a change touches more than about 40 source files or a shared core (shared/schema.ts, server/db.ts, server/middleware/**), run a named fast subset instead and say so: test:submission and test:security from package.json:80-83, plus tests/schema-contract. Add `ci:pushed-tests` and `ci:pushed-tests:selftest` to package.json next to ci:pushed-typecheck (package.json:291).
4. Insert the gate into .husky/pre-push after the typecheck block (around :697), using the same refusal pattern ('🚫 ERROR … exit 1'). The selftest must create a temporary source plus spec pair whose spec fails, run the checker against it, and assert exit 1, then assert exit 0 once the spec passes. Show both outcomes in the commit message.
5. Checkov on push: move the Checkov step from terraform-compliance.yml:28-38 into a new job in terraform-tests.yml (already on push to concept2cure-v2 for terraform/**), with soft_fail: false. Delete terraform-compliance.yml in the same change. Its plan step cannot run without AWS credentials, terraform-tests already runs validate, and the PR-comment step is dead under Rule 0. Because Checkov has not run since 2026-06-15, first run it locally (`checkov -d terraform/ --framework terraform`). Put each existing finding in a .checkov.yaml skip list with a written reason per entry, and extend ci:trivyignore-hygiene, or add a sibling guard, so an entry without a reason fails. Prove the job fails by adding a temporary public S3 bucket fixture.
6. Schema validation on push: add `push: branches: [concept2cure-v2]` with the same paths to db-schema-validation.yml:13-18. Prove it fails by temporarily breaking an FK target in a scratch schema file, then revert. For test-assembly.yml, danger.yml, neon-preview-db.yml, pr-checks.yml and ops-audit-plan.yml: either add a push trigger or delete the workflow, naming in the commit message the ci.yml step that already runs each gate. pr-checks.yml's gates are all already in ci.yml.
7. Remove the auto-refresh: delete .github/workflows/repo-health-baseline-refresh.yml. Make docs/reports/repo-health-scan-latest.json a human-maintained ratchet: CI's `audit:repo-health:no-regression` (ci.yml:1023-1025) fails on growth, the pusher either fixes it or updates the baseline in the same commit with a reason, and the pre-push hook runs the same no-regression check next to audit:repo-health:ceiling (:587). This also stops the [skip ci] tip commits that leave deploy-aws.yml's ci-verdict without a run for the tip SHA. Verify by pushing a commit that adds a duplicate basename and seeing pre-push refuse it.
8. Nightly strict: move the nightly-governance job (ci.yml:2459-2558) into its own workflow file (e.g. governance-nightly.yml, schedule plus dispatch). Its expected failures then stop marking the CI workflow red on trunk, and it keeps its counts and artifact upload.
9. Land on concept2cure-v2 only, merging and never rebasing. These gates only make sense once trunk is green, so do OPS-02 first or in the same window.
findings.acceptance: (a) `gh api repos/concept2cure/ClinicalSageAI-2-replit/rules/branches/concept2cure-v2` lists non_fast_forward and deletion rules, and under option A also required status checks plus a merge queue. A force-push to concept2cure-v2 is refused by GitHub. (b) ci:pushed-tests:selftest exits 1 on its failing fixture and 0 on its passing one. A real push whose change breaks a related vitest is refused by .husky/pre-push, as demonstrated in the commit message, and a docs-only push skips the test step and says so. (c) Checkov runs on a push touching terraform/** and fails on the public-bucket fixture; terraform-compliance.yml no longer exists, and .checkov.yaml has no entry without a reason (its guard fails when one is added). (d) db-schema-validation runs on a push to concept2cure-v2 touching shared/schema.ts. (e) repo-health-baseline-refresh.yml is gone and `git log --author=github-actions` gains no new commits after the change. A push adding a duplicate basename is refused pre-push. (f) Scheduled runs no longer appear as failures of the 'CI' workflow. (g) After OPS-02, ten consecutive push runs of ci.yml on concept2cure-v2 are green, and a v* tag on the tip SHA passes deploy-aws.yml's ci-verdict job.
findings.dependencies: OPS-02 (trunk must be green before required checks or a pre-push test gate are usable). Founder decision on Rule 0 versus a merge queue (step 1). GitHub admin access for the ruleset (step 2).

findings.title: Signing authority is now one enforced check on every signing route and approver/reviewer can be assigned; residuals: SCIM cannot assign signing roles, lock commands have no role gate, admins sign by default
findings.evidenceAtHead: FIXED PART: server/services/part11/signing-authority-gate.ts:44-55 checkSigningAuthority (membership-row role via resolve-signer-role.ts:25-44, fail-closed 503 on lookup error) is now the only authority check. /api/c2c/actions/sign and /revoke-signature ask it before re-auth regardless of GOVERNANCE_RBAC_ENFORCE (server/routes/c2c/actions.ts:113 SIGNATURE_COMMANDS, :667-670 before verifyReauth :673). AnA e-signature tier asks it before reverifySigner (server/routes/ana-ri/governed-esignature.ts:92 then :98). ESG transmit asks it before re-auth (server/routes/mdx-submission-gateway.ts:300 then :303; technical-rejection :546) and executeGovernedTransmit re-asserts it (server/services/submission-gateways/governed-transmit.ts:486 -> governed-transmit-checks.ts:218-232). Authoring freeze/e-sign/sign call it (authoring.router.ts:5037, 5311, 7397). Signing roles are assignable: shared/constants/org-roles.ts:32 ASSIGNABLE_ORG_ROLES = admin, approver, manager, reviewer, member, viewer, used by server/routes/tenant-users.ts:34,48 and the Admin UI (client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/AdminMemberActions.tsx:86); self re-role refused (tenant-users.ts:595 SELF_ROLE_CHANGE). CI: `node scripts/ci/check-sign-ceremony.mjs` -> 'every signer re-verification asks signing authority in its handler; 5 baselined re-authentication(s) sign nothing'; `node scripts/ci/check-sign-ceremony.selftest.mjs` -> 27 passed incl. 'the pre-fix Gateway transmit (re-authentication, no authority) fails the authority rule'. `npx vitest run server/routes/c2c/__tests__/governed-sign-authority.test.ts` -> 8/8 (viewer, member, manager refused 403 before password read, nothing written). STILL OPEN: (a) server/routes/scim.ts:70 VALID_ROLES = ['admin','manager','member','viewer'] - an IdP cannot provision approver/reviewer; (b) lock is not in SIGNATURE_COMMANDS (actions.ts:113) and POST /api/c2c/actions/lock (mounted with authMiddleware only, server/bootstrap/register-inline-routes.ts:347) and POST /api/c2c/documents/:id/lock (server/routes/c2c/documents.ts:942-963, mount :819) re-authenticate but apply no role check, so a viewer with their password can lock; (c) DEFAULT_SIGNING_ROLES still includes 'admin' (server/services/part11/signing-authority.ts:23), override only deployment-wide via ESIGNATURE_SIGNING_ROLES - account administration and signing are not segregated; (d) the per-resource permission gate is still dark behind GOVERNANCE_RBAC_ENFORCE, set nowhere (actions.ts:705-721, governed-signature-ceremony.ts:190).
findings.fixedBy: ddc8c0db5 (approver/reviewer assignable, P-18; shared/constants/org-roles.ts:32, tenant-users.ts:34,48); cf950eeb9 (QMS/action sign route authority); b86baf55e (authority on every signing route); 0f961354c (one checkSigningAuthority, ci:sign-ceremony authority rule; signing-authority-gate.ts:44-55, actions.ts:667-670); 505f71263 (authenticator required to sign outside dev/test)
findings.remaining: SCIM group mapping cannot assign approver/reviewer (scim.ts:70); /api/c2c/actions/lock and /api/c2c/documents/:id/lock admit any authenticated member including viewer (re-auth and not-author check only); admins hold signing authority by default with no per-org way to segregate it (founder decision); GOVERNANCE_RBAC_ENFORCE per-resource gate is dead code in practice.
findings.severityRationale: The P0 impact is closed: no viewer/member/manager can sign on any signing route, the check runs before the password, and a sponsor can map approvers/reviewers through Admin and access. What remains is not reachable from the UI (no client calls either lock route), affects only SCIM-provisioned orgs (a sales-led pilot can assign roles manually), or is a segregation-of-duties policy choice a small biotech commonly accepts if documented. All are enterprise-GA items.
findings.humanTestingNote: Not a defect testers will hit, but a setup prerequisite: only admin, approver or reviewer can sign, and outside NODE_ENV=development/test the signer must have an authenticator enrolled. A manager or member who tries to Approve/Sign/Transmit gets 403 'Your role does not permit applying an electronic signature ... Nothing was signed.' Workaround: in Admin and access assign the tester the Approver or Reviewer role (and enrol an authenticator in Account) before running signing journeys; use a second account for approval because authors cannot approve their own record.
findings.instructions:
1. SCIM (engineering): in server/routes/scim.ts replace the local `VALID_ROLES` (line 70) with `ASSIGNABLE_ORG_ROLES` imported from shared/constants/org-roles.ts, so GET /scim/v2/Groups (line ~1147, `let roles = [...VALID_ROLES]`), GET /Groups/:id (~1180) and PATCH /Groups/:id (~1192) accept 'approver' and 'reviewer'. Keep the remove semantics at ~1214 (demote to 'member' only from the group's own role) and the chained audit row via changeMemberRole. Add a test in server/routes/__tests__ (or next to existing scim tests) that is red at HEAD: PATCH /scim/v2/Groups/approver add member -> organization_users.role = 'approver' and one chained audit_logs row; GET /Groups lists six groups.
2. Lock role gate (engineering): in server/routes/c2c/actions.ts makeHandler (lines 642-680), for command 'lock' and 'unlock' call `checkSigningAuthority(userId, orgId)` (lock of an artifact is signed with meaning 'release' elsewhere, ARTIFACT_ACT_MEANING in server/services/artifact-approval-act.ts) BEFORE `verifyReauth` and return its status/code exactly as for SIGNATURE_COMMANDS. Do the same in server/routes/c2c/documents.ts POST '/:id/lock' (line 942) before `verifyReauth` (line 959). If the founder prefers editor-level lock, use `editorRoleDecision` from server/services/part11/editor-role.ts instead; either way fail closed (503) when the role lookup throws. Update the `authority` entries for server/routes/c2c/documents.ts in scripts/ci/sign-ceremony-baseline.json (shrink to 0) and run `node scripts/ci/check-sign-ceremony.mjs --write-baseline` only if the gate asks for it.
3. Write tests first (red at HEAD): extend server/routes/c2c/__tests__/governed-sign-authority.test.ts with 'refuses a viewer lock with 403 before the password is read, writing nothing' for /lock and a documents.ts lock test asserting no `UPDATE c2c_documents` and no `password_hash` query for a viewer.
4. Segregation of duties (founder decision first): record whether org admins may sign. If not, remove 'admin' from DEFAULT_SIGNING_ROLES (server/services/part11/signing-authority.ts:23); update server/services/part11/__tests__/one-signing-authority-policy.test.ts, governed-sign-authority.test.ts, the copy at client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/AdminMemberActions.tsx:91 and the `canSign` projection at server/routes/tenant-users.ts:373; and add an Admin and access warning when an organisation has no approver/reviewer (otherwise nobody can sign). If per-org policy is wanted, add an org setting read by `signingAuthorityRoles()` instead of the env var, with its change audited in-transaction.
5. GOVERNANCE_RBAC_ENFORCE: either enable it in terraform/stack/main.tf boot_environment after validating permission atoms against real role data, or delete the two dark branches (server/routes/c2c/actions.ts:705-721 and server/services/part11/governed-signature-ceremony.ts:190) with their tests so checkSigningAuthority is the single authority path (CLAUDE.md zero duplication). Not a user-facing capability, so no replacement path is needed, but name checkSigningAuthority in the commit.
6. Work on concept2cure-v2 only; merge, never rebase; run `npm run ci:sign-ceremony` and its selftest before push.
findings.acceptance: a) New lock tests fail at HEAD (viewer reaches the credential check / lock succeeds) and pass after: viewer and member get 403 ESIGNATURE_NO_AUTHORITY (or the editor refusal) on POST /api/c2c/actions/lock and POST /api/c2c/documents/:id/lock, with no password_hash query and no INSERT/UPDATE. b) SCIM test fails at HEAD (404 'Group not found.' for /Groups/approver) and passes after: approver/reviewer groups listed and assignable, each change with exactly one chained audit_logs row. c) `node scripts/ci/check-sign-ceremony.mjs` OK and `check-sign-ceremony.selftest.mjs` all pass. d) Founder decision on admin signing recorded; if admins are removed, an admin's POST /api/c2c/actions/sign returns 403 and an approver's reaches the credential check.

findings.title: QMS controlled documents: draft-to-effective and unsigned-effective holes closed, but the signature still covers no SOP content, versions are overwritten on revise, retirement is signed 'APPROVED', and the register shows no signature
findings.evidenceAtHead: FIXED: approval only from 'in_review' (server/services/qms/document-approval-signature.ts:120 APPROVABLE_STATES = ['in_review']; was ['draft','in_review'] at 92ccdba1:112) and the register offers 'Send for review' first (client/src/concept2cure/quality/SopRegister.tsx:415-429). The database now refuses an effective/retired document without a same-transaction signature (migrations/20261001_qms_document_signature_required.sql, in C2C_MIGRATION_FILES at scripts/db/migration-set.mjs:2975). Change-control writes carry requireEditorAccess (server/routes/mdx-qms.ts:1360,1401,1424,1526,1563,1588). Approve/retire check signing authority before the credential (mdx-qms.ts:563-600). The AnA create_qms_document role-check bullet was already wrong at 92ccdba1: it is a 'confirm' tool and the central writeRoleRefusal gate (AnaToolExecutor.ts:547-561 at HEAD; :425,444 at 92ccdba1) applies the editor role. STILL OPEN: (1) computeQmsDocumentContentDigest (document-approval-signature.ts:129-147) hashes the register row, metadata (a section skeleton: key/label/order/hint only, mdx-qms.ts:150-155) and the artifactId POINTER; no SOP body is stored or hashed, qms_documents.artifact_id has no FK (shared/schema.ts:19685) and nothing locks the linked content; the AnA create path does not set artifact_id at all. (2) No version table (grep for qms_document_versions/qms_document_revisions finds nothing); revise overwrites version, approver_id, approved_at in place (HTTP mdx-qms.ts:668-684; AnA revise_qms_document AnaToolExecutor.ts ~14323), so v1's approved content cannot be retrieved. (3) Retirement signs with the approval literal: retireBody = approveBody.omit(...) (mdx-qms.ts:528) whose meaning is z.literal('APPROVED'); retireQmsDocumentSigned stores params.meaning (document-approval-signature.ts:498,545); the client dialog passes meanings={['approval']} (SopRegister.tsx:617). (4) The register row (SopRegister.tsx:377-470) shows number, title, type, version, status, effective and review dates - no approver, signed-at or meaning; only a toast after signing (quality/qmsApproval.ts:40-54). A CSV compliance report with signer/meaning exists (server/services/audit/compliance-reports/queries/controlled-documents.ts:34-50) but no UI or PDF manifestation. (5) Send for review is an unsigned PATCH; PATCH writes its audit row after commit with field names only (mdx-qms.ts:496-506).
findings.fixedBy: cf950eeb9 (approval only from in_review; document-approval-signature.ts:120); 5726976d0 (DB refuses effective/retired without signature; migrations/20261001_qms_document_signature_required.sql); f1d2589ff (change-control writes need an editor); c6f2028b2 (legacy /api/qms deleted, canonical QMS writes refuse a viewer); MR-12 Stage 5 (2026-10-29): cd95dc9e6 (retirement signed with its own meaning, P-51), 5b7a6a79c (the register shows who approved each in-force version, when and as what), and the register edit's ledger row records each change from and to, on the edit's transaction (docs/evidence/MR-12/2026-10-29-register-edit-values/)
findings.remaining: Signature content binding (no controlled SOP body is stored or hashed, linked artifact not locked); no append-only version history (revise overwrites in place); retirement meaning is 'APPROVED'; no signature manifestation (name, UTC time, meaning) in the register or a printable record; review step unsigned; PATCH audit after commit with field names only.
findings.severityRationale: QMS controlled documents is in the launch catalog. A pilot customer using it for document control would fail a §11.70 / §11.10(e) / 21 CFR 820.40 audit: the approval signature does not bind any procedure text, prior approved versions are not retained, and retirement records a false meaning (§11.50). Not P0 because the database now prevents an unsigned effective document and approval requires review first, so no unsigned or unreviewed SOP can become effective.
findings.humanTestingNote: Testers can create, send for review, approve and retire SOPs. Visible defects: the register never shows who approved a document, when, or with what meaning (only a transient toast); the Retire dialog's only meaning is 'approval'; after Revise (via AnA) the previous approver/approval date disappear from the row and the earlier version cannot be opened; there is no place to write or view the SOP body in the register (clicking the number only asks AnA). Workaround for verifying signatures: Reporting -> controlled documents compliance report (CSV) lists the standing approval signature per document.
findings.instructions:
1. Founder decision (record it before coding): what is the system of record for SOP body text - (a) a body stored on the QMS version itself, or (b) a linked Authoring document (authoring_documents / concept2cure artifact). Also decide the retirement meaning word and whether 'Send for review' must be a signed 'REVIEWED' act.
2. Schema (Rule 1: new file, additive, IF NOT EXISTS; new table in public with organization_id INTEGER NOT NULL): add migrations/2026MMDD_qms_document_versions.sql creating public.qms_document_versions (id serial PK, organization_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id), document_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES qms_documents(id), version TEXT NOT NULL, title TEXT NOT NULL, body JSONB or TEXT per decision, body_sha256 TEXT NOT NULL, linked_artifact_id INTEGER NULL, linked_content_sha256 TEXT NULL, approval_signature_id INTEGER NULL, created_by INTEGER NOT NULL, created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), UNIQUE (document_id, version)), plus a BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger that raises (append-only). Insert it in C2C_MIGRATION_FILES (scripts/db/migration-set.mjs) before the final RLS sweep pair; run `npm run ci:migration-set-order` and `npm run ci:migration-drop-safety`. Add the trigger to the expected list in server/services/audit/audit-immutability-triggers.ts so the boot gate checks it. Mirror the table in shared/schema.ts next to qmsDocuments (line ~19668).
3. Bind content: in server/services/qms/document-approval-signature.ts approveQmsDocumentSigned, inside the caller's transaction after the FOR UPDATE read, (a) read the controlled body per the decision (for a linked artifact: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE and compute its content sha256; refuse with 409 if none), (b) INSERT the qms_document_versions snapshot, (c) add bodySha256/linkedContentSha256 to computeQmsDocumentContentDigest and change QMS_DOCUMENT_BINDING_BASIS to a new value (e.g. 'qms-document-version-content-sha256-v2') so pre-change rows remain verifiable under the old basis, (d) set approval_signature_id on the snapshot after persistGovernedActionSignature returns. For a linked artifact, lock it (status 'locked' through the existing signed-act path or a write-lock check in the authoring FROZEN/APPROVED middleware, authoring.router.ts ~423-470) so post-approval edits are refused; add a verdict helper that recomputes and reports 'does not cover' if the linked content hash differs.
4. Revise: in server/routes/mdx-qms.ts POST /qms/documents/:id/revise (650-712) move to one transaction (pool.connect, BEGIN, setTenantContextTx), assert the outgoing version has a snapshot row, then UPDATE and write the chained audit row with recordGovernedAction(client, ...) (as the AnA twin does at AnaToolExecutor.ts ~14307-14343) instead of the after-commit recordAuditRow at :691. Add GET /qms/documents/:id/versions returning snapshots with their signature.
5. Retirement meaning: add the chosen word to TASK_SIGNATURE_MEANINGS (server/services/part11/signature-meanings.ts:10-15, which flows into GOVERNED_SIGN_MEANINGS) and to client/src/concept2cure/_shared/esignMeanings.ts; export QMS_DOCUMENT_RETIREMENT_MEANING from document-approval-signature.ts; make retireBody (mdx-qms.ts:528) accept only that literal; change SopRegister.tsx:617 meanings to it.
6. Manifestation: extend GET /qms/documents (mdx-qms.ts:340) and GET /qms/documents/:id (:433) with a LEFT JOIN LATERAL to the standing approval/retirement signature (reuse the STANDING predicate from server/services/audit/compliance-reports/queries/controlled-documents.ts:24-26: signer_name, signed_at, signature_meaning, bound_payload_digest); add 'Approved by', 'Signed (UTC)' and 'Meaning' to the row grid and a detail panel in SopRegister.tsx; if the founder requires a printable record, add a PDF of the version with its signature block.
7. If the founder makes review a signed act: turn the draft->in_review PATCH into POST /qms/documents/:id/review using verifyApprovalSigner with meaning 'REVIEWED' and an electronic_signatures row of type 'qms-document-review'; refuse approval unless a standing review signature exists for the same version digest.
8. Write every test red first at HEAD, then green. Work on concept2cure-v2 only; merge, never rebase.
findings.acceptance: a) Editing the controlled body (or linked artifact) after approval is refused, or the signature verdict for that document reads 'does not cover' (test red at HEAD because the digest ignores content). b) After approve v1.0 -> revise -> approve v2.0, GET /qms/documents/:id/versions returns v1.0 with its body, body_sha256 and approval signature id (red at HEAD: no endpoint/table). c) UPDATE or DELETE on qms_document_versions raises; the boot immutability check lists the new trigger. d) POST /qms/documents/:id/approve on a draft returns 409 QMS_INVALID_STATE (already green - keep as regression). e) POST /retire with meaning 'APPROVED' returns 400; the stored electronic_signatures row for a retirement carries the retirement meaning. f) The register row and detail show printed name, UTC signed time and meaning for an effective document (component test red at HEAD). g) Revise writes its chained audit row in the same transaction: a forced audit failure leaves version/approver unchanged.
findings.dependencies: Founder decisions (SOP body system of record; retirement meaning word; signed review step). P11-01 (signing roles) is satisfied at HEAD. Overlaps P11-04 (QMS create/PATCH/revise after-commit audit).

findings.fixedBy: 8167aef12 and 0adb1b3ec (role changes, removals and settings changes audited in their transaction; membership-change.ts); 7863cf830 (AI-suggestion/AI-draft accept records in-transaction; authoring.router.ts:4288-4320); 8dab6c8f3 (tamper_proof_log names its tenant; audit-trail.ts:79-84); a8ddcf283 (Compose stacks enable AUDIT_TRAIL_ENABLED)
findings.remaining: QMS document create/PATCH/revise (HTTP) and submission leaf create/update audit after commit (loss reported, not prevented); QMS PATCH records field names only; audit_logs.old_values is never populated by any writer; discarded-audit baseline still 113 sites (launch files: authoring.router.ts 1, section-generation-service.ts 1, estar-submission-service.ts 2).
findings.severityRationale: The pilot's most-used governed paths (authoring saves and AI accept, Vault ingest/metadata, membership changes, every signature/approval/retire) now commit their audit row with the change, and every mutating request is additionally recorded with tenant and actor by a trail production refuses to boot without. The residual after-commit sites report a lost row to the user rather than hiding it, and leaf re-pointing records the previous document. Missing before-values on QMS draft edits and an always-null old_values column remain a customer-QA finding to close before enterprise GA; the QMS-specific record integrity is tracked at P1 under P11-03.
findings.humanTestingNote: Not observable in normal testing. Only if the audit store fails after a QMS create/edit or leaf placement does the response carry meta.auditTrail.persisted=false (surfaced to the user as 'saved, but its audit record was not written'); the change itself stays.
findings.instructions:
1. old_values: extend AuditLogEntry (server/services/auditService.ts) with an optional `oldValues` object and bind it to parameter 13 in writeChainedAuditRow (line ~322, currently `null`), JSON-stringified like new_values. Keep the payload hash over new_values unchanged so existing chains verify; if oldValues should be tamper-evident, add it to the hashed payload only for rows written after a dated cut-over and document that in the function header.
2. QMS create (server/routes/mdx-qms.ts:361-399): replace the autocommitted pool.query + recordAuditRow with one transaction (const client = await pool.connect(); BEGIN; setTenantContextTx(client, orgId)), INSERT ... RETURNING *, then `await writeChainedAuditRow(client, { tenantId: orgId, userId, action: 'mdx.qms.document.create', resourceType: 'qms_document', resourceId: String(row.id), details: <created row fields> })`, COMMIT; ROLLBACK on any throw and answer 500 with nothing created. Return meta.auditTrail {persisted:true, chained:true}.

findings.title: Gateway transmit now checks signing authority and refuses authorship and the package creator, but still records the signature after the bytes leave; two transmit paths remain
findings.evidenceAtHead: OPEN: In server/services/submission-gateways/governed-transmit.ts, executeGovernedTransmit calls gw.transmit at :662 and only afterwards (:736-857) opens the transaction that writes recordGovernedAction and persistGovernedActionSignature. If that transaction fails, it sets ledgerWriteFailed = true (:852) and returns success. Ran `npx vitest run server/services/submission-gateways/__tests__/governed-transmit-signature.test.ts`: 12/12 pass, including :159 'rolls the ledger transaction back and reports ledgerWriteFailed when the signature row cannot be written'. That test confirms the transmit completes with no signature on record. The route only reports the gap in the HTTP response (server/routes/mdx-submission-gateway.ts:331-363, transmitOutcomeNotices); nothing durable flags the transmittal. MEANING: SIGN_MEANINGS is still ['authorship','review','approval','responsibility','release'] (mdx-submission-gateway.ts:82, accepted at :274). 'authorship' is now refused server-side (server/services/submission-gateways/governed-transmit-checks.ts:248-262 via requiresIndependence) and removed from the form (client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/GatewayTransmittals.tsx:271-279, default 'release'), but 'review', 'approval' and 'responsibility' are still accepted for a transmission. TWO PATHS: both are reachable under 'Submit & file' (client/src/concept2cure/v2/registryModel.ts:638, :670). (a) POST /api/submissions/sequences/:seqId/transmit (server/routes/submissions.ts:1887; client SubmissionCenter.tsx:856) requires a committed governed signature with intent 'transmit' BEFORE the gateway (server/services/submission-service/submission-service.ts:2100-2107) and voids it on a pre-wire refusal (:2052-2066). (b) POST /api/mdx/gateways/:region/:gateway/transmit (mdx-submission-gateway.ts:278; client GatewayTransmittals.tsx:482) and the AnA command (server/services/ana-ri/mdx-command-handlers.ts:821-860) go through executeGovernedTransmit, which signs after transmit. CLOSED SINCE AUDIT: checkSigningAuthority now runs before re-auth (mdx-submission-gateway.ts:297-301; governed-transmit-checks.ts:217), the package creator is refused (SIGNER_IS_AUTHOR), and so is the authorship meaning.
findings.fixedBy: e7fdd5c39 (SEC-1008-1: only a role that may sign transmits; authority checked before re-auth); f7973d225 (package creator cannot transmit; 'authorship' refused, governed-transmit-checks.ts:248-283)
findings.remaining: (1) On the package-model gateway path (HTTP route and AnA command), the signature is still written after the irreversible send, and a failed write is tolerated. (2) The transmit meaning is not fixed to 'release'; 'review' is accepted. (3) Two transmit paths with different signing ceremonies remain reachable.
findings.severityRationale: The pilot's core regulatory act is an FDA ESG transmission. On a path reachable from the launch navigation, a submission can still reach FDA with no Part 11 signature on record, and a test executed at HEAD proves it. The window is narrow (a database failure between the gateway call and the signature commit), but the ordering defect is exactly what a sponsor's QA audit flags under §11.10(f)/§11.70. Pilot users must not rely on it for production filings until the signature commits first.
findings.humanTestingNote: Not visible unless the database fails between the gateway call and the signature write. Testers will see two transmit surfaces with different ceremonies: Submission Center > Dispatch, which signs first, and Gateway transmittals, which signs at transmit. On the second, a transmission can be signed as 'Review'. Use the Submission Center sequence path for test transmissions.
findings.instructions:
1. server/services/submission-gateways/governed-transmit.ts: move the signature transaction BEFORE gw.transmit (:662). After assertTransmitterIndependent (:658), take pool.connect(), BEGIN, then recordGovernedAction(command 'sign', target as at :743, payload {meaning, region, gateway, bundleSha256, sequence, submissionType, contentFingerprint {assembled, atTransmit}, intent:'transmit'}), then persistGovernedActionSignature with binding {digest: bundle.sha256, basis: BINDING_BASIS.TRANSMITTED_BUNDLE_SHA256}, then COMMIT. On any failure, ROLLBACK and throw GovernedTransmitInternalError('transmit-signature-before-wire', err). The gateway is never called.
2. Wrap gw.transmit in try/catch. If refusedBeforeWire(err) (server/services/submission-gateways/index.ts:152), void the signature in its own transaction with voidSignatureForRefusedAct (server/services/part11/signature-persistence.ts:253), mirroring voidingSignatureOnRefusal (server/services/submission-service/submission-service.ts:1069), and rethrow. Otherwise keep the signature (the bytes may be at the agency) and rethrow.
3. After a successful transmit, write a receipt in a second transaction: a chained row (recordGovernedAction command 'transmit-receipt' or writeChainedAuditRow) naming signatureId, transmittalId, transmissionId, contentAfterTransmit, the filed-sequence facts and the pre-transmit findings, plus the existing UPDATE submission_transmittals metadata stamp (:832-845). If that fails, return receiptWriteFailed (replacing ledgerWriteFailed; the signature already exists) and surface it through transmitOutcomeNotices.
4. Meaning: in server/routes/mdx-submission-gateway.ts transmitBody (:273-274), replace z.enum(SIGN_MEANINGS) with z.literal('release').default('release'), and keep SIGN_MEANINGS for the technical-rejection body (:526). In executeGovernedTransmit, refuse any other meaning with GovernedTransmitRefusal 422. In client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/GatewayTransmittals.tsx:271-279, replace the select with a fixed 'Release: I authorize submission to the agency' statement. In server/services/ana-ri/mdx-command-handlers.ts (~:837), pass 'release'.
5. Tests: in server/services/submission-gateways/__tests__/governed-transmit-signature.test.ts, invert :159 so that with failSignature, executeGovernedTransmit rejects and the gateway transmit mock is called 0 times (red on HEAD). Add a test that a pre-wire gateway refusal voids the signature, and one that a receipt-write failure leaves the signature committed and reports receiptWriteFailed. Update the AnA handler tests (server/services/ana-ri/__tests__) that assert the old ordering.
6. Founder decision, then apply CLAUDE.md's deletion rule: is package-model transmit (Gateway transmittals) in the pilot? If not, return 410 from POST /api/mdx/gateways/:region/:gateway/transmit naming the replacement, POST /api/submissions/sequences/:seqId/transmit (client SubmissionCenter.tsx:856), and remove only the transmit form from GatewayTransmittals.tsx (keep list, status, ack and technical-rejection). Name the replacement file and its reachability test in the commit message. If both paths stay, steps 1-5 make their ordering equivalent.
Commit directly on concept2cure-v2 (Rule 0).
findings.acceptance: (a) With persistGovernedActionSignature forced to throw, executeGovernedTransmit rejects with transmit-signature-before-wire and the gateway transmit mock is called 0 times. On HEAD it is called once and ledgerWriteFailed is true (red first). (b) A gateway refusal before the wire leaves the electronic_signatures row voided and no transmittal row. (c) POST /api/mdx/gateways/fda/esg/transmit with meaning 'review' returns 422, and the form offers no meaning choice. (d) Either exactly one transmit route remains, with the other returning 410 and naming its replacement, or the founder's decision to keep both is recorded and both sign before the wire.

findings.severityRationale: A GxP design partner has to validate its intended use and audit the supplier before relying on the system in production. findings.humanTestingNote: Not observable in the UI. There is no release number, so testers should record the commit from GET /api/version in every defect report.
findings.instructions:
1. Founder decisions, recorded in docs/RELEASE_GOVERNANCE.md: the version scheme (vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH), who approves a release, and how release tags are created. Recommended: tags are created by a CI workflow through the GitHub API, not by a local push, so .husky/pre-push (Rule 0 enforcement) stays unchanged.
2. Add .github/workflows/release-cut.yml (workflow_dispatch, input version). (a) Refuse unless github.sha is on concept2cure-v2 and the CI verdict for that SHA is success; reuse the ci-verdict job logic from deploy-aws.yml. (b) Refuse unless docs/releases/<version>.md exists with Change, Impact, Testing and Approval sections and a named approver. (c) Run `npm run validation:iq`, `npm run validation:oq` and `npm run validation:traceability` against the staging deployment, with VALIDATION_BASE_URL, VALIDATION_USER_EMAIL, the password/TOTP secrets, CHROMIUM_PATH from `npx playwright install chromium`, and VALIDATION_EVIDENCE_ROOT=$RUNNER_TEMP/validation-pack. Fail on any failed or deviation step. (d) Upload the pack as artifact validation-pack-<version>. (e) Create the annotated tag v<version> and a GitHub Release with the pack and the change record attached. Tags created with GITHUB_TOKEN do not trigger deploy-aws.yml's push:tags trigger, so either dispatch deploy-aws.yml explicitly (workflow_dispatch) or use a GitHub App token.
3. tests/validation/lib/harness.mjs:52-58 and scripts/validation/run-iq.mjs:24-26: when process.env.CI is set, throw if VALIDATION_USER_EMAIL, CHROMIUM_PATH or VALIDATION_EVIDENCE_ROOT is unset. Remove the founder-email default entirely: an unset email is an error everywhere. Add the case to tests/validation/lib/harness.selftest.mjs (validation:oq:selftest) and show it red first.
4. deploy-aws.yml: pass BUILD_VERSION (GITHUB_REF_NAME when the ref is a tag, else empty) into the task definition. server/startup/inline-endpoints.ts:196-198: return {version: process.env.BUILD_VERSION || null, commit, startedAt}.
5. Add docs/releases/TEMPLATE.md and a script, scripts/release/change-record.mjs, that pre-fills the change list from `git log <previous tag>..<sha>`. The approver fills impact, testing and approval.
6. Make the gate fail first: run release-cut on a SHA where one OQ step is forced to fail (e.g. a VALIDATION_FORCE_FAIL step id honoured only by the selftest), show the workflow failing with no tag created, then run it green.
All commits go on concept2cure-v2 (Rule 0); no release branches.
findings.acceptance: (a) release-cut on a SHA with a forced OQ failure fails and creates no tag or release (shown first). On a green SHA it produces tag vX.Y.Z and a GitHub Release carrying validation-pack-vX.Y.Z (IQ, OQ and traceability results naming the base URL and commit) and docs/releases/vX.Y.Z.md. (b) With CI=true and VALIDATION_USER_EMAIL unset, the harness exits non-zero before any request (selftest red on HEAD). (c) GET /api/version on the deployed environment returns {version:'vX.Y.Z', commit:<sha>}. (d) release-cut refuses when the change record is missing or has no approver.

findings.title: First-run setup is now gated by the deployment's SETUP_TOKEN in production and is race-safe; it still mints an admin (possibly platform-admin) session without MFA, and the compose stacks cannot use it
findings.evidenceAtHead: server/routes/setup.ts:70-104: setupTokenGate. Production with no SETUP_TOKEN, or one shorter than 32 characters, gives 403 SETUP_CLOSED. Otherwise the X-Setup-Token header is compared by sha256 plus crypto.timingSafeEqual. :129 mounts requireSetupToken on POST /initialize before the body is read. :175-180: the transaction takes pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('c2c:first-run-setup')) and re-counts users under it (AlreadyInitializedError -> 409). terraform/stack/main.tf:82-85 random_password.setup_token (48 characters); :137-140 stores it in Secrets Manager; :434 injects it into the API only; boot_contract.tftest.hcl:241-245 asserts that. terraform/stack/outputs.tf:120-121 gives the operator procedure. Command run: `npx vitest run server/routes/__tests__/setup.test.ts` -> 14/14 pass, including 'is closed in production when no setup token is configured — 403, nothing written', 'refuses a missing or wrong token', and 'two first calls at once create one administrator'. STILL OPEN: setup.ts:211-236 still calls openSession and signs a role=admin access JWT (expiresIn '1d', server/config/environment.ts:361) with no second factor, while password login always issues an MFA challenge (server/routes/auth.ts:704-740). outputs.tf:121 tells the operator to use the platform_owner_emails address, so that token is a platform-admin session. /api/setup is still mounted unconditionally under system scope (server/bootstrap/register-platform-routes.ts:142) and allowlisted as public (:250). docker-compose.yml:87 and docker-compose.beta.yml:82 run NODE_ENV=production but pass no SETUP_TOKEN (grep is empty; there is no env_file), so first-run setup is closed there, although docker-compose.yml:27-29 tells operators to use it. scripts/seed-admin.mjs is not in the runtime image (Dockerfile.optimized:188 copies only scripts/db).
findings.fixedBy: b221cd641 (D1: a deployment has a named owner, and only its operator can create the first account — server/routes/setup.ts:70-129,175-180; terraform/stack/main.tf:82-85,137-140,434); a4c8fea0e (lint marker)
findings.remaining: (1) The bootstrap response is still a 1-day admin session that bypassed MFA. For the platform owner's address it is a platform-admin session. The audit's fix ('never mint a session there; return sign in') was not applied. (2) The compose stacks pass no SETUP_TOKEN, so their documented first-run flow returns 403 SETUP_CLOSED, and the image has no in-container alternative. (3) Minor: the gate is a user count, so setup would reopen, still token-gated, if every user row were deleted.
findings.severityRationale: The P1 impact is closed: an unauthenticated takeover of a fresh deployment, operator lockout, and the double-create race. What remains is reachable only by whoever holds a 48-character secret in AWS Secrets Manager, plus a compose usability gap. Hardening, not a pilot blocker.
findings.humanTestingNote: Terraform staging: the operator must create the first admin with `POST /api/setup/initialize`, sending header `X-Setup-Token: <value of the setup_token secret>` (terraform output first_run_setup). Without the header the response is 403 SETUP_TOKEN_INVALID. There is no UI for this step. docker-compose.yml/beta: first-run setup always returns 403 SETUP_CLOSED because compose does not pass SETUP_TOKEN. Workaround: from the host checkout run `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:$DB_PASSWORD@localhost:${DB_PORT:-5432}/concept2cure ADMIN_EMAIL=<you> ADMIN_PASSWORD=<strong> NODE_ENV=production node scripts/seed-admin.mjs`, or add `SETUP_TOKEN` (32+ characters) to a local docker-compose.override.yml app environment and call the endpoint with the header. Under `npm run dev` with no SETUP_TOKEN the route is open.
findings.instructions:
All work on concept2cure-v2 (Rule 0).
1. Failing-first test: in server/routes/__tests__/setup.test.ts, change the test 'POST /initialize mints the bootstrap token as a registered session ... (P1-38)' to assert `res.body.token === undefined`, `res.body.next === 'sign_in'`, and that openSession was not called. Run `npx vitest run server/routes/__tests__/setup.test.ts` and show it failing.
2. server/routes/setup.ts: delete the openSession + jwt.sign block (lines ~211-229) and the now-unused imports (jwt, openSession). Return `res.status(201).json({ success: true, next: 'sign_in', organization, user })`. The replacement for the bootstrap session is the normal sign-in at POST /api/auth/login (server/routes/auth.ts), which issues the MFA challenge (auth.ts:704-740). Name that path in the commit message, as the deletion rule requires. Update the module header (lines 1-26) and terraform/stack/outputs.tf:121 to say 'then sign in'.
3. docker-compose.yml and docker-compose.beta.yml: add `SETUP_TOKEN: ${SETUP_TOKEN:?SETUP_TOKEN must be set (32+ characters) for first-run setup}` to the app service environment, and add SETUP_TOKEN to the 'Required .env' header list (docker-compose.yml:18-23). Add a rule to scripts/ci/check-compose-boot-contract.mjs requiring SETUP_TOKEN in a NODE_ENV=production app service. Show the contract failing first, then passing.
4. Optional (P3): make the gate durable. Keep the user count, and also refuse when any organization_users row with role 'admin' has ever existed (or record completion in an existing settings row in the same transaction). Add a test that deleting all users does not reopen setup.
5. Re-run setup.test.ts (all pass), and add a test that a login immediately after setup returns mfaRequired: true.

findings.title: API and worker tasks still hold the DB owner credential plus the audit HMAC, export, attestation and MFA keys; tenants-simple still queries on an owner connection outside the pool; RLS still has a session-GUC pass-through
findings.evidenceAtHead: terraform/stack/main.tf:315-328: boot_secrets includes DATABASE_URL (the owner, built from module.rds.master_username at :96), MFA_ENCRYPTION_KEY, AUDIT_HMAC_KEY, AUDIT_HMAC_SECRET, AUDIT_EXPORT_SIGNING_KEY and AUDIT_ATTESTATION_KEY. They go to api_secrets (:430-435, which adds APP_SERVICE_DB_PASSWORD) and to worker_secrets (:439). The stack's own comment at :37-41 still says 'the API at boot ... and server/routes/tenants-simple.ts serves routes through a client on it, outside RLS. A known exposure.' server/routes/tenants-simple.ts:67-74 opens a module-load `postgres(DATABASE_URL)` client, used by GET / (:129-145, every organization for platform admins), POST / (:177), PATCH /:id (:262) and GET /:tenantId/users (:324). Boot DDL runs on the owner: server/db/bootstrap/index.ts:33-43 (ensureAuthTables opens an owner pool) and server/startup/services.ts:130 (ensureCoreTables(process.env.DATABASE_URL)). The RLS policies still pass through when app.rls_enforce is not 'on' or app.current_user_role='app_super_admin' (db/migrations/20260801_tenant_isolation_sweep.sql:188-197, 332-341; the same clause in migrations/20260928_users_membership_rls.sql, 20261004_user_presence_rls.sql and others). There is no KMS-backed audit sealing: the only KMS signer is the release signer (server/services/signature/kms-signer.ts). Mitigations added since the audit, which are detective or least-privilege and not a boundary against the owner credential: the runtime pool uses app_service via APP_DATABASE_URL (server/db/getDatabaseUrl.ts:62-83); app_service is append-only on 30+ stores (scripts/db/provision-app-role.mjs:199-250); audit-chain anchors go to the object-locked evidence bucket (AUDIT_ANCHOR_BUCKET, main.tf:294); pgaudit is required (DB_AUDIT_REQUIRED, main.tf:258).
findings.remaining: All four fix items remain. (1) DATABASE_URL (owner) and APP_SERVICE_DB_PASSWORD are still in the API task, and DATABASE_URL is also in the worker. (2) tenants-simple still runs on its own owner connection. (3) The audit seal and signing keys still live in the API and worker environment. (4) RLS can still be switched off by any SQL primitive that can SET a session GUC. With RCE or SQL injection in the API process, an attacker can still read and write across tenants, DISABLE TRIGGER on the append-only stores, rewrite rows and re-seal the HMAC chain. Only the object-locked anchors and pgaudit would show it after the fact.
findings.severityRationale: A GxP buyer is sold tamper-evident Part 11 records and DB-enforced tenant isolation. While the request-serving process holds the owner credential and the seal keys, both claims hold only against non-owner roles, and one app compromise voids them. The pilot has at least two tenants on the database (the platform org and the design partner). Detective anchors and pgaudit reduce this from undetectable to detectable, which is why it is P1 and not P0.
findings.instructions:
All work on concept2cure-v2 (Rule 0). Do SEC-04 first so the immutability triggers exist before the owner credential is removed.
1. server/routes/tenants-simple.ts: delete the `postgres` import (:6), cleanDatabaseUrl (:44-63) and the `sql` client (:67-74). Rewrite the four `sql` queries (:129, :136, :177, :262, :324) as parameterized `pool.query` calls on the `pool` already imported at :14. Wrap the platform-admin all-organizations read and the tenant-users read in runWithSystemTenantScope('tenants:<route>', ...) (the pattern at server/startup/services.ts:129) so the cross-tenant scope is explicit and audited. Add a CI grep gate (scripts/ci/, wired in package.json and .husky/pre-push) that fails on `process.env.DATABASE_URL` or `from 'postgres'` under server/routes/**. Show it failing on today's tenants-simple.ts first.
2. Make API boot schema-verify-only in production: in server/db/bootstrap/index.ts ensureAuthTables, when NODE_ENV=production and APP_DATABASE_URL is set, do not open an owner pool. Move applyAuthSchemaMigrations, seedOrganizations and applyModuleCatalogSchema into scripts/db/deploy-migrate.mjs (or into idempotent files in C2C_MIGRATION_FILES, Rule 1), and at boot only verify. Do the same for server/startup/services.ts:130: call ensureCoreTables with the runtime URL in verify mode.
3. Terraform: remove the DATABASE_URL entry from local.boot_secrets (terraform/stack/main.tf:316), and remove APP_SERVICE_DB_PASSWORD from api_secrets (:431). In .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml, pass both to the migrate job through ecs-one-off-task.sh's existing EXTRA_SECRETS_JSON (scripts/ops/ecs-one-off-task.sh header). Do the same in provision-database.yml. Update the preflight required-name list in deploy-aws.yml, scripts/ci/check-compose-boot-contract.mjs, and terraform/stack/tests/boot_contract.tftest.hcl: assert DATABASE_URL is absent from module.ecs.api_container.secrets and worker_container.secrets, and run `terraform test` failing first. Update the comment at main.tf:31-41.
4. Boot refusal: in the production branch of server/config/environment.ts, refuse to start when DATABASE_URL is present alongside APP_DATABASE_URL in an API or worker process. Extend the boot posture probe to refuse a runtime role that owns any public table (`SELECT 1 FROM pg_tables WHERE tableowner = current_user LIMIT 1`). Write unit tests failing first.
5. Seal keys (may be split into a P2 follow-up if the pilot date requires): put audit sealing behind AWS KMS HMAC keys (KeySpec HMAC_256) via a seal adapter used by the audit chain writer and the tamper_proof_log writer. Give the task role kms:GenerateMac only, and give verification (server/jobs/auditChainIntegritySweep.ts) kms:VerifyMac. Then drop AUDIT_HMAC_KEY and AUDIT_HMAC_SECRET from boot_secrets. Keep the raw-key path for non-AWS installs behind an explicit flag.
6. RLS GUC pass-through (P2): amend db/migrations/20260801_tenant_isolation_sweep.sql in place, with a dated header note (Rule 1: no appended DROP POLICY), so the shadow-mode and app_super_admin clauses do not apply when current_user = 'app_service'. Re-run the sweep's replay test.
7. Integration test (tests/db/*.dbtest.ts): connected as app_service, `ALTER TABLE public.authoring_signatures DISABLE TRIGGER ALL` fails with 42501, `UPDATE public.authoring_signatures ...` fails, and `SET app.rls_enforce='off'` followed by a cross-tenant SELECT returns 0 rows (after step 6). Show the same statements succeeding as the owner to prove the test can see the difference.
findings.acceptance: (a) `terraform test` in terraform/stack fails on HEAD with an assertion that DATABASE_URL must be absent from the api and worker containers, and passes after. (b) The CI grep gate fails on the current tenants-simple.ts, and the GET /api/tenants and /:tenantId/users tests pass on the pooled implementation. (c) The API boots in production with only APP_DATABASE_URL, and refuses to boot when DATABASE_URL is also set (test shown failing first). (d) deploy-migrate still succeeds with the secrets passed through EXTRA_SECRETS_JSON (staging run captured). (e) The app_service integration test of step 7 passes, and its owner-control half shows the statements succeed as the owner.
