findings.title: Authoring signatures and audit trail are now append-only by trigger and grant; frozen_documents (the signed freeze snapshot) is still mutable, and the boot probe does not watch authoring_signatures
findings.evidenceAtHead: authoring_signatures: migrations/20261001_domain_history_append_only.sql:166-181 adds BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE and BEFORE TRUNCATE triggers using public.domain_history_append_only(). The file is in the set at scripts/db/migration-set.mjs:2883. authoring_audit_trail: db/migrations/20260725_authoring_audit_trail.sql:72-110 adds its triggers (`git show 92ccdba1:db/migrations/20260725_authoring_audit_trail.sql | grep -c 'CREATE TRIGGER'` = 0, so they are new). They are listed in EXPECTED_AUDIT_IMMUTABILITY_TRIGGERS (server/services/audit/audit-immutability-triggers.ts:60-61). Grants: scripts/db/provision-app-role.mjs:212 and :244 put both tables in APPEND_ONLY_TABLES, which withholds UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE from app_service (:470-507). ci:sign-ceremony now recognizes insertAuthoringSignature (scripts/ci/check-sign-ceremony.mjs:103-107). Commands run: `npx vitest run server/services/audit/__tests__/audit-immutability-triggers.pglite.test.ts` -> 9/9 pass. A PGlite probe applying migrations/20261001_domain_history_append_only.sql gave: UPDATE and DELETE on authoring_signatures REFUSED ('IMMUTABILITY_VIOLATION: authoring_signatures is append-only'); `UPDATE frozen_documents SET frozen_content='tampered'` ALLOWED (1 row); `DELETE FROM frozen_documents` ALLOWED (1 row). STILL OPEN: frozen_documents (created at db/migrations/20260725_authoring_document_loop_tables.sql:120-131) has no trigger in any migration and is not in APPEND_ONLY_TABLES. `grep table: 'authoring_signatures'` in audit-immutability-triggers.ts is empty, so a disabled authoring_signatures trigger is not detected at boot (acknowledged in server/db/__tests__/provision-app-role-append-only.test.ts:156). Signatures are still written by direct INSERT (server/routes/authoring.router.ts:4920 in insertAuthoringSignature, and a second copy at :7448 on the /sign path), not through server/services/part11/signature-persistence.ts. The only frozen_documents writers are INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (authoring.router.ts:5126, :5271, :7256). No UPDATE or DELETE exists on any server path, and the tenant purge (server/services/tenant/) does not list the table, so a trigger breaks nothing.
findings.fixedBy: 00f94ee9f (P1-24: authoring_signatures append-only trigger, migrations/20261001_domain_history_append_only.sql:166-181); 7863cf830 (authoring_audit_trail triggers plus registry entry); a114d7771 and fd69c098d (append-only grant ceiling, scripts/db/provision-app-role.mjs:212,244); c6bfd10c7 (sign-ceremony gate sees insertAuthoringSignature)
findings.remaining: (1) frozen_documents, the frozen content a freeze or approval signature covers, can still be UPDATEd, DELETEd or TRUNCATEd by app_service and the owner. (2) authoring_signatures' two triggers are not in EXPECTED_AUDIT_IMMUTABILITY_TRIGGERS, so boot and security-health do not report them when they are disabled or missing (each deploy re-arms them). (3) Two copies of the authoring_signatures INSERT (authoring.router.ts:4920 and :7448), contrary to the zero-duplication rule. (4) The owner credential can still DISABLE TRIGGER (tracked in SEC-03).
findings.severityRationale: Authoring sign and freeze is a launch journey whose output is a Part 11 record (11.10(e), 11.70). The signature rows are now protected, but the signed content snapshot they bind to is still alterable and deletable by the runtime role. An auditor would flag that before pilot users rely on signed documents. The fix is small (S).
findings.instructions:
All work on concept2cure-v2 (Rule 0).
1. Failing-first: add a PGlite test (next to server/services/audit/__tests__/audit-immutability-triggers.pglite.test.ts) that applies the authoring subsystem files (scripts/db/authoring-subsystem.mjs AUTHORING_SUBSYSTEM_FILES) and migrations/20261001_domain_history_append_only.sql, inserts a frozen_documents row, and expects `UPDATE frozen_documents SET frozen_content='x'`, `DELETE FROM frozen_documents` and `TRUNCATE frozen_documents` all to throw IMMUTABILITY_VIOLATION. Show it failing on HEAD.
2. Create migrations/20261013_frozen_documents_append_only.sql. It is additive and replay-safe (Rule 1): a header with the date, the why, and the writer census (only INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING at server/routes/authoring.router.ts:5126, :5271, :7256). Guard with to_regclass('public.frozen_documents'). Then `DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS` of this file's own trigger names, followed by CREATE TRIGGER trg_frozen_documents_append_only BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE FOR EACH ROW and trg_frozen_documents_no_truncate BEFORE TRUNCATE FOR EACH STATEMENT, both executing public.domain_history_append_only(). Create no table and drop no other file's object.
3. Register the file in C2C_MIGRATION_FILES (scripts/db/migration-set.mjs) after 'migrations/20261001_domain_history_append_only.sql' (function dependency) and before the final sweep pair. Run `npm run ci:migration-set-order` and `npm run ci:migration-drop-safety`.
4. scripts/db/provision-app-role.mjs: add `{ schema: 'public', name: 'frozen_documents' }` to APPEND_ONLY_TABLES (:199-250), next to authoring_signatures, and update server/db/__tests__/provision-app-role-append-only.test.ts.
5. server/services/audit/audit-immutability-triggers.ts: add four entries to EXPECTED_AUDIT_IMMUTABILITY_TRIGGERS. These are authoring_signatures/trg_authoring_signatures_append_only and trg_authoring_signatures_no_truncate (source 'migrations/20261001_domain_history_append_only.sql'), and frozen_documents/trg_frozen_documents_append_only and trg_frozen_documents_no_truncate (source the new file). Update the pglite test's migration list (:59) and the provision-app-role-append-only.test.ts:156 note. Add a test case that disables trg_authoring_signatures_append_only and expects assertAuditImmutabilityTriggers to name it as disabled.
6. Zero duplication: replace the inline INSERT at server/routes/authoring.router.ts:7448 with a call to insertAuthoringSignature (:4899), extending its row type with an optional signedAt if needed, so there is one writer. Run `npm run ci:sign-ceremony` and its selftest.
7. Run the test from step 1 (now passing), the audit-immutability pglite test, and the authoring e-sign/freeze route tests to confirm that ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING inserts still succeed.
findings.acceptance: The new pglite test fails on HEAD (UPDATE/DELETE frozen_documents succeed) and passes after. assertAuditImmutabilityTriggers reports authoring_signatures and frozen_documents triggers as missing or disabled when they are dropped or disabled (shown failing first). provision-app-role's audit lists frozen_documents with UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE withheld from app_service. ci:migration-set-order, ci:migration-drop-safety and ci:sign-ceremony pass. Authoring e-sign, /sign and freeze still return success, and re-approving the same version still inserts nothing (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING).
findings.dependencies: None. SEC-03 separately closes the owner-level DISABLE TRIGGER path.

findings.title: QMS: the /api/qms second door is deleted and every mdx-qms write now needs an editor role, but supplier approval and NC disposition are still unsigned and their audit rows are written after the commit
findings.evidenceAtHead: FIXED PART: server/routes/qms.ts and server/services/qms/qms.service.ts no longer exist at HEAD. server/bootstrap/register-document-routes.ts:271-278 is now only the removal note. A grep for a '/api/qms' mount outside tests finds nothing. In server/routes/mdx-qms.ts every write route is gated: 18 carry requireEditorAccess (lines 361, 448, 650, 714, 906, 941, 1019, 1051, 1120, 1182, 1216, 1360, 1401, 1424, 1526, 1563, 1588); /qms/documents/:id/approve (602) and /qms/changes/:id/approve (1482) use verifyApprovalSigner (556) plus a BEGIN/COMMIT signed write; training-ack (757) takes userId from the session (getUserId), not from the body. At 92ccdba1, 16 of the 20 write routes had no requireEditorAccess (git show 92ccdba1:server/routes/mdx-qms.ts | grep -v requireEditorAccess count = 16). OPEN PART: supplierCreate (mdx-qms.ts:873-878) accepts approvalStatus from SUPPLIER_STATUS, 'approved' included. POST /qms/suppliers (906) and PATCH /qms/suppliers/:id (941, COL map at 950: approvalStatus -> approval_status) write it with a plain pool.query and no signature. The audit row comes from recordAuditRow after the committed write (the code's own comment calls it 'a log beside it'). PATCH /qms/nonconforming/:id/disposition (1216) has the same shape: pool.query UPDATE of disposition (scrap/rework/use_as_is), then recordAuditRow, with no signature and no guard against re-dispositioning. Internal-audit PATCH (1051) and management-review POST (1120) are also unsigned. client/src calls only mdx/qms/{documents,changes,templates,training}, with no supplier or nonconforming caller.
findings.fixedBy: c6f2028b2 (P1-31/DP-34: deleted server/routes/qms.ts and qms.service.ts, removed the mount at register-document-routes.ts:271, added requireEditorAccess to the supplier/internal-audit/management-review/NC routes in server/routes/mdx-qms.ts:906,941,1019,1051,1120,1182,1216); f1d2589ff (change-control writes need an editor, mdx-qms.ts:1360-1588); cf950eeb9 and 0f961354c (signing authority on the QMS approve routes, mdx-qms.ts:602,1482).
findings.remaining: (1) An editor can set a supplier to approved or qualified through POST or PATCH /api/mdx/qms/suppliers with no electronic signature, no signing-authority check and no meaning or reason. (2) An editor can disposition a nonconforming product (use_as_is, scrap) with no signature, and can re-disposition an already-dispositioned NC. (3) For both, the audit row is written after the record commits: if it fails, the decision stands with no audit trail. (4) Internal-audit completion and management reviews are unsigned. (5) Minor: training-ack accepts a self-reported quizScore from the body.
findings.severityRationale: The P1 core is closed: the viewer-writable second door is gone and every QMS write needs an editor. The launch-catalog surface, QMS controlled documents, is signed with chained audit. Supplier and NC decisions have no UI in the shipped client, so only an editor calling the API directly can reach them, and the pilot is FDA-only with founder support. They must be signed governed writes before GA to ISO 13485 / 21 CFR 820 medtech buyers.
findings.humanTestingNote: Testers cannot see this through the six apps: the client has no supplier or nonconforming-product screen. The only way to reproduce it is by API: as an editor, PATCH /api/mdx/qms/suppliers/:id {"approvalStatus":"approved"} returns 200 with no signature prompt.
findings.instructions:
1. server/routes/mdx-qms.ts:873-886: remove approvalStatus and approvalDate from supplierCreate, and therefore from supplierPatch, which is supplierCreate.partial(). In the PATCH COL map at line 950, drop approvalStatus and approvalDate. POST /qms/suppliers (906) then always inserts 'pending' (the COALESCE($6,'pending') becomes the literal 'pending'). A body that still carries approvalStatus is answered 422 with code SUPPLIER_STANDING_REQUIRES_SIGNATURE. Do not silently ignore it.
2. Add POST /qms/suppliers/:id/approval with body {approvalStatus: 'approved'|'conditional'|'disqualified'|..., reason, meaning, password, totp?}. Copy the /qms/changes/:id/approve handler (1482-1524): getUserId, verifyApprovalSigner(res, userId, orgId, body) (556), pool.connect, BEGIN, then a new service function approveQmsSupplierSigned(client, {...}) in server/services/qms/supplier-approval-signature.ts, modelled on server/services/qms/change-approval-signature.ts:157 approveQmsChangeSigned. Inside the transaction that function must: UPDATE qms_suppliers SET approval_status, approval_date=now() WHERE id AND organization_id AND deleted_at IS NULL (404 when no row); persist the signature through the same signature persistence approveQmsChangeSigned uses; and write the chained audit row in the same client. Then COMMIT, with ROLLBACK on any throw.
3. Replace PATCH /qms/nonconforming/:id/disposition (1216-1240) with a signed POST /qms/nonconforming/:id/disposition that follows the same ceremony (verifyApprovalSigner, transaction, signature, chained audit row in the same transaction). Refuse with 409 when disposition is already not 'pending' unless the body carries reopen:true plus a reason. Removing the PATCH removes no user-facing capability, because no client calls it (client/src greps clean). Name the new POST route in the commit message as the replacement.
4. For PATCH /qms/internal-audits/:id (1051) when status moves to completed, and for POST /qms/management-reviews (1120): at minimum, wrap the write and a writeChainedAuditRow (server/services/auditService.ts:269) in one pool.connect transaction instead of recordAuditRow after commit.
5. Tests, written and seen to fail first: add server/routes/__tests__/mdx-qms-supplier-nc-signed.test.ts with these cases. (a) Editor PATCH /api/mdx/qms/suppliers/:id {approvalStatus:'approved'} returns 422 and the row is unchanged; this returns 200 at HEAD. (b) POST /qms/suppliers/:id/approval with no password returns 4xx and nothing is written. (c) With a valid signature it returns 200, writes one signature row and one chained audit_logs row, and approval_status is 'approved'. (d) With the audit insert forced to throw, the request returns 500 and approval_status is still the old value. Write the same four cases for NC disposition. Run each red on HEAD, then green.
6. Run npm run ci:sign-ceremony and npm run ci:discarded-audit-write. The new routes must pass, and the baselines must shrink, not grow.
findings.acceptance: A viewer and an editor both get 422/403 when they try to change supplier approval_status or NC disposition through the unsigned routes, and the row is unchanged (failing first: 200 at HEAD). The signed routes return 200 only with a verified signature, write a signature row and a chained audit_logs row in the same transaction, and roll back completely when the audit write fails. Re-dispositioning a dispositioned NC returns 409. ci:sign-ceremony passes with no new baseline entries.
findings.dependencies: None. Reuses verifyApprovalSigner (server/routes/mdx-qms.ts:556) and the change-approval-signature.ts ceremony.

findings.title: Legacy /api/projects: DELETE now needs an editor and refuses to delete records, but POST and PATCH have no role gate and the delete and update audit rows are unattributed (userId null), unchained and written after commit
findings.evidenceAtHead: server/routes/projects-management.ts at HEAD: DELETE at 341 is `router.delete('/:projectId', requireEditorAccess, ...)`. Lines 369-379 run db.transaction with projectDeletionHolds and projectDeletionRefusal (server/services/c2c/project-retention.ts:55-131). These lock the rows and refuse with 409 for the anchor of a live program or any artifact past draft, signed, snapshotted or carrying review comments. Still open: POST '/' (153) and PATCH '/:projectId' (433) carry no role middleware. The router has no router.use gate (line 38), and the mount at server/bootstrap/register-project-routes.ts:32-33 adds none. The DELETE audit (383-414) is a plain db.insert(auditEvents) after the transaction commits, with `userId: null` at 391, inside a try/catch that only logs (411). The PATCH audit has `userId: null` at 479 and a swallowed catch at 499. The PATCH UPDATE (~460) filters by id only; the org check is the read before it. At 92ccdba1 none of POST/DELETE/PATCH (150/336/408) had a role gate. Reachability: client/src only GETs /api/projects (TaskBoard.tsx:326,1485,1673; CollabLauncher.tsx:173). The shipped Projects app writes through /api/c2c/projects (register-inline-routes.ts:851), whose mutations are authorized by canMutateProgram (server/services/c2c/program-access.ts).
findings.fixedBy: 2b33033e4 and 9109aa770 (PF-08/PF-13: requireEditorAccess on DELETE, projectDeletionHolds in the deleting transaction, server/routes/projects-management.ts:341,369-379; server/services/c2c/project-retention.ts); 0ecc058c5 (database refusal answered 409, projects-management.ts:419-425).
findings.remaining: (1) A viewer can POST a new project and PATCH any project in the org (name, description, status including 'archived', priority) by direct API call. This includes a regulatory program's anchor row. (2) DELETE and PATCH audit rows are not attributable: userId is null, and only userName is filled from getRequestActor. They are plain audit_events rows rather than chained, written after commit, and a failed write is swallowed. POST's audit (312) is likewise swallowed. (3) Deleting a drafts-only project still hard-cascades non-governed children (tasks, review threads, report_os_*) with no legal-hold check.
findings.severityRationale: The destructive half of the P1 is closed: a viewer can no longer delete, and no delete can cascade away records. What remains is role over-permission on non-destructive metadata writes to a legacy table the shipped UI only reads, plus Part 11 attributability gaps in its audit rows. That is real before GA, but it does not stop an invited-org pilot.
findings.humanTestingNote: Testers cannot see this through the UI: the Projects app creates, edits and deletes through /api/c2c/projects, and the client only reads /api/projects. It can only be reproduced by API: as a viewer, PATCH /api/projects/:id {"status":"archived"} returns 200.
findings.instructions:
1. server/routes/projects-management.ts: import requireEditorAccessForWrites and governedActorId from '../middleware/orgMembership' (line 11 already imports requireEditorAccess). Add `router.use(requireEditorAccessForWrites);` directly after `const router = Router();` (line 38), so POST, PATCH, DELETE and any future write need a writing role while GET stays open to viewers.
2. DELETE (341-431): before opening the transaction, read `const actorId = governedActorId(req)` and return 401 when it is null. Inside the db.transaction at 369, after `tx.delete(...)` succeeds, call `await writeChainedAuditRow(queryableFromDrizzle(tx), { tenantId: organizationId, userId: actorId, action: 'project_delete', resourceType: 'project', resourceId: String(projectId), details: { oldValues: existingProject, reason: 'Project deleted' } })` (server/services/auditService.ts:269). Delete the post-commit auditEvents insert and its swallowed catch (383-414). An audit failure then throws, the transaction rolls back, and the handler answers 500 with nothing deleted.
3. PATCH (433-520): wrap the UPDATE and a writeChainedAuditRow (action 'project_update', userId governedActorId(req), details {changedFields, oldValues, newValues}) in one db.transaction. Add `and(eq(projects.id, projectId), eq(projects.organizationId, organizationId))` to the UPDATE where-clause, and remove the swallowed-catch insert at ~466-501.
4. POST (153-330): replace the swallowed catch at 312 with the same chained write. Run it in the same transaction if atomicCreateProject (server/services/atomicQuotaService.js) can take a client; otherwise fail the response with 500 and an explicit `auditTrail: {persisted:false}`. Never return 201 silently.
5. Tests, seen to fail first: add server/routes/__tests__/projects-management-governed-writes.test.ts modelled on server/routes/__tests__/device-projects-delete-ownership.test.ts. (a) A viewer gets 403 on POST, PATCH and DELETE and nothing changes; POST and PATCH return 2xx at HEAD. (b) An editor DELETE of a drafts-only project writes one audit_logs row whose actor_id equals the session user and whose chain fields are set. (c) With writeChainedAuditRow forced to throw, DELETE returns 500 and the project row still exists. Run red on HEAD, then green.
6. Extend scripts/ci/check-regulated-delete-audit.mjs to refuse an audit insert in a delete handler whose user field is the literal null. Show its selftest failing on projects-management.ts:391 before the fix.
findings.acceptance: A viewer gets 403 on POST, PATCH and DELETE /api/projects (failing first: 2xx for POST and PATCH at HEAD). Every successful project update or delete has exactly one chained audit_logs row carrying the session user id, written in the same transaction. A forced audit failure leaves the project unchanged and returns 500. ci:regulated-delete-audit fails on a null-user delete audit (selftest shown red), and passes after the fix.
findings.dependencies: None.

findings.title: MCP connector: bearer and grant checks now go through verifyLiveToken and registration fails closed in production, but tenant lifecycle (read-only and deny states other than 'suspended'), refresh-token reuse detection and consent re-authentication are still open. The connector is now enabled in Terraform.
findings.evidenceAtHead: FIXED: server/mcp/auth/platform-token.ts:122-145 decodeAccessClaims now calls verifyLiveToken (134). That is server/services/token-revocation.ts:289-313: revocation list, account standing, password change or sign-out-everywhere (sessionEndedByStanding), and idle/lifetime/superseded via sessionInactivityReason. At 92ccdba1 it called verifyJwtWithRotation only (git show 92ccdba1:server/mcp/auth/platform-token.ts lines 67-76). provider.ts:175-205 liveGrantorMembership applies the same standing to both /token exchanges, so a password change or suspension ends refresh tokens and unredeemed codes. Consent verifies for the 'grant' purpose and refuses connector tokens (platform-token.ts:126-131; consent.ts:152). DCR: config.ts:148 sets closedInProduction when no allowlist is set, and index.ts:114-119 refuses registration in that case. terraform/stack/main.tf:275-277 now sets MCP_ENABLED=true and MCP_CLIENT_REDIRECT_ALLOWLIST=https://claude.ai,https://claude.com (absent at 92ccdba1). Per-org enablement is off by default (connector-enablement.ts:86-90). Governed tools require an editor role (runtime.ts:226). OPEN: (a) /mcp has no tenant-lifecycle check. Its chain (index.ts:247-253) is cors, rateLimit, json, requireBearerAuth, mcpEndpoint, and a grep for getTenantAccessPosture or enforceTenantLifecycle under server/mcp is empty. findMembership (store.ts:143-171) refuses only organizations.status='suspended'. So pending_deletion, inactive, purged/deleted, an unrecognised status and payment past_due/unpaid/canceled (tenant-lifecycle.ts:101-119), all of which /api refuses or makes read-only, are admitted, and c2c_file_draft_for_review (server/mcp/tools/governed.ts) still writes. (b) provider.ts:132: a revoked (already-rotated) refresh token gets InvalidGrantError only, with no revocation of its rotated_from family. provider.ts:144 ignores whether revokeRefreshToken changed a row (store.ts:357-366 returns void), so two concurrent refreshes with one token both mint new token pairs. (c) consent.ts:103-104 still reads localStorage 'trialsage_access_token' and goes straight to Allow with no fresh authentication or MFA. (d) The governed write is audited after the write: upsertLeaf audits with recordAuditRow after its INSERT, and runtime.ts:249 writeAudit runs after spec.run, flagging rather than rolling back a missing row.
findings.fixedBy: 3bdb50458, f8d404745 (verifyLiveToken in server/mcp/auth/platform-token.ts:134; standing in provider.ts:175-205); db9f1f3c9 (grant purpose refuses connector tokens, platform-token.ts:126-131); 9a086c0c7 and 2c2ea3401 (registration closed in production, config.ts:148 / index.ts:114; a password change ends grants); 0adb1b3ec (per-org enablement, connector-enablement.ts); 42842480f (Terraform mounts the connector with the allowlist, terraform/stack/main.tf:275-277).
findings.remaining: (1) A tenant that /api treats as read-only (pending_deletion, past_due, unpaid, canceled) or denied (inactive, purged/deleted, unrecognised status) can still use /mcp and the /token exchanges. A read-only tenant can still file a governed draft leaf. (2) There is no refresh-token reuse detection or family revocation, and concurrent rotation of one refresh token forks the family. A stolen refresh token stays usable for up to 30 days. (3) The consent page grants draft and file scopes on an existing browser session with no re-authentication or fresh MFA. (4) The connector's governed write and its audit row are not one transaction.
findings.severityRationale: The P1 impact is closed: logged-out, password-reset or suspended tokens no longer work on /mcp, and open DCR is refused in production. The connector is now on in production, but each org stays off until its owner or admin enables it, and redirects are limited to Claude's origins. The remaining gaps need a tenant in a non-active lifecycle state, which a paying pilot is not, or a stolen refresh token or hijacked browser session. Fix before enterprise GA.
findings.humanTestingNote: Ordinary connector testing (enable it for the org, connect Claude, read, file a draft leaf) behaves correctly. A tester would only see a defect after setting the test org to pending_deletion or past_due: the app's /api then refuses writes, but c2c_file_draft_for_review over the connector still files a draft leaf. No workaround is needed for the pilot path.
findings.instructions:
1. server/mcp/auth/platform-token.ts verifyPlatformBearer (213-245): after `if (!enabled) ...` at 224, call `getTenantAccessPosture(organizationId)` (server/services/tenant/tenant-lifecycle.ts:354). On null, throw ServerError('Organization status could not be verified. Try again.'), which fails closed. On posture.decision === 'deny', throw InvalidTokenError(posture.reason). Add `tenantDecision: 'allow' | 'read_only'` and `tenantReason: string | null` to McpPrincipal (line ~75) and set them.
2. server/mcp/tools/runtime.ts registerTool: next to the governed role check at 226, refuse any tool whose spec.annotations.readOnlyHint === false (this covers every spec.governed tool) when principal.tenantDecision !== 'allow'. Return refused(principal.tenantReason) and writeAudit(... outcome 'denied'), exactly as the scope refusal does.
3. server/mcp/auth/provider.ts liveGrantorMembership (175-205): after findGrantMembership, read the same posture. Throw InvalidGrantError(reason) on 'deny' and ServerError on null. The consent POST (consent.ts:152) is covered by step 1 because it goes through verifyPlatformBearer.
4. Refresh reuse detection: (a) server/mcp/auth/store.ts revokeRefreshToken (357-366) returns `(result.rowCount ?? 0) === 1`. (b) Add store.revokeRefreshFamily(token), which inside inGrantTenant runs a WITH RECURSIVE over mcp_oauth_refresh_tokens.rotated_from to collect ancestors and descendants of sha256Hex(token) and sets revoked_at = now() on all of them. The rotated_from column already exists (migrations/20260920_mcp_oauth.sql; store.ts:300). (c) In provider.exchangeRefreshToken: when stored.revoked (132), call revokeRefreshFamily, log a security event (logger.warn with clientId, userId, organizationId) and throw InvalidGrantError. When `await store.revokeRefreshToken(refreshToken)` at 144 returns false, call revokeRefreshFamily and throw InvalidGrantError before issueTokens.
5. Consent re-authentication: in server/mcp/auth/consent.ts, delete the localStorage shortcut at 103-104 so the login form, with its MFA step, always renders. Alternatively, in consentHandler (132+) refuse a platform token whose session start (sessionStartSecondsOf, server/services/session-inactivity.ts:159) is more than 300 s old, re-rendering the login form with 'Sign in again to authorise this connection.'
6. Atomic governed write: give submission-service.upsertLeaf (server/services/submission-service/submission-service.ts:2878) an optional pg client parameter. In the MCP tool (server/mcp/tools/governed.ts), open pool.connect, BEGIN, call upsertLeaf with the client, call writeChainedAuditRow (server/services/auditService.ts:269) with the same client, then COMMIT. Return refused(...) and ROLLBACK when the chained row fails, instead of the 'audit NOT persisted' flag.
7. Tests, red first: extend server/mcp/__tests__/mcp-account-standing.dbtest.ts with these cases. (a) organizations.status='pending_deletion': read tools succeed and c2c_file_draft_for_review is refused with the posture reason; it succeeds at HEAD. (b) status 'inactive': /mcp answers 401. (c) payment_status 'past_due': the governed write is refused. (d) Rotate a refresh token, then present the old one: invalid_grant, and the newly issued refresh token is now refused too. (e) Two concurrent exchanges of one refresh token: exactly one succeeds. Add a consent test that the rendered page no longer reads localStorage, or that a stale-sst token is refused.
findings.acceptance: On /mcp, a token of an org in pending_deletion, past_due, unpaid or canceled can run read tools but is refused on every write tool. An org in inactive, purged, deleted or unrecognised status gets 401/invalid_grant on /mcp and /token. These tests fail at HEAD and pass after. Presenting a rotated refresh token revokes its whole family. Concurrent rotation yields one success. The consent page requires a fresh sign-in with MFA. A forced audit failure on c2c_file_draft_for_review leaves no leaf.
findings.dependencies: None. Uses the existing getTenantAccessPosture and the existing rotated_from column.

findings.title: No Redis by decision: sign-in sessions (idle, concurrent-session limit, superseded) are now coordinated through Postgres across tasks, but HTTP rate limits are still counted per task in memory
findings.evidenceAtHead: terraform/: grep -ri 'redis|elasticache|valkey' is still empty, and terraform/environments/production/terraform.tfvars.example:46 sets api_desired_count = 2 (staging example :48 = 1). FIXED PART: commit 77e11b07d (product decision B6: Postgres is the coordination store) moved the session state into migrations/20261001e_session_activity.sql. That table is in public with organization_id INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, IF NOT EXISTS, and listed in scripts/db/migration-set.mjs:3033. server/services/session-inactivity.ts:261-301 reads and writes last activity per session in session_activity, with the in-process write throttled to min(30 s, idle/4). The concurrent-session registry runs in one transaction under an advisory lock at 336-375, and superseded markers are rows too. sessionInactivityReason (480-503) therefore sees activity recorded by any task before it falls back to iat. The revocation list has a DB tier (token-revocation.ts:203-216), and the five-failure account lockout is DB-backed (auth-security-service.ts:29,145-195). OPEN PART: server/middleware/redisRateLimiter.ts:97-110 falls back to an in-process memoryStore (167, checkMemoryRateLimit) when REDIS_URL is unset, which it is in production. Every bucket (auth, api, ai, documents, upload, ...) is therefore counted per task: the effective ceiling is limit times api_desired_count, and it resets on every deploy. server/middleware/sign-in-limits.ts uses express-rate-limit's default memory store, with the same effect. session-inactivity.ts:220-233 store() silently falls back to process memory, logging only a warning, when session_activity cannot be read. No readiness probe checks that table: grep finds session_activity only in session-inactivity, tenant-offboarding and tenant-full-export.
findings.fixedBy: 77e11b07d (D1/D6 U20: sessions live in Postgres; migrations/20261001e_session_activity.sql; server/services/session-inactivity.ts:197-415; tests/db/session-activity-across-tasks.dbtest.ts).
findings.remaining: (1) HTTP rate limits, including the fail-closed auth and documents buckets and the per-account sign-in limits, are enforced per task: twice the configured ceiling with two API tasks, reset on each deploy. Brute force on one account is still bounded by the DB lockout. (2) If session_activity is unreachable or missing, sessions silently revert to per-task memory, which brings back random idle sign-outs and a concurrent-session limit that does not hold, and no readiness signal reports it.
findings.severityRationale: The impact that made this P1, active users signed out at random and a concurrent-session limit that did not hold in the two-task topology, is fixed through Postgres. What remains is that rate-limit ceilings double with two tasks. The DB account lockout still bounds credential guessing, so for a single small pilot tenant this is polish and hardening, not a blocker.
findings.humanTestingNote: Testers cannot observe this: local and staging run one API task (staging tfvars api_desired_count = 1), so the rate limits behave exactly as configured.
findings.instructions:
1. Keep decision B6 (no Redis). Add a shared counter for the fail-closed categories: new migration migrations/2026101x_rate_limit_counters.sql with `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.rate_limit_counters (organization_id INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, bucket_key TEXT NOT NULL, window_start TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL, hits INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, PRIMARY KEY (organization_id, bucket_key, window_start))` plus an index on window_start, with the same header contract as 20261001e_session_activity.sql (no DROP; organization 0; system scope only). Append it to C2C_MIGRATION_FILES in scripts/db/migration-set.mjs before the final tenant-isolation sweep pair, and run npm run ci:migration-set-order and npm run ci:migration-drop-safety.
2. server/middleware/redisRateLimiter.ts: add checkPostgresRateLimit(key, max, windowMs) under runWithSystemTenantScope (as session-inactivity.ts store() does). It does `INSERT ... VALUES (0, $key, date_bin(window, now(), epoch), 1) ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET hits = rate_limit_counters.hits + 1 RETURNING hits`, and prunes rows older than two windows opportunistically. Use it instead of checkMemoryRateLimit when redis is unavailable and the category is in RATE_LIMIT_FAIL_CLOSED_CATEGORIES (auth, documents). Other categories may keep memory, but then divide their ceiling by Number(process.env.API_REPLICA_COUNT || 1), and set API_REPLICA_COUNT from var.api_desired_count in terraform/stack/main.tf's task environment.
3. server/middleware/sign-in-limits.ts: give the express-rate-limit instances a store backed by the same table, or the replica divisor.
4. server/lib/health-check.ts /ready (line 327): in production, add a check that `SELECT 1 FROM session_activity LIMIT 1` succeeds under the system scope, and answer 503 when it fails, so a missing or unreachable table cannot silently degrade sessions to per-task memory. Show the check failing first by pointing it at a database without the table.
5. Test, red first: following tests/db/session-activity-across-tasks.dbtest.ts (fresh module graphs as tasks), exhaust the auth bucket on task A; the next request on task B must be 429. At HEAD it is admitted.
findings.acceptance: With two module graphs on one real Postgres, a client that exhausts the auth or documents bucket on one task is refused (429) on the other (failing first at HEAD). /health/ready returns 503 in production when session_activity cannot be read (shown failing on a database without the table). ci:migration-set-order and ci:migration-drop-safety pass with the new migration.
findings.dependencies: Founder decision B6 (Postgres, not Redis, as the coordination store). If Redis is chosen instead, this needs ElastiCache in Terraform and REDIS_URL in the task definition.

findings.title: verify-chain: the estate-wide walk is now platform-admin only; any member can still trigger an unbounded walk of their own organisation's chain
findings.evidenceAtHead: server/routes/c2c/actions.ts:799-848: the handler checks resolvePlatformAdmin(req) at :807. A caller who is not a platform admin gets verifyTenantChainOnAdminScope(orgId) (:808) with scope 'organization', the break redacted by breakForTenant (:821) and no estate `tenants` count. Only a platform admin reaches the estate walk on the app_super_admin connection (:825-832). resolvePlatformAdmin (server/middleware/requirePlatformAdmin.ts:111) decides from PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS or an active platform_role_grants row, never from the membership role. server/services/audit/tenant-chain-verdict.ts:77-97 passes { tenantId: orgId } to verifyAuditChain, so chain.ts readChainRows (:634-702) adds `AND tenant_id = $1`. /api/decision-lineage/verify-chain has the same split (server/routes/decision-lineage.ts:188-222, DP-77). I ran `npx vitest run server/services/audit/__tests__/chain-head-on-demand.test.ts -t IAM-26`: 4 passed. They cover: the org-8 admin gets org 8 only; another org's break reads 'another organization'; a membership super_admin with no grant gets organisation scope; the platform admin gets the estate. What remains: readChainRows has no LIMIT or pagination. For a tenant with legacy (unsequenced) rows it also loads every other tenant's legacy rows as context (chain.ts:687-700). The route is mounted with authMiddleware only (server/bootstrap/register-inline-routes.ts:347) and has no limiter of its own beyond the generic /api limiter (server/startup/middleware.ts:59-60).
findings.fixedBy: f97d49331 (2026-10-01, IAM-26) server/routes/c2c/actions.ts:799-848; f0209791a (DP-77) server/routes/decision-lineage.ts:188-222; shared verifier server/services/audit/tenant-chain-verdict.ts:77-97
findings.remaining: 1. Any signed-in member, a viewer included, can still trigger an on-demand walk of their organisation's whole audit_logs chain on demand. The walk is unpaginated and runs on a super-admin-scoped connection, so request volume is limited only by the generic /api limiter. 2. If the organisation has legacy (unsequenced) rows, the walk also reads every other tenant's legacy rows (id, tenant_id, occurred_at, sha256_chain) into API memory. Nothing from those rows is returned, but the work is cross-tenant. A fresh pilot database writes no legacy rows (chain.ts:219-243 refuses a tenantless write outside vitest), so this applies only to a database migrated from before chain_seq. The estate-wide DoS and the metadata leak in the finding are closed.
findings.severityRationale: The P1 core is closed in code and covered by a passing test: a viewer can no longer scan every tenant or read platform totals and other tenants' break hashes. What is left is resource use bounded by one tenant's own audit volume. A small pilot tenant will not notice it, and the ledger and document-history reads already run the same walk.
findings.humanTestingNote: A tester sees nothing different. A non-admin calling GET /api/c2c/actions/verify-chain or opening the Decision Lineage surface (/api/decision-lineage/verify-chain) gets scope 'organization' and their own org's verdict only.
findings.instructions:
1. On concept2cure-v2 (Rule 0), in server/routes/c2c/actions.ts, put a per-organisation limiter in front of router.get('/verify-chain', ...) at :799. Build it with createRedisRateLimiter (server/middleware/redisRateLimiter.ts:521) with perOrganization: true and one rule, for example 6 requests per 10 minutes per org. Platform admins get their own small allowance. Wire the same limiter on server/routes/decision-lineage.ts:227.
2. In server/services/audit/chain.ts, add `maxRows?: number` to VerifyAuditChainOptions (:629-632). In readChainRows (:634), first run a `SELECT count(*)` with the same WHERE clause. If the count exceeds maxRows, throw a new AuditChainTooLargeError instead of loading the rows. Fail closed: the error is never a partial verdict.
3. In server/services/audit/tenant-chain-verdict.ts verifyTenantChainOnAdminScope (:77), take an optional maxRows and pass it through. In actions.ts :808 and decision-lineage.ts chainVerdictFor (:203), pass a configured ceiling, for example AUDIT_CHAIN_ON_DEMAND_MAX_ROWS (default 250000). Map AuditChainTooLargeError to 503 { error: 'AUDIT_CHAIN_TOO_LARGE_FOR_ON_DEMAND', detail: 'The daily integrity sweep is the authoritative verdict for a chain this size.' }. Never return ok:true.
4. Keep the legacy-context read (chain.ts:687-700) only for platform admins. For a non-admin caller whose tenant has legacy rows, return the latest daily-sweep verdict for that org (server/jobs/auditChainIntegritySweep.ts records it) or a 503 'verify on the operator path'. Do not walk other tenants' legacy rows on the caller's request.
5. Tests first, in server/services/audit/__tests__/chain-head-on-demand.test.ts next to the IAM-26 describe block (:342). (a) The seventh request from one org within the window gets 429. (b) A tenant whose row count exceeds maxRows gets 503 and the walk's SELECT of rows is never issued (assert on the mocked client's query log). (c) A non-admin in a tenant with legacy rows causes no query with `tenant_id IS DISTINCT FROM`. Run them against HEAD first and record the red, then implement.
findings.acceptance: Each new test fails at HEAD before the change and passes after. The existing 4 IAM-26 tests still pass. A viewer's 7th request in the window returns 429. An over-ceiling tenant returns 503 AUDIT_CHAIN_TOO_LARGE_FOR_ON_DEMAND, never ok:true. A non-admin request issues no cross-tenant SELECT on audit_logs (asserted on the query log).
findings.dependencies: None. The limiter is per task without Redis (SEC-08), so it holds across tasks only once ElastiCache exists.

findings.fixedBy: 8fdfc74bd (2026-10-05): the demo JWT block in .gitleaksignore:44-58 is dispositioned 'not a secret'. The code basis is server/middleware/tokenType.ts:98-104. The commit also added a rotation runbook, which is a claim, not evidence.

One caution: if a staging or test environment points at the ep-wild-forest or ep-icy-brook Neon endpoints, anyone with the repo history can read the tester data there. Run human testing against the AWS staging stack or a freshly credentialed database.

Founder, Neon console, project ep-frosty-salad-afl93crk (named in .devcontainer/devcontainer.json:16): reset the neondb_owner password on the branches behind ep-wild-forest-ahbojhu4 and ep-icy-brook-aha5br78. findings.title: Terraform production still has no WAF, GuardDuty, AWS Config, VPC flow logs, ALB access logs or CloudWatch alarms/SNS (RDS is now on a customer-managed KMS key)
findings.evidenceAtHead: A case-insensitive grep across terraform/**/*.tf (tests excluded) for aws_wafv2|web_acl|guardduty|aws_config_|configuration_recorder|flow_log|cloudwatch_metric_alarm|aws_sns_topic|elasticache|waf|alarm|sns|redis finds no resource. The only hit is the comment at terraform/modules/cloudfront/main.tf:149-156: 'No WAF yet: a founder decision, not defaulted', with #trivy:ignore:AWS-0011 on the distribution. ALB access logs are still off: terraform/modules/alb/variables.tf:40-43 defaults access_logs_bucket = "", alb/main.tf:41-44 enables logging only when that is set, and module "alb" in terraform/stack/main.tf:363-374 does not pass it. terraform/modules/vpc-secure/main.tf:4 aws_vpc.this has no aws_flow_log. CloudTrail with CloudWatch Logs and CMK is present (terraform/modules/compliance-evidence/main.tf:262-351). The audit-chain sweep's incident alert (server/jobs/auditChainIntegritySweep.ts:484-497 calling reportSecurityAlert) reaches an operator only through SECURITY_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL (server/services/security-alerts.ts:15). Neither terraform/ nor .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml provisions that variable, so in production it is a console line no alarm watches. Fixed since the audit: the RDS instance, its snapshots and Performance Insights now use aws_kms_key.database and the task secrets use aws_kms_key.secrets (terraform/stack/database_keys.tf:36-57; main.tf:119, :357).
findings.remaining: 1. No WAFv2 web ACL on CloudFront, so no managed rules and no edge rate rule. 2. No GuardDuty detector. 3. No AWS Config recorder or rules. 4. No VPC flow logs. 5. No ALB access logs. 6. No CloudWatch alarms or SNS topic, so 5xx bursts, unhealthy targets, RDS pressure, auth-failure spikes, CloudTrail CIS events and the daily audit-chain sweep incident alert nobody. 7. SECURITY_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL is not provisioned. Redis/ElastiCache is still absent too, tracked under SEC-08. Of the original evidence, only the RDS-default-KMS sub-point is closed (5ef2787a5).
findings.severityRationale: For one small FDA-only pilot the missing WAF is a founder cost decision that can wait if it is recorded. But with no alarms and no forwarding for the audit-integrity alert, a Part 11 audit-chain break or an outage in production would go unseen until a user reports it. GuardDuty, flow logs and ALB logs are the minimum an incident responder and a GxP vendor-qualification questionnaire expect. All of this must exist before pilot users rely on production. None of it blocks starting the pilot on a non-production stack.
findings.humanTestingNote: Testers cannot see this on a local or staging deployment. If staging comes from this Terraform, operators have no alarm on 5xx or the audit sweep, so a failed request a tester hits is visible only in CloudWatch Logs. Pull logs manually when a tester reports an error.
findings.instructions:
1. Founder: record the WAF decision (cost about $5/month plus $1 per rule per month plus per-request fees). Recommended: on, with AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet's SizeRestrictions_BODY overridden to COUNT, so Vault uploads and AnA turns over 8 KB are not blocked.
2. On concept2cure-v2 (Rule 0), add terraform/stack/detective_controls.tf with: (a) aws_guardduty_detector "this" { enable = true }, plus aws_guardduty_detector_feature for S3_DATA_EVENTS, RDS_LOGIN_EVENTS and RUNTIME_MONITORING (ECS Fargate agent management). (b) An AWS Config IAM role (managed policy AWS_ConfigRole), aws_config_configuration_recorder (all supported resources), aws_config_delivery_channel to module.evidence's bucket under prefix 'config/', aws_config_configuration_recorder_status enabled, and managed rules: s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited, s3-bucket-ssl-requests-only, rds-storage-encrypted, rds-instance-public-access-check, cloudtrail-enabled, restricted-ssh, vpc-flow-logs-enabled. (c) aws_sns_topic "ops_alarms" with kms_master_key_id = aws_kms_key.secrets.arn and an email subscription from a new variable alarm_email (required when environment == "production"; validate in variables.tf). findings.title: Organisations created by scripts/seed-admin.mjs cannot create programs (NO_CLIENT_WORKSPACE) until deploy-migrate runs again
findings.evidenceAtHead: Observed at aa4ee1e29 (2026-10-18) on a database provisioned from empty: after scripts/seed-admin.mjs (docs/LOCAL_TESTING.md §2) and sign-in, POST /api/c2c/projects returned PROJECT_RECORD_UNAVAILABLE / NO_CLIENT_WORKSPACE; scripts/seed-local-testing.ts did not change that; re-running node scripts/db/deploy-migrate.mjs applied migrations/20260923_organization_default_client_workspace.sql's repair sweep (client_workspaces 0 → 1) and the same request then created the program. See docs/evidence/reviews/2026-10-13-market-readiness/smoke-at-head.md. Fixed 2026-10-18 by 969d1e727: scripts/seed-admin.mjs and scripts/seed-founder.mjs (and the GA demo seeder, which carried its own unmarked INSERT) now execute that same repair migration through scripts/seed/organization-workspace.mjs. Proved on a fresh database at d0cde23b9 plus the fix: POST /api/c2c/projects 409 NO_CLIENT_WORKSPACE with trunk's seed-admin, 201 and anchored with the fixed one (docs/evidence/W1/2026-10-18-seeded-workspace/).
findings.severityRationale: Does not affect real tenants (signup, first-run setup and the boot seed create the workspace; deploys repair existing organisations), but it stops every human tester who follows the documented local setup at journey 1.
findings.humanTestingNote: Fixed by 969d1e727: on that commit or later, seed-admin gives the organisation its workspace and no extra step is needed. On an older checkout, run `node scripts/db/deploy-migrate.mjs` (owner database URL) once after seeding.
findings.instructions:
1. Red first: add a test that runs scripts/seed-admin.mjs against an empty provisioned database and then calls POST /api/c2c/projects; it fails today with NO_CLIENT_WORKSPACE.
2. In scripts/seed-admin.mjs, after the organisation and membership are written, create its default client workspace through the canonical writer (server/services/c2c/organization-default-workspace.ts) — or, if the script cannot import TypeScript, execute migrations/20260923_organization_default_client_workspace.sql (the idempotent repair sweep) as its last step. Do not write a second INSERT into client_workspaces (zero duplication).
3. Add one line to docs/LOCAL_TESTING.md §2 saying the account step now includes the workspace.
findings.acceptance: The new test fails on the current script and passes after the change; a tester following docs/LOCAL_TESTING.md §1–3 can create a program with no extra step.
findings.dependencies: none
